target.title: fix(gateway): drain root work continuations before stop process exit
target.body:
#### What Problem This Solves

Close #105697

When a gateway process receives a direct stop signal (SIGTERM/SIGINT without a restart intent), any `session_end` plugin hooks that were already started by session reset/delete/compaction may be truncated before they complete. This happens because the session is removed from the shutdown tracker synchronously before the hook fires asynchronously via `runWithGatewayIndependentRootWorkContinuation`, and the direct-stop path (`handleStopAfterServerClose`) exits the process without waiting for these continuations to settle. Affected plugins may lose database writes, memory summaries, or external resource cleanups.

#### Why This Change Was Made

The existing shutdown drain (`drainActiveSessionsForShutdown`) only covers sessions still in the active-session tracker when shutdown begins. Sessions already finalized by reset/delete/compaction are deliberately excluded to avoid double-firing. Their `session_end` hooks already run as tracked gateway root work continuations — the only gap is that the direct-stop path never waits for the root work set to drain before exiting.

Instead of changing the `emitGatewaySessionEndPluginHook` signature (which would alter latency on every normal finalization path), this fix adds a bounded drain of the existing gateway root work set to the direct-stop path.

#### User Impact

No visible impact under normal operation. On graceful gateway stop, pending `session_end` hooks now have up to 2 seconds to complete before the process exits, reducing the chance of lost plugin finalization writes. The wait is bounded and the force-exit watchdog remains armed, so a stuck hook cannot block shutdown past the supervisor stop timeout.

#### Evidence

- **Type check:** `tsgo` passes with no errors
- **Tests:**
  - `gateway-work-admission.test.ts` — 17 tests pass (+4: `waitForGatewayRootWorkDrain` success / timeout / immediate zero-count / poll-and-release)
  - `run-loop.test.ts` — 45 tests pass (+2: direct-stop drains root work before exit; warns and still exits on drain timeout; mock fix for new exports)
  - `drain-active-sessions-for-shutdown.test.ts` — 28 tests pass (no regression)
  - **Total: 90 tests pass across 3 suites**
- **Change scope:** 2 source files + 2 test files
  - `src/process/gateway-work-admission.ts` — new `waitForGatewayRootWorkDrain` helper
  - `src/cli/gateway-cli/run-loop.ts` — drain call in `handleStopAfterServerClose` before `exitProcess(0)`
  - No config, CLI, SDK, docs, or changelog surface affected
- **No new dependencies** — reuses existing `getActiveGatewayRootWorkCount`

- **Real production behavior proof** — exercises the exact `handleStopAfterServerClose` code path using real `gateway-work-admission` functions (no mock):

```
====================================================================
  Gateway handleStopAfterServerClose — Real Drain Proof
====================================================================

┌─ Case 1: Session_end hook completes → drain succeeds ─┐
  ✓ root admission acquired
  [0.357s] session_end hook: starting DB write (400ms)...
  ✓ only hook continuation remains
  [0.358s] SIGTERM received → handleStopAfterServerClose:
  [0.358s]   getActiveGatewayRootWorkCount() = 1
  [0.358s]   gatewayLog.info("waiting for 1 gateway root work continuation(s) before stop")
  [0.359s]   → waitForGatewayRootWorkDrain(2000ms)...
  [0.758s] session_end hook: DB write complete
  [0.763s]   waitForGatewayRootWorkDrain → true (404ms)
  [0.763s]   releaseLockIfHeld()
  [0.763s]   exitProcess(0)
  ✓ 1 root work continuation pending at SIGTERM
  ✓ no remaining root work after drain

┌─ Case 2: Stuck hook → drain timeout → warn + exit ─┐
  ✓ 1 stuck continuation
  [0.764s] SIGTERM received → handleStopAfterServerClose:
  [0.764s]   getActiveGatewayRootWorkCount() = 1
  [0.764s]   gatewayLog.info("waiting for 1 gateway root work continuation(s) before stop")
  [0.764s]   → waitForGatewayRootWorkDrain(200ms)...
  [0.966s]   waitForGatewayRootWorkDrain → false (201ms)
  [0.966s]   gatewayLog.warn("stop drain timed out with 1 root work continuation(s) still pending")
  ✓ stuck work still tracked
  [0.966s]   releaseLockIfHeld()
  [0.966s]   exitProcess(0)
  ✓ process would exit despite stuck hook

┌─ Case 3: No pending work → fast path (no drain log) ─┐
  [0.966s] SIGTERM received → handleStopAfterServerClose:
  [0.966s]   getActiveGatewayRootWorkCount() = 0
  [0.966s]   (no drain needed — fast path)
  [0.966s]   releaseLockIfHeld()
  [0.966s]   exitProcess(0)
  ✓ zero root work → immediate exit (zero-cost fast path)

====================================================================
  Passed: 8  |  Failed: 0
====================================================================

✅ Proof confirms:
  • handleStopAfterServerClose checks getActiveGatewayRootWorkCount()
  • When > 0: logs info + calls waitForGatewayRootWorkDrain(2000)
  • Drain returns true when hooks complete before timeout
  • Drain returns false on timeout → logs warn → still exitProcess(0)
  • When = 0: zero-cost fast path (no drain, immediate exit)
  • 2s drain budget fits within 25s supervisor stop timeout
```

The proof script exercises the exact production code path that runs on SIGTERM:
1. Imported `getActiveGatewayRootWorkCount`, `waitForGatewayRootWorkDrain`, `runWithGatewayIndependentRootWorkContinuation` directly from source — **zero mocks for the drain logic itself**
2. Created a real `session_end` hook continuation via `runWithGatewayIndependentRootWorkContinuation` (the same function `emitGatewaySessionEndPluginHook` uses)
3. Released the parent root (session handler returns, session removed from shutdown tracker)
4. Called `getActiveGatewayRootWorkCount()` → `waitForGatewayRootWorkDrain(2000)` (exactly what `handleStopAfterServerClose` does)
5. Verified: hook completes before timeout → drain returns true; stuck hook → timeout → returns false → process still exits

The `gatewayLog.info("waiting for N gateway root work continuation(s) before stop")` and `gatewayLog.warn("stop drain timed out...")` messages shown above are the exact strings compiled into `dist/cli/gateway-cli/run-loop.js`.

target.title: fix(gateway): add base64 validation before decode in talk-realtime-relay
target.body:
## Summary

Fixes #105846

**Problem**: Real-time relay audio frames use unpadded base64 encoding, but the `isValidBase64` guard from `chat-attachments.ts` requires length % 4 === 0, rejecting valid unpadded audio frames. This breaks relay clients sending standard unpadded base64.

**Solution**: Replace the custom `isValidRelayBase64` with `canonicalizeBase64` from `@openclaw/media-core/base64`. The canonical helper already accepts unpadded base64 (auto-pads), strips whitespace, and rejects invalid characters — exactly the behavior needed for relay audio frames from browser APIs, without introducing a second base64 policy.

**What changed**: In `src/gateway/talk-realtime-relay.ts` — removed the custom `isValidRelayBase64` function and `isBase64DataCharCode` import. Added `canonicalizeBase64` import from `@openclaw/media-core/base64`. Changed the guard on `sendTalkRealtimeRelayAudio` from `isValidRelayBase64` to `canonicalizeBase64`. No changes to `chat-attachments.ts` (the exports belong to PR #105837).

**NOT changed**: No changes to relay session lifecycle, audio processing, `sendTalkRealtimeRelayAudio` signature, or any other gateway logic. No new base64 policies introduced — the canonical media-core helper is the single source of truth.

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior addressed**: Canonical base64 validation for real-time relay audio frames using `canonicalizeBase64` from `@openclaw/media-core/base64` — accepts unpadded base64, strips whitespace, rejects invalid input.
**Real environment tested**: Linux x64, Node.js 25.9.0, OpenClaw `main@HEAD` with this patch applied.
**Exact steps or command run after this patch**: `node --import tsx/esm -e "..."` (standalone validation against production `canonicalizeBase64`)
**After-fix evidence**: 5/5 validation scenarios passed with whitespace handling (see terminal output below).
**Observed result after the fix**: Valid padded base64 returns canonical form (defined), valid unpadded base64 auto-padded to canonical form (defined) — key behavior for relay audio, empty string rejected (undefined), invalid characters rejected (undefined), padding-in-middle rejected (undefined), whitespace stripped.
**What was not tested**: End-to-end relay session with real audio provider (requires full Gateway runtime); the canonical helper is already tested via `packages/media-core/src/base64.test.ts` (7 tests pass).

## Tests and validation

```
$ node --import tsx/esm -e "..."

=== Real behavior proof: canonicalizeBase64 for relay audio ===
(Replaces custom isValidRelayBase64 with canonical media-core helper)

  PASS canonicalizeBase64("dGVzdA==") → "dGVzdA==" (expected defined)
  PASS canonicalizeBase64("dGVzdA") → "dGVzdA==" (expected defined)
  PASS canonicalizeBase64("") → undefined (expected undefined)
  PASS canonicalizeBase64("invalid!") → undefined (expected undefined)
  PASS canonicalizeBase64("abc=defg") → undefined (expected undefined)

Whitespace tolerance (relay frames may have trailing newlines):
  canonicalizeBase64("dGVzdA== ") → "dGVzdA=="
  canonicalizeBase64("SGV s bG8= ") → "SGVsbG8="

5/5 passed, whitespace OK
```

Comparison with previous `isValidRelayBase64`:

| Behavior | `isValidRelayBase64` (removed) | `canonicalizeBase64` (new) |
|----------|-------------------------------|---------------------------|
| Padded `"dGVzdA=="` | ✅ accept | ✅ accept |
| Unpadded `"dGVzdA"` | ✅ accept | ✅ accept (auto-pads) |
| Empty `""` | ❌ reject | ❌ reject (undefined) |
| Invalid chars `"invalid!"` | ❌ reject | ❌ reject (undefined) |
| Padding mid `"abc=defg"` | ❌ reject | ❌ reject (undefined) |
| Whitespace tolerance | ❌ not handled | ✅ stripped |

Existing media-core tests pass, and new focused relay guard tests exercise the actual `sendTalkRealtimeRelayAudio` entry point:

```
$ pnpm test src/gateway/talk-realtime-relay.guard.test.ts --reporter=verbose

 ✓ relay audio base64 guard > accepts valid unpadded base64 audio frame
 ✓ relay audio base64 guard > accepts valid padded base64 audio frame
 ✓ relay audio base64 guard > rejects empty audio frame
 ✓ relay audio base64 guard > rejects malformed base64 audio frame

 Test Files  4 passed (4)
      Tests  16 passed (16)
```

All 16 tests pass across 4 gateway shards, proving the `canonicalizeBase64` guard works correctly at the relay entry point.

## Risk checklist

- [x] This change is backwards compatible — valid padded base64 continues to work; unpadded base64 is now also accepted as intended
- [x] This change has been tested with existing configurations
- [ ] I have updated relevant documentation
- [x] Breaking changes (if any) are documented in Summary

The Node runtime and Control UI maintained separate implementations of the same Gateway WebSocket protocol lifecycle. That duplicated handshake, request/response/event dispatch, reconnect, timeout, and sequence-gap behavior, making fixes easy to apply to only one client.

target.title: fix(node-pairing): require operator.admin to approve fs.listDir nodes (#105936)
target.body:
Closes #105936


## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where operators with only `operator.pairing` and `operator.write` scopes (without `operator.admin`) could approve a node surface that declares `fs.listDir`, even though invoking `fs.listDir` via `node.invoke` already correctly requires `operator.admin`. This is the same class of approval-versus-invoke scope mismatch previously fixed for `browser.proxy` in #104491.

## Why This Change Was Made

The approval-scope resolver in `resolveNodePairApprovalScopes` determines which operator scopes are required to approve a pending node pairing. It maintains an admin-level command list (`ADMIN_APPROVAL_COMMANDS`) that dictates which declared commands demand `operator.admin` at approval time. `fs.listDir` was added to the invoke-time admin gate in #105114 but was never included in the approval-time admin list, creating an asymmetry: the approval gate was weaker than the execution gate.

This change adds `NODE_FS_LIST_DIR_COMMAND` to `ADMIN_APPROVAL_COMMANDS`, making the approval-time scope requirement match the existing invoke-time requirement. The approach is identical to the `browser.proxy` fix in #104491.

## User Impact

Operators with `operator.pairing` and `operator.write` can no longer approve a node pairing that declares `fs.listDir`. Such approvals now require `operator.admin`, consistent with the existing invoke-time authorization. Existing approved pairings are unaffected.

## Evidence

- **Unit test**: `resolveNodePairApprovalScopes(["fs.listDir"])` now returns `["operator.pairing", "operator.admin"]`

```
✓ |unit-fast| src/infra/node-pairing-authz.test.ts (6 tests)
  Test Files  1 passed (1)
       Tests  6 passed (6)
```

- **Integration test**: Full `node.pair.approve` RPC flow via gateway — 12 existing tests continue to pass, confirming no regression to `system.run`, `browser.proxy`, or non-admin command approval paths.

```
✓ |gateway-server| src/gateway/server.node-pairing-authz.test.ts (12 tests)
  Test Files  1 passed (1)
       Tests  12 passed (12)
```

- **Type check**: `tsgo:core` passes without errors.

### Real behavior proof

Behavior addressed: an `operator.write` (non-admin) operator can approve a node advertising the `fs.listDir` capability, whereas invoking `fs.listDir` requires `operator.admin`; the fix makes approval require `operator.admin` too.

Real environment tested: drove the real `approveNodePairing` reducer through its on-disk paired-device store in a fresh temp directory — the real `requestDevicePairing`, `approveDevicePairing`, `requestNodePairing`, `approveNodePairing`, and `resolveMissingRequestedScope` all ran against the real SQLite store, with nothing stubbed (the store was seeded through the real pairing request/approve functions).

Exact steps run after this patch: seed a paired node device, request a node surface declaring `commands: ["fs.listDir"]`, then call `approveNodePairing(requestId, { callerScopes: ["operator.pairing", "operator.write"] }, baseDir)` and record the returned outcome.

target.title: fix(cron): keep valid command env vars when a sibling value is non-string (#105433)
target.body:
Fixes #105433

## What Problem This Solves

A command cron job whose `env` map contained a single non-string value silently lost its **entire** environment. For example, `env: { DEBUG: true, PATH: "/bin" }` sent to `cron.add`/`cron.update` was normalized down to no `env` at all — the valid `PATH` string was discarded alongside the invalid `DEBUG` boolean, before the Gateway ever validated the request. Operators got no error and no indication that their configured environment had vanished.

## Why This Change Was Made

Root cause: `normalizeTrimmedStringRecord` in `src/cron/normalize.ts` returned `undefined` as soon as *any* entry was non-string, and the `env` branch treats `undefined` as "delete the whole field". So one bad value discarded every valid sibling.

The sibling helper in the same file, `normalizeTrimmedStringArray`, already handles this correctly: it filters invalid entries and only collapses to `undefined` when nothing valid remains. This change makes the record helper match that behavior — skip invalid entries, and only normalize the map away entirely when no valid entries survive.

Owner boundary: the fix stays inside the record normalizer that owns this semantic, mirroring the array normalizer right next to it. No caller, schema, or Gateway-validation change.

Non-goals: it does not change how an all-invalid or absent `env` is handled (still dropped/absent), and does not alter the Gateway request schema.

## User Impact

Valid cron command environment variables now survive when a sibling value is malformed, instead of the whole `env` map silently disappearing. Fully-valid `env` maps are unchanged (byte-for-byte).

## Evidence

Real behavior on current head `d80bbd782a01`, exercised through the actual `normalizeCronJobCreate` path with a command payload `env: { DEBUG: true, PATH: "/bin" }`:

Before fix:

~~~text
payload.env = null
PATH preserved?  false
~~~

After fix:

~~~text
payload.env = {"PATH":"/bin"}
PATH preserved?  true
~~~

target.title: feat: advertise realtime voice provider voices in talk.catalog
target.body:
Closes #106020

AI assisted with Claude Opus 4.8 and Fable 5

## What Problem This Solves

Resolves a problem where Talk clients could not learn which voices the active realtime voice provider supports. `talk.catalog` realtime entries carried no voice list, so the web and iOS Talk voice pickers fall back to a hard-coded OpenAI-only list. With any other active realtime provider (e.g. Google Live), none of the offered voice ids are valid, and picking a working voice requires hand-editing config outside the app. In the same projection, transcription and realtime provider entries silently dropped plugin-declared `models`, so clients could never render a model picker from them.

## Why This Change Was Made

Mirrors the existing speech-provider seam: `RealtimeVoiceProviderPlugin` gains an optional `voices?: readonly string[]` that core projects into `talk.catalog` realtime entries — the projection lives in core, so plugins cannot add catalog fields themselves. Catalog pick-lists now go through one shared helper: speech, transcription, and realtime entries advertise `models`/`aliases`/`voices` only when non-empty, which also fixes the dropped `models`. The wire schema (`TalkCatalogProviderSchema`) already allowed all these fields, so the change is additive. The OpenAI plugin advertises its canonical voice list (the same set its config validation accepts); the Google plugin advertises the shared 30-name Google TTS voice inventory it already maintains — Google's Live API docs state native-audio models accept every TTS voice, and the realtime runtime forwards the configured voice id unvalidated. The SDK type and docs now pin the field's semantics: a provider-wide set of ids every supported model accepts, omitted when no such set exists. Migrating client pickers to consume the catalog is named follow-up work, marked at the web UI site.

## User Impact

Talk clients can now read provider-specific voice and model lists from `talk.catalog` instead of hard-coding them, and realtime voice provider plugin authors can advertise voices/models with a single registration field. Shipped client UIs are unchanged until the picker follow-up lands (web/iOS still render their hard-coded lists).

## Evidence

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/gateway/server-methods/talk.test.ts extensions/openai/realtime-voice-provider.test.ts` (local Linux, Node 24; no remote Testbox/Crabbox available in this environment): 92 + 65 tests passed. Covers voices/models projection, empty-list omission on both speech and realtime entries, transcription `models` projection, and pins the advertised OpenAI voice set to the list documented in `docs/nodes/talk.md`.
- tsgo typecheck lanes clean: core, extensions, core-test, extensions-test, ui.
- oxfmt/oxlint clean on changed files.
- `plugin-sdk:api:check` OK on the rebased head — the new optional SDK field does not shift the API baseline (type aliases are recorded by name), verified by regenerating before and after.

### Live Gateway proof (updated for the Google voices review finding)

Real setup on this PR head: fresh `pnpm build`, isolated `$OPENCLAW_HOME`, config with `talk.realtime.provider: "openai"` (no credentials configured — the catalog projection is registration-driven), gateway started with `openclaw gateway --bind loopback --allow-unconfigured`, then a real WS RPC via `openclaw gateway call talk.catalog --json`. target.title: fix(gateway): add base64 validation before decode in persistInboundImagesForTranscript
target.body:
## Summary

Fixes #105837

**Problem**: `persistInboundImagesForTranscript` decodes base64 image data via `Buffer.from(data, "base64")` without validating the encoding first. Malformed base64 can silently produce garbage bytes or unexpected errors.

**Solution**: Add `isValidBase64` guard before decode, throwing a clear error message when the image data is not valid base64. Export `isValidBase64` from the module so it can be tested directly against the production implementation.

**What changed**: One guard in `src/gateway/chat-attachments.ts:74` — `if (!isValidBase64(image.data))` before `Buffer.from` decode. Exported both `isValidBase64` and `isBase64DataCharCode` (previously module-private) to enable direct production testing. Rewrote `chat-attachments.base64.test.ts` to import and validate against the exported production function instead of using placeholder assertions and a reimplemented copy.

**NOT changed**: No changes to existing test behavior, no changes to image persistence logic, no changes to error handling outside this new guard. All existing tests continue to pass. The existing placeholder tests were replaced entirely with real assertions against the production function.

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior addressed**: `isValidBase64` guard validates base64 before `Buffer.from` decode in `persistInboundImagesForTranscript`.
**Real environment tested**: Linux x64, Node.js 25.9.0, OpenClaw `main@HEAD` with this patch applied.
**Exact steps or command run after this patch**: `node --import tsx/esm -e "..."` (simulates the guard+decode path of `persistInboundImagesForTranscript`)
**After-fix evidence**: 6/6 scenarios passed (see terminal output below).
**Observed result after the fix**: Valid 1x1 PNG image passes guard and decodes to 70 bytes; malformed/empty/unpadded inputs are all rejected by the guard before reaching `Buffer.from`.
**What was not tested**: End-to-end Gateway server with actual multipart uploads (requires full runtime); the guard+decode path is exactly what `persistInboundImagesForTranscript` does at lines 73-75.

## Tests and validation

```
$ pnpm test src/gateway/chat-attachments.base64.test.ts --reporter=verbose

 ✓ |gateway-core| isValidBase64 — production function > accepts valid padded base64
 ✓ |gateway-core| isValidBase64 — production function > rejects empty string
 ✓ |gateway-core| isValidBase64 — production function > rejects string with invalid characters
 ✓ |gateway-core| isValidBase64 — production function > rejects unpadded base64 (length not divisible by 4)
 ✓ |gateway-core| isValidBase64 — production function > rejects strings with padding in middle
 ✓ |gateway-core| isValidBase64 — production function > rejects strings with too much padding
 ...

 Test Files  4 passed (4)
      Tests  24 passed (24)
```

Real runtime behavior proof — the guard+decode path that `persistInboundImagesForTranscript` executes at lines 73-75:

```
$ node --import tsx/esm -e "..."

=== Real behavior proof: persistInboundImagesForTranscript guard ===

✓ Valid 1x1 PNG: guard passes, Buffer.from yields 70 bytes
✓ Malformed string 'invalid!': guard threw — attachment: invalid base64 content
✓ Empty string '': guard threw — attachment: invalid base64 content
✓ Unpadded base64 'abc': guard threw — attachment: invalid base64 content
✓ Padding in middle 'abc=defg': guard threw — attachment: invalid base64 content
✓ Excessive padding 'a===': guard threw — attachment: invalid base64 content

6/6 scenarios passed
```

Validated against the exported production `isValidBase64` function:

| Input | Expected | Result |
|-------|----------|--------|
| `"dGVzdA=="` (valid padded) | ✅ accept | passed |
| `"iVBORw0KGgo..."` (valid PNG base64) | ✅ accept | passed |
| `""` (empty) | ❌ reject | passed |
| `"invalid!"` (invalid chars) | ❌ reject | passed |
| `"abc"` (unpadded, length 3) | ❌ reject | passed |
| `"abc=defg"` (padding in middle) | ❌ reject | passed |
| `"a==="` (excessive padding) | ❌ reject | passed |

## Risk checklist

- [x] This change is backwards compatible — valid base64 inputs continue to decode as before
- [x] This change has been tested with existing configurations
- [ ] I have updated relevant documentation
- [x] Breaking changes (if any) are documented in Summary

---

target.title: fix: keep LINE group allowlists scoped [AI]
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where LINE operators who leave DMs open but configure group access as an allowlist could have group messages admitted without any group-specific allowlist entries.

## Why This Change Was Made

LINE group access now uses only the group-level allowlist sources when group policy is set to allowlist. The DM allowlist remains scoped to DMs, while group-specific overrides and account-level group allowlists continue to work through the existing channel ingress path.

## User Impact

Operators can keep DM access open without that DM setting broadening access in LINE groups. Existing group allowlist entries still admit the intended senders, and empty group allowlists now deny group senders consistently.

Compatibility note: LINE group configurations that previously relied on top-level DM `allowFrom` entries should set `groupAllowFrom` or per-group `allowFrom` for group senders.

## Evidence

- AI-assisted.
- AWS Crabbox `cbx_93178783bc9f` / `run_8181ae25ce5f`: `corepack pnpm test extensions/line/src/bot-handlers.test.ts -- --reporter=verbose`
- Result: `extensions/line/src/bot-handlers.test.ts` passed, 29 tests.

target.body:
Related: #102260

This is the focused current-main replacement for the deterministic goal-driver slice discussed in #102261 and #103586. It deliberately does not carry forward their unrelated question, plan, judge, wait-barrier, UI, generated, or Hermes-labelled scope.

## What Problem This Solves

OpenClaw can persist, display, budget, pause, block, resume, and complete a session goal, but an active goal still stops whenever a turn ends. Operators must send another message to keep an otherwise idle goal moving.

## Why This Change Was Made

This adds a default-off, deterministic gateway driver that uses the existing session goal, active-run, queued-turn, system-event, heartbeat, context, UI, and `goal_changed` paths. It reserves each bounded continuation durably before enqueueing a wake, lets user work win races, and auto-pauses at the configured ceiling.

The driver is intentionally limited to agent-scoped session keys. Current-main system-event queues cannot safely distinguish the same bare `global` key in multiple agent stores, and expanding queue identity belongs in a separate change. The durable-owner repair in #104265 is also kept separate rather than duplicated here.

## User Impact

Operators who explicitly enable `tools.experimental.goalDriver.enabled` can let an active session goal continue after a fixed idle delay without sending a synthetic user message. Existing goal controls and status UI remain the source of truth. The feature remains inert by default.

## Evidence

- RED contract: fork CI at exact test-only SHA `b5c2f60d959a3714af01be27eddd00b46aa6e7e6` reported the expected missing driver, service, goal reservation/rollback, and gateway-wiring symbols: https://github.com/100yenadmin/openclaw/actions/runs/29228761335
- Tests cover exact delay/no jitter, one timer per durable target, active/user/system queue precedence, persistence failure, race rollback, rejected enqueue, no self-rearm, dynamic disable, startup recovery, unsafe bare-key refusal, bounded concurrent reservations, resume reset, and terminal-persistence ordering.
- Structured pre-commit review of the tests-only contract completed with no actionable findings.
- GREEN exact-head CI and non-repository visual evidence will be added before this draft is marked ready.

target.title: fix(ai): avoid websocket cache clobber on stale reused release
target.body:
Closes #105434

## What Problem This Solves
Releasing a reused ChatGPT Responses WebSocket deleted `websocketSessionCache` by session id without checking whether a newer same-session connection already owned that slot. A stale release could close/evict a valid replacement connection.

## Why This Change Was Made
The new-connection release path already guarded deletion with an identity check (`cache.get(sessionId) === entry`). The reused-lease release path and idle-expiry callback did not, so a replacement-before-release race could clobber the newer socket. This extends the same ownership guard to those async teardown paths.

## User Impact
Cached WebSocket sessions are less likely to drop a healthy replacement connection when an older reused lease later releases or expires. No config or API changes.

## Evidence
- Source: `packages/ai/src/providers/openai-chatgpt-responses.ts` reused `release` + `scheduleSessionWebSocketExpiry` now delete only when the cache still references the captured entry (mirrors the existing new-connection release guard).
- Test: added replacement-before-release coverage in `packages/ai/src/providers/openai-chatgpt-responses.test.ts`.
- Proof: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs packages/ai/src/providers/openai-chatgpt-responses.test.ts` — 33 passed (Testbox warmup unavailable; local Vitest fallback).

target.title: perf: avoid event-loop stall during embedded_run bootstrap-context
target.body:
## Summary

Fix event-loop stalls during `embedded_run` bootstrap-context that block the event loop for 14-22 seconds, causing message loss.

### Root causes addressed

1. **Synchronous file I/O** — `readFileSync`/`closeSync` in workspace file loading blocks the event loop while reading root bootstrap files (AGENTS.md, SOUL.md, etc.)
2. **Unbounded blocking glob walks** — `fs.glob` for extra bootstrap files traverses the entire workspace tree synchronously inside Node, including `.git`/`node_modules` directories, without yielding to the event loop
3. **Uninterrupted hook chains** — `triggerInternalHook` executes all handlers back-to-back without yielding

### Changes

**`src/agents/workspace.ts`**
- Replace sync `readFileSync`/`closeSync` with callback-based async `readFdToString`/`closeFdAsync`
- Parallelize root bootstrap file reads via `Promise.all` (previously serial `for` loop)
- Replace `fs.glob` with an async traversal walker that yields via `setImmediate` every 256 entries, so a sparse pattern like `**/AGENTS.md` over a large workspace never blocks the event loop. The walker performs no directory pruning — it walks the full tree and returns every file matching the configured patterns, with no traversal cutoff and no artificial match cap; the downstream bootstrap character budget owns content limiting.
- Preserve `fs.glob` no-match parity: a configured glob that matches nothing resolves to an empty set (not the literal pattern), so it no longer emits a phantom missing-file diagnostic; the literal `[pattern]` result is reserved for the no-glob-support fallback only.
- Preserve `fs.glob` explicit directory-symlink parity: descend a symlink only when its aligned pattern segment is literal (non-wildcard) and `realpath` confirms a directory inside the workspace root, so an explicit configured pattern like `linked/**/AGENTS.md` still reaches descendants when `linked` is an in-workspace directory symlink. Symlinks reached through a wildcard segment stay terminal (matching `fs.glob`), workspace containment rejects symlink targets that escape the root, and a `realpath` ancestor-chain guard refuses re-entry into a directory already on the descent path so an ancestor-pointing symlink (`a/loop -> a`) cannot loop.
- Suppress `closeFdAsync` rejections to avoid masking read errors on NFS/FUSE

**`src/hooks/internal-hooks.ts`** / **`src/hooks/internal-hook-dispatch.ts`**
- Keep the public `triggerInternalHook(event)` signature (re-exported via `plugin-sdk/hook-runtime`) unchanged and matching `main` — no new public parameter or exported options type.
- Move the bootstrap-only handler scheduling (`yieldBetweenHandlers` with `setImmediate` yield between handlers) and per-handler timing/slow-handler (>500ms) warning into an internal `internal-hook-dispatch` module that is not on the plugin SDK surface.

**`src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/attempt.ts`**
- Instrument bootstrap-context substages (`workspace-file-load`, `hook-overrides`) with `performance.now` timing
- Log substage durations when total bootstrap-context exceeds 2 seconds
- Enable yielding between handlers for `agent:bootstrap` hook triggers (via the internal dispatch entrypoint)

**`src/agents/bootstrap-files.ts`** / **`src/agents/bootstrap-hooks.ts`**
- Keep the public `resolveBootstrapFilesForRun` params (re-exported via `plugin-sdk/agent-harness-runtime`) callback-free and matching `main`; route embedded-runner substage timing through an internal `resolveBootstrapFilesForRunWithTiming` variant kept off the SDK surface.
- Support the new async workspace file loading interface.

### Tests

- `workspace.test.ts` — 3 new tests for async fd read (happy path, cache hit, fd close on failure)
- `workspace.load-extra-bootstrap-files.test.ts` — every matching file returned without an artificial cap (no directory pruning), and a regression test asserting a late-appearing match in a large tree is still loaded (no traversal cutoff)
- `handler.test.ts` — no truncation warning is emitted for large glob scans
- `internal-hooks.test.ts` — yield-between-handlers ordering, handler timing reporting, and slow handler warning exercised through the internal dispatch entrypoint
- `workspace.load-extra-bootstrap-files.test.ts` — a no-match glob resolves to an empty set with no missing-file diagnostic (fs.glob parity)
- `workspace.load-extra-bootstrap-files.test.ts` — explicit directory-symlink glob parity across three states (real `fs.symlink`): a literal-named directory symlink is descended and its descendants match; a `**`-reached symlink stays terminal; an ancestor-pointing (cyclic) literal symlink terminates without looping

The public plugin SDK surface is unchanged: `node scripts/plugin-sdk-surface-report.mjs` exits 0 with no new package-exported entrypoints. All existing tests pass without modification.

### Performance impact

- Root bootstrap file loading: serial sync → parallel async (estimated 3-5x speedup for 8 files)
- Glob walks: synchronous/blocking → async with periodic `setImmediate` yields (prevents multi-second event-loop stalls on large workspaces). The walk completes fully; all configured matches are kept, and the existing bootstrap character-budget truncation handles content limiting.
- Hook chains: uninterrupted → yielded (prevents monopolizing the event loop during bootstrap)

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed**: Event-loop stalls during `embedded_run` bootstrap-context loading caused by synchronous I/O and a blocking `fs.glob` walk over large workspaces, which blocks the loop and drops messages. This change makes the glob walk async/yielding so the loop stays responsive, while preserving every configured `bootstrap-extra-files` glob match (the earlier iteration of this branch added a hard 20,000-entry traversal cutoff that silently dropped late matches — that cutoff is removed here).
- **Real environment tested**: Local patched OpenClaw checkout on macOS arm64, Node.js `v24.10.0`, run via `tsx` against the real exported `loadExtraBootstrapFiles` from `src/agents/workspace.ts`. Before/after captured from two git commits on the PR branch: before = `5849e709f4` (walker with the 20,000-entry cutoff), after = `5ce395d645` (cutoff removed).
- **Real environment scenario**: A workspace of ~26,100 filesystem entries (a 3-tier tree, 30×30×28 filler files) with a single configured-glob target `AGENTS.md` planted in the subtree the depth-first walker drains last, so the target is only reached after more than 20,000 visited entries. A 5ms repeating timer runs during the load as an event-loop liveness probe (steady ticks ⇒ the loop never stalled).
- **Failing proof before fix**: commit `5849e709f4` (cutoff present):
  ```
  approx filesystem entries: ~26100 (old cutoff was 20000)
  elapsed: 82.9ms
  liveness timer ticks during load: 16 (loop responsive)
  matched bootstrap files returned: 0
  deep AGENTS.md (past old 20k cutoff) loaded: false
  RESULT: late configured glob match was DROPPED (pre-fix behavior)
  ```
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch**:
  ```
  # against the patched checkout (commit 5ce395d645) a script that builds the
  # ~26,100-entry workspace, starts a 5ms liveness timer, then calls the real
  # loadExtraBootstrapFiles(root, ["**/AGENTS.md"]) and checks the deep match:
  npx tsx proof-live.mts
  ```
- **Evidence after fix**: terminal output from `node`/`tsx` against commit `5ce395d645` (cutoff removed):
  ```
  approx filesystem entries: ~26100 (old cutoff was 20000)
  elapsed: 99.4ms
  liveness timer ticks during load: 20 (loop responsive)
  matched bootstrap files returned: 1
  deep AGENTS.md (past old 20k cutoff) loaded: true
  RESULT: configured glob match beyond old cutoff is PRESERVED; event loop stayed live
  ```
- **Observed result after fix**: With the cutoff removed, the configured `**/AGENTS.md` match located past the old 20,000-entry frontier is now loaded (1 file returned vs 0 before in the terminal output above), so existing broad `bootstrap-extra-files` configs no longer silently lose AGENTS.md/TOOLS.md context. The liveness timer kept ticking throughout the async walk (20 ticks during the ~99ms load), confirming the periodic `setImmediate` yields — not the cutoff — are what keep the event loop responsive.
- **What was not tested**: No full live `embedded_run` with active channel connections was driven end-to-end; this proof exercises the real glob-resolution code path and event-loop liveness directly rather than through a connected channel. The focused regression coverage lives in `workspace.load-extra-bootstrap-files.test.ts` and `handler.test.ts`.

### Directory-symlink glob parity proof

- **Behavior addressed**: The cooperative walker only descended `Dirent.isDirectory()` entries and emitted symlinks as leaf candidates, so an explicit configured pattern such as `linked/**/AGENTS.md` no longer reached descendants when `linked` is an in-workspace directory symlink — Node's `fs.glob` resolves that case, so the walker silently dropped configured bootstrap context. The walker now descends a literal-named path-segment symlink when `realpath` confirms a directory inside the workspace, keeps wildcard-reached symlinks terminal, and guards against ancestor cycles.
- **Real environment tested**: Local patched OpenClaw checkout on macOS arm64, Node.js `v24.10.0`. Three regression tests build real temp directories with real `fs.symlink` links and drive the real exported extra-bootstrap glob resolver.
- **Steps run**: `npx vitest run src/agents/workspace.load-extra-bootstrap-files.test.ts src/agents/workspace.test.ts`
- **Observed result**: `Test Files 4 passed (4)`, `Tests 156 passed (156)`. The three symlink states are covered: (a) literal-named directory symlink is descended and its descendants match; (b) a `**`-reached symlink stays terminal; (c) an ancestor-pointing (cyclic) literal symlink terminates without looping (guarded by a 15s timeout). A TDD red check confirmed test (a) fails on the pre-fix walker (missing the `linked/` descendants) and passes after the fix; `tsgo:core` exits 0 and `oxfmt --check` reports both files formatted.
- **What was not tested**: Behavior on Windows/`EPERM`/`ENOSYS` filesystems where symlink creation is unavailable — those cases skip cleanly rather than assert.

Closes #87509

target.title: feat(teams): add exact-tab workspace sharing
target.body:
Refs #105322.

Builds on the Workspaces foundation landed in #104139.

## What Problem This Solves

OpenClaw's operator dashboard is intentionally single-operator and privileged. Teams need a narrower way to share selected workspace tabs with external members without exposing chat, gateway state, global presence, other workspaces, or workspace administration.

## Why This Change Was Made

- add opt-in, gateway-local Teams accounts, opaque sessions, one-time invites, and a scope-less `member` role
- add exact resource RBAC, domain isolation, server-attested agent delegation, and host-bound plugin Teams primitives
- partition Workspaces by isolation domain and support exact-tab read, request-change, and write access
- add a restricted `/teams` portal with owner invite/review controls and no operator dashboard navigation or global gateway state

### Security and privacy boundaries

- member sockets receive no gateway-global presence, health, defaults, chat, or plugin broadcasts
- remote plaintext Teams authentication is rejected; loopback HTTP remains an explicit local-development path
- invite codes and session tokens are omitted from ordinary JSON/list responses and browser persistence
- invited users and delegated agents cannot receive workspace-admin or sharing-admin authority in v1
- CLI-backed agent harnesses carry the server-owned Teams subject only through an opaque loopback grant; the subject is cache-bound and is not projected into child environment variables, headers, or plugin-visible context fields
- logout, expiry, revocation, membership removal, and grant removal are revalidated against open member sessions

## User Impact

- Workspace owners can invite a member and grant exact-tab `read`, `request changes`, or `write` access.
- Members use a restricted `/teams` portal rather than the privileged operator Control UI.
- Requests for changes return to the owning user for approval; members and agents cannot become workspace or sharing administrators in v1.
- The feature remains local and opt-in. It adds no SaaS identity, email delivery, SSO/SCIM, billing, cross-gateway federation, or member access to the normal operator dashboard.

## Evidence

- 611 focused feature assertions pass across six Vitest shards: gateway, CLI, plugin API, Workspaces, and UI
- 160 MCP grant/tool-resolution assertions pass, plus targeted CLI-subject and loopback domain-cache isolation regressions
- production core/extensions and core/extensions test TypeScript projects pass
- scoped oxfmt, oxlint, and `git diff --check` pass
- bootstrap -> invite -> exact read -> cross-tab denial -> session revocation integration flow passes
- independent reviews of security, Workspaces semantics, UI privacy, rebase conflict adaptations, and CLI-harness identity propagation found no remaining concrete issues

The repository-wide UI-test TypeScript project currently reports four strictness errors in unchanged `ui/src/pages/chat/chat-view.test.ts`; the 67 focused Teams/UI assertions pass.

target.title: fix(recovery): reclaim terminal-phase reply operations in stuck-session recovery
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Stuck-session recovery unconditionally keeps the lane for any reply operation in the registry (`reason=active_reply_work`), even operations that will never produce progress — permanently wedging the lane until gateway restart.
- **Problem**: Two phantom scenarios exist:
  1. A ReplyOperation with terminal phase (completed/failed/aborted) remains in the registry via `retainFailureUntilComplete` or `terminalSettleTimer`. Recovery sees `isEmbeddedAgentRunActive = true` and keeps the lane forever — no progress data means `isActiveRunProgressStale` never triggers.
  2. A ReplyOperation in non-terminal phase (running) but with zero diagnostic progress events (`lastProgressAgeMs = undefined`). `isActiveRunProgressStale` returns `false` for undefined ages, so the stale-progress path never fires. The lane stays wedged.
- **Solution**: 
  1. Terminal-phase check before `active_reply_work`/`keep_lane` — reclaim completed/failed/aborted operations after the 60s terminal settle window.
  2. `fallbackAgeMs` parameter in `isActiveRunProgressStale` — when no diagnostic progress exists, fall back to the overall session age so phantoms without any activity can still be reclaimed.
- **What changed**: `diagnostic-stuck-session-recovery.runtime.ts` (terminal-phase branch + `fallbackAgeMs` in stale check), `diagnostic-stuck-session-recovery.runtime.test.ts` (settle window guard test, no-progress phantom test, `it.each` for all three terminal phases)
- **What did NOT change**: `reply-run-registry.ts`, `runs.ts`, `classifySessionAttention`, `isActiveAbortRecoveryEligible`; deferred-maintenance and running-phase behavior; embedded run handle detection

## Change Type

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] Feature
- [ ] Refactor required for the fix

## Motivation

Issue #105712 reports that a chat session lane can get wedged by a phantom active run: the lane's claim says an `embedded_run` is doing reply work, but no such run exists. The stuck-session recovery detects the stuck session, but then declines to act because `reason=active_reply_work` exempts the claim unconditionally. The only recovery is a full gateway restart.

This affects builds where a ReplyOperation finishes but stays in the registry (terminal phase) or where a run died before emitting any diagnostic events (no-progress phantom). The root cause is twofold:
1. `isActiveRunProgressStale` returns `false` when `lastProgressAgeMs` is `undefined`
2. The reply-work branch has no fallback for terminal-phase operations

The diagnostic classification system (`classifySessionAttention`) also cannot set `allowActiveAbort: true` for these phantoms because there's no active work kind.

## Evidence

- Behavior addressed: Session recovery keeps the lane for terminal-phase or no-progress reply operations, permanently wedging the channel lane until gateway restart
- Real environment tested: Linux (Ubuntu Azure VM), Node v24.14.0, branch `fix/reclaim-terminal-embedded-run-105712`

  2. Terminal-phase operations still within the 60s settle window keep the lane — logged as "still within settle window"

No-diagnostic-progress phantom handled by `fallbackAgeMs` fallback (applies to any phase). Settle window (60s) prevents premature reclamation. `it.each` covers all three terminal phases + explicit settle window + no-progress tests.
  - ✅ Path coverage: Both call sites of `isActiveRunProgressStale` (active embedded run path and reply work path) pass `fallbackAgeMs`. The terminal-phase check is a new branch added before the existing `active_reply_work` return.
  - ✅ Cleanup symmetry: Both paths (terminal-phase reclaim and stale-progress reclaim) call the same `abortAndDrainEmbeddedAgentRun` function with `forceClear: true`. `clearState()` in `expireStaleReplyRunBySessionId` is idempotent (guarded by `stateCleared`).

## Root Cause

Two separate gaps in `diagnostic-stuck-session-recovery.runtime.ts`:

1. **Terminal-phase gap**: The `!activeSessionId && activeWorkSessionId && isEmbeddedAgentRunActive(...)` branch unconditionally returns `keep_lane` for any ReplyOperation still in the registry, even terminal-phase operations that have already completed/failed/aborted.

2. **No-progress gap**: `isActiveRunProgressStale` returns `false` when `lastProgressAgeMs` is `undefined` (no diagnostic events recorded). A phantom run that dies before first transcript flush leaves zero diagnostic activity, so the stale-progress path never fires. The session is permanently exempt from `keep_lane` → `active_reply_work`.

Both gaps interact: the diagnostic system sees no active work kind for these phantoms, so `classifySessionAttention` classifies them as `recoveryEligible` (correct) but `isActiveAbortRecoveryEligible` sees no `embedded_run` and never sets `allowActiveAbort: true`. | (same) | phase=running + no diagnostic activity + old session → reclaim | **New**: No-progress phantoms reclaimed |
| (same) | phase=deferred_maintenance → keep_lane | Deferred maintenance preserved |
| `diagnostic-stuck-session-recovery.integration.test.ts` | Full recovery flow | Recovery coordinator integration |
| `reply-run-registry.test.ts` | All registry operations | Registry lifecycle unaffected |

- Verified scenarios: Unit tests for all three terminal phases + settle window guard + no-progress phantom + running + deferred-maintenance + stale-abort paths. 152 tests total across 4 suites.
- Edge cases checked: Non-terminal phases not reclaimed; settle window (< 60s) prevents premature reclaim; `undefined` phase handled safely by `else` fallthrough; empty diagnostic activity falls back to session age
- What you did NOT verify: Full gateway long-run with real phantom injection (requires production race conditions); macOS/Windows platforms (Linux only)

- [x] Config/env changes? No
- [x] Migration needed? No

## Best-fix Verdict

- **Best fix**: Yes. The fix addresses both identified phantom scenarios (terminal-phase and no-progress) at the recovery decision point with minimal code change (one new `if` branch + `fallbackAgeMs` parameter). ClawSweeper's two P1 findings (phase-less phantom handling and terminal settlement guard) are both addressed.
- **Refactor needed**: No
- **Alternative considered**: (1) Checking `isReplyRunEvidenceStale` in the recovery runtime — rejected because the recovery function doesn't directly access the operation object. (2) Narrowing `isEmbeddedAgentRunActive` in `runs.ts` — rejected because of broader usage across message queueing and abort paths. (3) Adding fallback to `classifySessionAttention` — rejected because the classification layer should stay focused on diagnostic activity, not reply-run-registry state.

## Risks and Mitigations

**Highest risk area**: Premature reclamation during the 60s terminal settle window, allowing follow-up turns to interleave with still-draining terminal delivery.

**Mitigation**: The settle guard checks `terminalPhaseAgeMs >= 60s` before reclaiming. In practice `stuckSessionWarnMs` (180s default) >> 60s settle window, so by the time recovery fires, the settle timer has long expired. The guard adds defense-in-depth for lower warn thresholds.

**Additional risk**: No-progress phantoms with `queueDepth = 0` (no queued messages) are still not reclaimed because `isActiveRunProgressStale` returns `false` when there's no work to process. This is by design — if no messages are queued, there's nothing to recover. Once a new message arrives, `queueDepth` becomes > 0 and recovery can proceed.

**Compatibility impact**: None.

target.title: fix(slack): bound userCache growth with pruneMapToMaxSize
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`userCache` in Slack monitor context stores resolved user names from `users.info` API calls but has no pruning — every unique user ID accumulates forever. On a busy Slack workspace with thousands of users, this Map grows without bound.

## Why This Change Was Made

`channelCache` already uses `pruneMapToMaxSize(channelCache, 1024)` but `userCache` was missed. The fix adds the same pattern at 2048 entries.

## User Impact

- Prevents unbounded memory growth in long-running Slack monitor sessions
- Oldest entries are evicted when the cap is reached
- No behavioral change for typical usage (2048 entries covers most workspaces)

## Evidence

### Real Slack API — Token + users.info

```
$ curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer \$SLACK_TOKEN" https://slack.com/api/auth.test
{
    "ok": true,
    "bot_id": "B0BGACNKEGJ",
    "team_id": "T0BG72E2G2Z",
    "user_id": "U0BFV1X131V"
}

$ curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer \$SLACK_TOKEN" https://slack.com/api/users.info?user=U0BFV1X131V
{
    "ok": false,
    "error": "missing_scope",
    "needed": "users:read",
    "provided": "channels:history,channels:read,chat:write,..."
}
```

The token is valid but lacks `users:read` scope, matching the `missing_scope` error path already handled by the catch block in `resolveUserName`. Real Slack workspaces with `users:read` scope would resolve successfully and fill the cache.

### Unit Test — Proves actual eviction

```
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/slack/src/monitor/context.test.ts
 ✓ evicts the oldest user name when the bounded user cache fills
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  10 passed (10)
```

Test flow:
1. resolveUserName("U0OLDEST") → 1 API call, cached
2. Fill 2048 more users → 2048 API calls, U0OLDEST evicted
3. Re-request resolveUserName("U0OLDEST") → fresh API call (cache miss)
4. expect(usersInfo).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(2050) → PASS

Without eviction, step 3 would return the stale cached entry and total would stay at 2049.

### Lint + Format
```
$ npx oxlint -c .oxlintrc.json extensions/slack/src/monitor/context.ts  # No errors
$ npx oxfmt --check extensions/slack/src/monitor/context.ts              # Correct format
```

## What Changed

- extensions/slack/src/monitor/context.ts: +2 lines (SLACK_USER_CACHE_MAX_ENTRIES + pruneMapToMaxSize)
- extensions/slack/src/monitor/context.test.ts: +19 lines (eviction test with re-request assertion)

- **AI-assisted**: Yes
- **Co-Authored-By**: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>
- **Human confirmed understanding**: Yes

target.title: fix(goals): preserve durable owner across completion wakes
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Completion wakes can execute under a transient run-session key even though a session goal is owned by the durable user-facing origin route, such as a Telegram topic. Goal tools previously preferred the transient `runSessionKey`, so `get_goal` could return `null` while the goal still existed on the durable owner session.

## Why This Change Was Made

Goal tool scope resolution now prefers a concrete `agentSessionKey`, which represents the durable owning thread, and uses the run-session key only for legacy `global` contexts or when no owner key exists. This keeps completion wakes and recovered runs attached to the same goal without adding a channel-specific rule or changing the persisted goal shape.

The change is intentionally limited to core goal owner resolution, its focused regression coverage, and the directly coupled goal documentation.

## User Impact

`get_goal`, `create_goal`, and `update_goal` continue to resolve the durable thread goal when execution temporarily runs under another session key. Existing structured goals require no migration.

Compatibility limitation: legacy goals containing only an objective plus an external Markdown checklist do not contain a structured executable phase ledger. This lookup fix cannot infer missing phase identities or automatically launch missing phases; durable multi-phase scheduling still requires a task or flow controller that persists phase state.

## Evidence

target.title: fix(release): keep reviewed migration residue nonfatal
target.body:
## Summary

- keep canonical SQLite-vs-retired JSON plugin-install conflicts visible as Doctor notices instead of fatal migration warnings
- keep an explicitly non-Codex-owned legacy binding sidecar visible as a Doctor notice without importing or deleting it
- preserve warnings for invalid JSON, failed writes/archives, ambiguous ownership, and other unresolved migration failures

## Root cause

The `release/2026.7.1` startup checkpoint treats every state-migration warning as fatal. Two reviewed, non-converging residue conditions still emitted warnings after `openclaw doctor --fix`: an obsolete JSON plugin-install index that conflicts with newer canonical SQLite rows, and a legacy Codex binding sidecar whose session is explicitly owned by another harness. The next gateway start therefore repeated the same warning and refused readiness indefinitely.

This change preserves both artifacts and their operator visibility while separating them from unresolved migration failures.

Refs #103076 and #90213.

## Verification

- `pnpm test src/infra/state-migrations.state-dir.test.ts src/commands/doctor-state-migrations.test.ts extensions/codex/doctor-contract-api.test.ts` (112 tests passed)
- `pnpm format:check -- src/infra/state-migrations.ts src/infra/state-migrations.state-dir.test.ts src/commands/doctor-state-migrations.test.ts extensions/codex/src/migration/session-binding-sidecars.ts extensions/codex/doctor-contract-api.test.ts`
- `pnpm build`
- independent Codex review; initial P2 notice-propagation finding fixed with a red/green regression test; final review clean with no actionable findings

## Real behavior proof

Behavior addressed: `2026.7.1-beta.6` gateway restart loop after updater completion when Doctor cannot remove reviewed migration residue.

Real environment tested: managed Linux VM upgraded from `2026.6.11` to core and official Codex plugin `2026.7.1-beta.6`; customer identity and addresses withheld.

Exact steps or command run after this patch:

- built an installable beta.6 core artifact with the canonical OpenClaw package helper and installed it over the managed beta.6 service
- installed the official `@openclaw/codex@2026.7.1-beta.6` package, then overlaid the reviewed Codex migration module from this branch so the plugin retained official-install trust
- ran `openclaw doctor --fix --non-interactive`, restarted the managed gateway, and checked systemd state plus both gateway/proxy listeners
- temporarily allowed `codex/gpt-5.6-sol` (without changing the default), then ran a fresh explicit agent session at `thinking=high`; removed the temporary allowlist entry after the smoke

Evidence after fix:

target.title: fix(channels): progress drafts only for long tasks, with the model's own preamble as the status headline
target.body:
Closes #105872

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Discord (and other progress-mode channels) showed an AI-written "working" status even for tasks that finish in a few seconds. The progress-draft start gate promised a 5-second delay but started immediately on the second work event, which nearly every tool-using turn triggers; the utility-model narrator additionally burned a paid completion on every small turn even when the draft never rendered. Separately, the narrated status was fully synthetic even though the model already narrates its own work in typed pre-tool preamble events.

## Why This Change Was Made

Small tasks should get just the answer; only genuinely long turns should show a working status, and that status should prefer the model's own words. The gate is now purely time-based (explicit immediate-start paths such as approvals and patches are unchanged), the narrator defers all utility-model calls until the draft is actually visible, and in progress mode the draft's status line is now the model's freshest typed preamble - always on, no new config - with utility narration only as filler when the model has been quiet for ~20s or emits no preamble. Preambles never start the draft early, so the time gate still owns the small-vs-big decision. The opt-in `streaming.progress.commentary` lane and its receipt counters are unchanged. LOC-ratchet compliance is paid for with real splits (`progress-draft-status-text.ts`, Telegram `progress-draft-preview.ts`, and small ownership moves) plus lower-only baseline updates.

## User Impact

- Small/fast tasks on Discord and Telegram no longer flash a status draft or an activity receipt; they get a plain answer.
- Long tasks show a status headline written by the model itself ("Reading the gateway config, then restarting agents.") refreshed as work progresses, with cheap-model narration covering silences; the final answer still carries the `-#` activity receipt and the draft is deleted.
- Operators stop paying for narration completions that were never rendered.

## Evidence

- Gate fast-path root cause: `createChannelProgressDraftGate.noteWork()` started on `workEvents > 1` (src/channels/streaming.ts); default delay `DEFAULT_PROGRESS_DRAFT_INITIAL_DELAY_MS = 5000` almost never applied.
- Eager narrator: first tool note always passed `shouldRunNow` (src/auto-reply/reply/progress-narrator.ts) regardless of draft visibility.
- Typed preamble lane (no string inference): embedded commentary normalization and CLI `onCommentaryText` both emit `kind: "preamble"` item events (src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner-execution.ts).
- Validation on Blacksmith Testbox through Crabbox (leases `tbx_01kxcm7g262wveq2pqqgr1yst5`, `tbx_01kxcrd3xm285wg71xz0sn4kmf`, `tbx_01kxcrwtc2ampzrvvrj5at85c6`): `pnpm test:changed` (auto-reply/discord/telegram/matrix/msteams/slack/compositor/narrator suites green after fixes), `pnpm plugin-sdk:surface:check` green (freshness constant kept off the SDK barrels), `pnpm build` green (plugin-sdk DTS budget respected), LOC ratchet: this branch removes 2 violations vs origin/main and adds 0 (diff proof against stashed clean main on the same box).
- Known pre-existing failures on latest origin/main, unrelated to this diff and reproduced on a clean stashed tree on the same Testbox: LOC-ratchet drift on ~50 files (locales, embedded runner, cli-output, etc.) that cannot be baseline-raised by design, plus flaky broad-shard timeouts (live-network Telegram polling, ui custom-element re-registration); shard-level base-vs-branch comparison output retained in the session logs.

target.title: fix(clickclack): accept prefixed mixed-case message targets
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users sending ClickClack messages could hit an unsupported target error when the target included the ClickClack provider prefix or used mixed-case target kinds.

The broken case is a mismatch between ClickClack's advertised target contract and its private target parser:

- ClickClack already declares `targetPrefixes: ["clickclack", "cc"]`.
- ClickClack already wires `normalizeTarget: normalizeClickClackTarget`.
- The parser only accepted lowercase, unprefixed target kinds before this change.

That means a target like `ClickClack:Channel:General` looked like a valid ClickClack target to OpenClaw's provider-target layer, but the ClickClack parser treated `ClickClack` as the target kind and rejected the whole value.

Before this fix:

```text
Input target:       ClickClack:Channel:General
Parsed target kind: ClickClack
Result:            Unsupported ClickClack target
```

After this fix:

```text
Input target:       ClickClack:Channel:General
Canonical target:   channel:General
Channel id used:    General
```

This matters for users who type a target manually, copy a value from another tool, or generate targets through scripts/integrations that preserve display-style casing such as `ClickClack:` or `Channel:`.

The same mismatch affected direct messages and thread targets:

```text
cc:DM:usr_1
clickclack:Thread:msg_1
```

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing ClickClack target contract already allows provider-qualified targets through `clickclack:` and `cc:`. This change makes the ClickClack parser follow that same contract for:

```text
clickclack:
cc:
channel:
thread:
dm:
```

The fix is intentionally narrow:

- It stays inside the ClickClack plugin boundary.
- It changes only prefix matching, not the accepted target syntax.
- It does not add config, dependencies, migrations, or fallback behavior.
- It preserves the target id text after stripping the provider/kind prefixes.

The parser is the right place for the fix because it feeds normalization, outbound delivery, and session routing. Fixing only the send call site would leave normalized target behavior and session route behavior inconsistent.

This is the narrowest correct owner-boundary fix because all ClickClack send, route, and normalize paths already funnel through `parseClickClackTarget`. Fixing the parser makes the behavior consistent for:

- message-tool target normalization through `normalizeClickClackTarget`
- outbound HTTP delivery through `sendClickClackText`
- outbound session routing through `resolveOutboundSessionRoute`

The change deliberately does not modify shared outbound target policy or session-key generation. Existing canonical ClickClack targets keep the same behavior, and session routing keeps its current route/session-key semantics.

## User Impact

Users and agents can now send ClickClack messages when the target comes from a provider-qualified form or mixed-case user input. These examples now resolve to the intended canonical target:

| User-provided target | Canonical target after parsing |
| --- | --- |
| `ClickClack:Channel:General` | `channel:General` |
| `CC:Channel:General` | `channel:General` |
| `cc:DM:usr_1` | `dm:usr_1` |
| `clickclack:Thread:msg_1` | `thread:msg_1` |

Lowercase inputs continue to behave the same:

| Existing target | Canonical target |
| --- | --- |
| `channel:general` | `channel:general` |
| `dm:usr_1` | `dm:usr_1` |
| `thread:msg_1` | `thread:msg_1` |

That removes a user-visible delivery failure without requiring users to know that ClickClack's internal parser previously only accepted lower-case, unprefixed target syntax.

## Evidence

### Code-path proof

- `extensions/clickclack/src/channel.ts` already declares `targetPrefixes: ["clickclack", "cc"]`, `normalizeTarget: normalizeClickClackTarget`, and sends outbound session targets through `parseClickClackTarget`.
- `extensions/clickclack/src/outbound.ts` calls `parseClickClackTarget(params.to)` before choosing channel, thread, or DM delivery.
- `extensions/clickclack/src/channel.ts` calls the same parser from `resolveOutboundSessionRoute()` before building the outbound session route.
- `src/agents/embedded-agent-subscribe.tools.ts` normalizes message-tool targets through `normalizeTargetForProvider`, so the ClickClack normalizer is on the real agent message-send path.
- `src/plugin-sdk/core.ts` provides `stripChannelTargetPrefix`, which strips known provider prefixes case-insensitively while preserving the remaining target text.

Because these call sites share `parseClickClackTarget()`, stripping provider prefixes and comparing target kinds case-insensitively aligns detection, normalization, session routing, and message sending without adding a second path.

### Before/after behavior covered by tests

The parser regression test in `extensions/clickclack/src/target.test.ts` proves provider-prefixed and mixed-case targets normalize while preserving the target id:

```text
parseClickClackTarget("ClickClack:Channel:General") -> { kind: "channel", id: "General" }
normalizeClickClackTarget("CC:Channel:General") -> "channel:General"
buildClickClackTarget(parseClickClackTarget("clickclack:Thread:msg_1")) -> "thread:msg_1"
parseClickClackTarget("CC:DM:usr_1") -> { kind: "dm", id: "usr_1" }
```

The send-path regression test in `extensions/clickclack/src/outbound.test.ts` proves the actual outbound message path uses the stripped channel id:

```text
sendClickClackText({ to: "ClickClack:Channel:General", text: "hi", ... })
```

The mocked ClickClack client is asserted against:

```text
createChannelMessage("General", "hi", ...)
```

The session-route regression test in `extensions/clickclack/src/session-route.test.ts` proves provider-prefixed mixed-case targets become canonical route targets:

```text
cc:DM:usr_1 -> to: "dm:usr_1", chatType: "direct"
ClickClack:Channel:General -> to: "channel:General", chatType: "group"
```

### Validation run

Focused ClickClack tests:

```bash
env OPENCLAW_HEAVY_CHECK_LOCK_SCOPE=worktree OPENCLAW_VITEST_NO_OUTPUT_TIMEOUT_MS=120000 node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/clickclack/src/target.test.ts -- --reporter=verbose
```

Result:

```text
[test] passed 1 Vitest shard in 13.33s
```

```bash
env OPENCLAW_HEAVY_CHECK_LOCK_SCOPE=worktree OPENCLAW_VITEST_NO_OUTPUT_TIMEOUT_MS=120000 node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/clickclack/src/outbound.test.ts -- --reporter=verbose
```

Result:

```text
[test] passed 1 Vitest shard in 12.54s
```

```bash
env OPENCLAW_HEAVY_CHECK_LOCK_SCOPE=worktree OPENCLAW_VITEST_NO_OUTPUT_TIMEOUT_MS=120000 node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/clickclack/src/session-route.test.ts -- --reporter=verbose
```

Result:

```text
[test] passed 1 Vitest shard in 19.82s
```

Diff whitespace check:

```bash
git diff --check
```

Result: passed.

### Validation notes

Remote Testbox validation could not be completed from this checkout earlier because the Crabbox wrapper failed its basic binary sanity check before running tests. The focused local fallback above was used for the touched ClickClack surface.

Autoreview could not be completed in this environment because `python3` is Python 3.6 and the script requires a newer parser; running it with `python3.13` reached the review helper but failed because the `codex` executable is not installed.

target.body: ## What Problem This Solves Skills are copied into the sandbox workspace on every sandbox setup. For users who do not use skills or have already preinstalled them in their sandbox Docker image, this sync is unnecessary overhead and adds startup latency. Related: #97638 ## Why This Change Was Made Adds `skipSkillsSync` (Docker-only) under `agents.defaults.sandbox.docker` and `agents.list[].sandbox.docker`, defaulting to `false`. When enabled: 1. **File copying skipped**: `syncSkillsToWorkspace` is not called — no skill files are copied into the sandbox workspace. 2. **Skill eligibility preserved**: `computeSandboxSkillsEligibility` still runs; remote skill eligibility is advertised in agent prompts. 3. **Safe name-only prompt**: A new `SkillSnapshot` is built from `resolvedSkills` with sandbox-agnostic name-only entries (no host `` paths). Skill names are XML-escaped. Prompt respects configured `skills.limits.maxSkillsInPrompt` and `maxSkillsPromptChars`. The `skills` array is preserved for env overrides. 4. **Command prompt guard**: When `skipSkillsSync=true`, the command/system-prompt skill inspection returns empty early, preventing fallthrough to host-path-based snapshot resolution. ## User Impact ```json5 { agents: { defaults: { sandbox: { docker: { skipSkillsSync: true, setupCommand: "mkdir -p /workspace/skills && cp -r /preloaded-skills/* /workspace/skills/" } } } } } ``` Safe-use contract: Docker-only backend option. Skills must be preinstalled via `docker.setupCommand` or `docker.binds`. target.title: fix(memory): backfill provider.model with resolved model name
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When a memory embedding adapter returns an empty `provider.model` (because the user did not explicitly configure a model, leaving it to `adapter.defaultModel`), the downstream memory identity, `providerKey`, chunk model tags, and vector search filters all see `""` instead of the resolved model name. This causes persistent `Dirty` index state and broken vector search (`WHERE c.model = ''` returns zero rows), reported as issue #90042.

## Why This Change Was Made

The `createWithAdapter` function already resolves the model via `resolveProviderModel(adapter, options.model)` and passes it into `adapter.create(...)`. But the returned `result.provider.model` can be empty if the adapter itself returns an empty string — the resolved model is discarded after `create` returnscars, leaving downstream consumers with no fallback.

The fix is a single-line backfill at the return site: `result.provider.model || resolvedModel`. This is a *runtime backfill*, not a persisted-data migration.

## Behavior Matrix

| Scenario | result.provider.model | adapter.defaultModel (resolvedModel) | Before | After | Changed? |
|----------|----------------------|--------------------------------------|--------|-------|----------|
| User explicitly sets model | `"qwen3-8b"` | irrelevant | `"qwen3-8b"` | `"qwen3-8b"` (short-circuit `\|\|`) | ❌ No |
| User leaves empty, adapter has default | `""` | `"text-embedding-3-small"` | `""` (bug) | `"text-embedding-3-small"` | ✅ Fix |
| User leaves empty, adapter has no default | `""` | `""` | `""` | `""` (`"" \|\| ""` = `""`) | ❌ No |
| User leaves empty, provider returns correct model | `"ada-002"` | irrelevant | `"ada-002"` | `"ada-002"` (short-circuit `\|\|`) | ❌ No |

Only scenario 2 changes, which is the exact bug from issue #90042.

## User Impact

Transparent for correct configurations (scenarios 1, 3, 4 — zero change). Users who saw a persistent `Dirty` index due to an empty `provider.model` will find their vector search working again after upgrade. No migration or reindex needed.

## Real Behavior Proof

**Real environment tested**: Linux x86_64, Node v24.13.1, upstream/main

**Exact steps or command run after this patch**:

```bash
node --import tsx --input-type=module -e "
import { createEmbeddingProvider } from './extensions/memory-core/src/memory/embeddings.ts';

// Scenario 1: Explicit model + live embedding via ZTE MaaS endpoint
const r1 = await createEmbeddingProvider({
  provider: 'openai-compatible',
  model: 'Qwen3-Embedding-8B',
  config: { models: { providers: { 'openai-compatible': { api: 'openai', baseUrl: '<redacted>', apiKey: '<redacted>' } } } },
  remote: { baseUrl: '<redacted>', apiKey: '<redacted>' },
});
console.log('Explicit model provider.model:', JSON.stringify(r1.provider?.model));
const vec = await r1.provider?.embedQuery?.('hello world');
console.log('embedQuery dims:', vec?.length);

// Scenario 2: No explicit model — backfill from adapter.defaultModel
const r2 = await createEmbeddingProvider({
  provider: 'openai',
  model: '',
  config: { models: { providers: { openai: { api: 'openai', baseUrl: '<redacted>', apiKey: '<redacted>' } } } },
  remote: { baseUrl: '<redacted>', apiKey: '<redacted>' },
});
console.log('Empty model provider.model (backfilled):', JSON.stringify(r2.provider?.model));
"
```

**Evidence after fix**:

```
Explicit model provider.model: "Qwen3-Embedding-8B"
embedQuery dims: 4096
Empty model provider.model (backfilled): "text-embedding-3-small"
```

**Observed result after fix**: Explicit model → `provider.model` matches. Empty model → `provider.model` backfilled from `adapter.defaultModel` (`"text-embedding-3-small"`). On upstream/main (without this patch), scenario 2 returns `""`.

**What was not tested**: Full `openclaw memory index --force` reindex through the gateway (requires full workspace setup). The proof covers the production `createEmbeddingProvider` → `embedQuery` code path with a real embedding endpoint, which is the exact code path changed by this PR.

Supersedes #91660 (31 days old, merge conflicts, larger diff with unrelated deletions). This branch is based on latest upstream/main with a focused +5/-2 diff.

target.title: fix(ui): order model-dependent chat settings
target.body:
Related: #102871, #103253

## What Problem This Solves

Control UI could show a newly selected model while a reasoning or speed update was still validated against the previous model. Switching from Anthropic Claude Fable 5 to OpenAI GPT-5.6 Sol and choosing Sol's `ultra` reasoning level could therefore fail with an error claiming `ultra` was unsupported for Fable.

## Why This Change Was Made

The immediate-apply picker sent model, reasoning, and speed changes as independent overlapping `sessions.patch` requests. The renderer disabled model-dependent controls during a switch, but an already-dispatched event could still cross that render boundary, and rapid model selections could be applied by the Gateway out of user order.

Control UI now tracks pending model switches by the same canonical session identity used for its existing pending-settings gate. Model-dependent reasoning and speed updates wait for the selected model to commit, failed model switches drop and roll back dependent settings, and rapid model switches preserve selection order. The shared coordination moved into a focused module, bringing `chat-session.ts` below the repository's 500-line production-file limit.

Gateway validation remains strict. This fixes the client ordering bug instead of weakening provider-specific thinking-level checks or adding a fallback.

## User Impact

The model picker can switch between providers with different reasoning labels without reporting the previous provider's validation error. GPT-5.6 Sol's Ultra level is applied only after Sol is the committed session model; failed model changes do not leak dependent settings.

## Evidence

- Blacksmith Testbox `tbx_01kxcz354kck4w7xjcg9d66ggf`, exact head `2f40164f154`:
  - `pnpm check:changed` — passed, including LOC ratchet, formatting, core-test/UI typechecks, and lint.
  - Focused rapid-switch ordering and failed-switch rollback tests — 2 passed.
- Same rebased patch before the final rapid-switch hardening (`fe9dbe242e2`), Blacksmith Testbox `tbx_01kxcz354kck4w7xjcg9d66ggf`:
  - `pnpm test ui/src/pages/chat/chat-view.test.ts ui/src/pages/chat/chat-send.test.ts` — 390 passed.
  - `pnpm test:ui:e2e ui/src/e2e/chat-flow.e2e.test.ts -t "applies provider-specific reasoning after the selected model is saved"` — 1 passed.
  - `pnpm build` — passed, including the production Control UI build.
- Mocked browser proof delayed the model response, verified reasoning stayed locked, swapped Fable's label set for Sol's, selected Ultra, and observed no unsupported-level error.
- Fresh Codex autoreview: no accepted or actionable findings, overall confidence 0.93.

AI-assisted: yes, Codex.
