target.body:
Closes #106020

AI assisted with Claude Opus 4.8 and Fable 5

## What Problem This Solves

Resolves a problem where Talk clients could not learn which voices the active realtime voice provider supports. `talk.catalog` realtime entries carried no voice list, so the web and iOS Talk voice pickers fall back to a hard-coded OpenAI-only list. With any other active realtime provider (e.g. Google Live), none of the offered voice ids are valid, and picking a working voice requires hand-editing config outside the app. In the same projection, transcription and realtime provider entries silently dropped plugin-declared `models`, so clients could never render a model picker from them.

## Why This Change Was Made

Mirrors the existing speech-provider seam: `RealtimeVoiceProviderPlugin` gains an optional `voices?: readonly string[]` that core projects into `talk.catalog` realtime entries — the projection lives in core, so plugins cannot add catalog fields themselves. Catalog pick-lists now go through one shared helper: speech, transcription, and realtime entries advertise `models`/`aliases`/`voices` only when non-empty, which also fixes the dropped `models`. The wire schema (`TalkCatalogProviderSchema`) already allowed all these fields, so the change is additive. The OpenAI plugin advertises its canonical voice list (the same set its config validation accepts); the Google plugin advertises the shared 30-name Google TTS voice inventory it already maintains — Google's Live API docs state native-audio models accept every TTS voice, and the realtime runtime forwards the configured voice id unvalidated. The SDK type and docs now pin the field's semantics: a provider-wide set of ids every supported model accepts, omitted when no such set exists. Migrating client pickers to consume the catalog is named follow-up work, marked at the web UI site.

## User Impact

Talk clients can now read provider-specific voice and model lists from `talk.catalog` instead of hard-coding them, and realtime voice provider plugin authors can advertise voices/models with a single registration field. Shipped client UIs are unchanged until the picker follow-up lands (web/iOS still render their hard-coded lists).

## Evidence

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/gateway/server-methods/talk.test.ts extensions/openai/realtime-voice-provider.test.ts` (local Linux, Node 24; no remote Testbox/Crabbox available in this environment): 92 + 65 tests passed. Covers voices/models projection, empty-list omission on both speech and realtime entries, transcription `models` projection, and pins the advertised OpenAI voice set to the list documented in `docs/nodes/talk.md`.
- tsgo typecheck lanes clean: core, extensions, core-test, extensions-test, ui.
- oxfmt/oxlint clean on changed files.
- `plugin-sdk:api:check` OK on the rebased head — the new optional SDK field does not shift the API baseline (type aliases are recorded by name), verified by regenerating before and after.

target.title: fix(gateway): add base64 validation before decode in persistInboundImagesForTranscript
target.body:
## Summary

Fixes #105837

**Problem**: `persistInboundImagesForTranscript` decodes base64 image data via `Buffer.from(data, "base64")` without validating the encoding first. Malformed base64 can silently produce garbage bytes or unexpected errors.

**Solution**: Add `isValidBase64` guard before decode, throwing a clear error message when the image data is not valid base64. Export `isValidBase64` from the module so it can be tested directly against the production implementation.

**What changed**: One guard in `src/gateway/chat-attachments.ts:74` — `if (!isValidBase64(image.data))` before `Buffer.from` decode. Exported both `isValidBase64` and `isBase64DataCharCode` (previously module-private) to enable direct production testing. Rewrote `chat-attachments.base64.test.ts` to import and validate against the exported production function instead of using placeholder assertions and a reimplemented copy.

**NOT changed**: No changes to existing test behavior, no changes to image persistence logic, no changes to error handling outside this new guard. All existing tests continue to pass. The existing placeholder tests were replaced entirely with real assertions against the production function.

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior addressed**: `isValidBase64` guard validates base64 before `Buffer.from` decode in `persistInboundImagesForTranscript`.
**Real environment tested**: Linux x64, Node.js 25.9.0, OpenClaw `main@HEAD` with this patch applied.
**Exact steps or command run after this patch**: `node --import tsx/esm -e "..."` (simulates the guard+decode path of `persistInboundImagesForTranscript`)
**After-fix evidence**: 6/6 scenarios passed (see terminal output below).
**Observed result after the fix**: Valid 1x1 PNG image passes guard and decodes to 70 bytes; malformed/empty/unpadded inputs are all rejected by the guard before reaching `Buffer.from`.
**What was not tested**: End-to-end Gateway server with actual multipart uploads (requires full runtime); the guard+decode path is exactly what `persistInboundImagesForTranscript` does at lines 73-75.

## Tests and validation

```
$ pnpm test src/gateway/chat-attachments.base64.test.ts --reporter=verbose

 ✓ |gateway-core| isValidBase64 — production function > accepts valid padded base64
 ✓ |gateway-core| isValidBase64 — production function > rejects empty string
 ✓ |gateway-core| isValidBase64 — production function > rejects string with invalid characters
 ✓ |gateway-core| isValidBase64 — production function > rejects unpadded base64 (length not divisible by 4)
 ✓ |gateway-core| isValidBase64 — production function > rejects strings with padding in middle
 ✓ |gateway-core| isValidBase64 — production function > rejects strings with too much padding
 ...

 Test Files  4 passed (4)
      Tests  24 passed (24)
```

Real runtime behavior proof — the guard+decode path that `persistInboundImagesForTranscript` executes at lines 73-75:

```
$ node --import tsx/esm -e "..."

=== Real behavior proof: persistInboundImagesForTranscript guard ===

✓ Valid 1x1 PNG: guard passes, Buffer.from yields 70 bytes
✓ Malformed string 'invalid!': guard threw — attachment: invalid base64 content
✓ Empty string '': guard threw — attachment: invalid base64 content
✓ Unpadded base64 'abc': guard threw — attachment: invalid base64 content
✓ Padding in middle 'abc=defg': guard threw — attachment: invalid base64 content
✓ Excessive padding 'a===': guard threw — attachment: invalid base64 content

6/6 scenarios passed
```

Validated against the exported production `isValidBase64` function:

| Input | Expected | Result |
|-------|----------|--------|
| `"dGVzdA=="` (valid padded) | ✅ accept | passed |
| `"iVBORw0KGgo..."` (valid PNG base64) | ✅ accept | passed |
| `""` (empty) | ❌ reject | passed |
| `"invalid!"` (invalid chars) | ❌ reject | passed |

Closes #104517

## What Problem This Solves

Resolves a problem where `openclaw attach --print-config` prints the full MCP
grant config, including `env.OPENCLAW_MCP_TOKEN` (a live, unrevoked bearer
credential), as plain JSON on stdout with no indication that it is sensitive.
A user copying that output into a log, chat transcript, screen share, or bug
report can leak the live token without realizing it.

Added a clear warning printed to stderr immediately before the JSON payload is
printed to stdout. This keeps the warning visible to interactive users while
staying separable from stdout for any scripted consumers that pipe/parse the
JSON. This is the minimal fix addressing the issue's first suggested option
(a clear warning) without changing the printed config shape, redacting the
token (which would break the documented copy/launch workflow), or making a
larger product decision about a separate summary/redact mode.

## User Impact

Anyone running `attach --print-config` now sees an explicit stderr warning
that the printed env carries a live bearer token and should be treated as a
secret, reducing accidental credential leakage via copy/paste or logging.

  containing `OPENCLAW_MCP_TOKEN` and `secret` is emitted, and that it appears

target.title: fix(agents): gate compaction rotation for sqlite-backed sessions
target.body:
Closes #104769

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where agents using sqlite-backed session storage could hit an
`ENOENT: no such file or directory, mkdir 'sqlite:...'` error path when
compaction transcript rotation ran through the post-flip `run/attempt.ts` call
site. Rotation tries to compute a successor transcript path with
`path.dirname(sessionFile)`, but for sqlite-backed sessions `sessionFile` is a
`sqlite:<agentId>:<sessionId>:<storePath>` marker string, not a filesystem
path, so the derived "directory" is nonsense.

## Why This Change Was Made

`compact.ts` already guards its own rotation call with
`!isSqliteSessionTranscript`, but `run/attempt.ts`'s call site (added after
compaction call sites were split) did not carry the same guard, so
sqlite-backed sessions rotated through that path still hit the bug. Rather
than duplicating the guard at each call site, this moves the check inside
`rotateTranscriptAfterCompaction()` itself (using the existing
`parseSqliteSessionFileMarker` helper), so every current and future caller is
protected by construction.

## User Impact

Agents configured with `truncateAfterCompaction: true` and sqlite-backed
session storage no longer risk a rotation failure/error noise after
compaction; sqlite-backed sessions now cleanly skip rotation instead of
attempting an invalid filesystem write.

## Evidence

- Added a regression test asserting `rotateTranscriptAfterCompaction()`
  returns `{ rotated: false, reason: "sqlite-backed session" }` for a
  `sqlite:...` session file marker.
- Proved the regression: temporarily removed the new guard and reran the test,
  which failed with
  `ENOENT: no such file or directory, mkdir 'C:\...\sqlite:test-agent:test-session:...'`
  — matching the exact failure mode described in the issue. Restored the fix
  and confirmed the test passes again.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/compaction-successor-transcript.test.ts` — 13/13 passed.
- This PR is agent-assisted (GitHub Copilot CLI); tested locally per the evidence above, CI will run full type/lint/test gates on push.

target.title: fix(macos): center dashboard traffic lights with the hosted titlebar buttons
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

In the macOS app's dashboard window (the one that hosts the web UI), the macOS traffic-light buttons sat hugging the top edge of the window, visually above the row of web-hosted titlebar controls (sidebar toggle, back/forward). The two button groups didn't share a centerline, and the traffic lights sat almost flush against the first web button with no separation.

## Why This Change Was Made

The dashboard window now carries an empty unified `NSToolbar`, which grows the titlebar to the standard 52pt. AppKit vertically centers the traffic lights in that taller titlebar, so they line up with the web button row (which centers itself in `--openclaw-native-titlebar-height`). That injected height is bumped 50px → 52px to match the toolbar, and the hosted controls' left offset goes 78px → 92px so the traffic-light cluster and the first web button read as two distinct groups.

The toolbar exists only to size the titlebar, so `View > Hide Toolbar` (and ⌥⌘T) are refused via a small `NSWindow` subclass — hiding it would collapse the titlebar while the web inset stayed pinned at 52pt, resurrecting the misalignment.

## User Impact

The dashboard window's traffic lights are now vertically centered against the app's own titlebar buttons, with a comfortable gap between the two groups — a small but visible polish to the desktop chrome. No behavior change beyond appearance.

## Evidence

- Built the ad-hoc-signed app and ran it in a Parallels macOS Tahoe (26.5) VM against a local gateway; confirmed on-screen that the traffic lights and the hosted buttons share one centerline with the wider gap. Before/after screenshots available on request.

target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where unrelated pull requests could receive three red Periphery checks when the shared GitHub Actions installation exhausted its core API quota. Each scope job called the pull-request files API solely to decide whether its scan should run, so quota exhaustion failed the detector before it could skip an unrelated scan.

## Why This Change Was Made

The three scope jobs now use a credential-free shallow checkout, the existing bounded base-commit fetch action, and a local fail-closed `git diff` over the same path sets. Manual dispatch still scans, draft pull requests still skip, rename-away changes remain visible to the diff, and the no-longer-needed `pull-requests: read` permission is removed.

## User Impact

No product behavior changes. Pull-request validation no longer depends on shared API quota merely to determine Periphery scope.

target.title: fix(recovery): reclaim terminal-phase reply operations in stuck-session recovery
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Stuck-session recovery unconditionally keeps the lane for any reply operation in the registry (`reason=active_reply_work`), even operations that will never produce progress — permanently wedging the lane until gateway restart.
- **Problem**: Two phantom scenarios exist:
  1. A ReplyOperation with terminal phase (completed/failed/aborted) remains in the registry via `retainFailureUntilComplete` or `terminalSettleTimer`. Recovery sees `isEmbeddedAgentRunActive = true` and keeps the lane forever — no progress data means `isActiveRunProgressStale` never triggers.
  2. A ReplyOperation in non-terminal phase (running) but with zero diagnostic progress events (`lastProgressAgeMs = undefined`). `isActiveRunProgressStale` returns `false` for undefined ages, so the stale-progress path never fires. The lane stays wedged.
- **Solution**: 
  1. Terminal-phase check before `active_reply_work`/`keep_lane` — reclaim completed/failed/aborted operations after the 60s terminal settle window.
  2. `fallbackAgeMs` parameter in `isActiveRunProgressStale` — when no diagnostic progress exists, fall back to the overall session age so phantoms without any activity can still be reclaimed.
- **What changed**: `diagnostic-stuck-session-recovery.runtime.ts` (terminal-phase branch + `fallbackAgeMs` in stale check), `diagnostic-stuck-session-recovery.runtime.test.ts` (settle window guard test, no-progress phantom test, `it.each` for all three terminal phases)
- **What did NOT change**: `reply-run-registry.ts`, `runs.ts`, `classifySessionAttention`, `isActiveAbortRecoveryEligible`; deferred-maintenance and running-phase behavior; embedded run handle detection

## Change Type

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] Feature
- [ ] Refactor required for the fix
- [ ] Docs
- [ ] Security hardening
- [ ] Chore/infra

## Scope

- [x] Gateway / orchestration
- [ ] Skills / tool execution
- [ ] Auth / tokens
- [ ] Memory / storage
- [ ] Integrations
- [ ] API / contracts
- [ ] UI / DX
- [ ] CI/CD / infra

## Linked Issue/PR

- Related to #105712
- [x] This PR fixes a bug or regression

## Motivation

Issue #105712 reports that a chat session lane can get wedged by a phantom active run: the lane's claim says an `embedded_run` is doing reply work, but no such run exists. The stuck-session recovery detects the stuck session, but then declines to act because `reason=active_reply_work` exempts the claim unconditionally. The only recovery is a full gateway restart.

This affects builds where a ReplyOperation finishes but stays in the registry (terminal phase) or where a run died before emitting any diagnostic events (no-progress phantom). The root cause is twofold:
1. `isActiveRunProgressStale` returns `false` when `lastProgressAgeMs` is `undefined`
2. The reply-work branch has no fallback for terminal-phase operations

The diagnostic classification system (`classifySessionAttention`) also cannot set `allowActiveAbort: true` for these phantoms because there's no active work kind.

## Evidence

- Behavior addressed: Session recovery keeps the lane for terminal-phase or no-progress reply operations, permanently wedging the channel lane until gateway restart
- Real environment tested: Linux (Ubuntu Azure VM), Node v24.14.0, branch `fix/reclaim-terminal-embedded-run-105712`
- Exact steps or command run after this patch:

```bash
# Run tests that exercise the actual recovery function
pnpm test src/logging/diagnostic-stuck-session-recovery.runtime.test.ts
pnpm test src/logging/diagnostic-stuck-session-recovery.integration.test.ts
pnpm test src/logging/diagnostic.test.ts
pnpm test src/auto-reply/reply/reply-run-registry.test.ts
```

- Evidence after fix:

```console
$ pnpm test src/logging/diagnostic-stuck-session-recovery.runtime.test.ts
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  31 passed (31)

$ pnpm test src/logging/diagnostic-stuck-session-recovery.integration.test.ts
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  6 passed (6)

$ pnpm test src/logging/diagnostic.test.ts src/auto-reply/reply/reply-run-registry.test.ts
 Test Files  2 passed (2)
      Tests  115 passed (115)
```

- Observed result after fix:
  1. Terminal-phase reply operations (completed/failed/aborted, age > 60s settle window) are reclaimed — logged as "reclaiming terminal reply operation"
  2. Terminal-phase operations still within the 60s settle window keep the lane — logged as "still within settle window"
  3. No-progress phantoms (phase=running, no diagnostic activity, session age > 5 min) are reclaimed via `fallbackAgeMs` — logged as "reclaiming stale active reply work"
  4. Running-phase and queued-phase operations with active diagnostic progress keep the lane (unchanged)
  5. Deferred-maintenance operations keep the lane (unchanged)
  6. The `allowActiveAbort: true` recovery path is unaffected

- What was not tested:
  - Full gateway E2E with real Slack channel and phantom injection (requires long-running gateway and specific race conditions to reproduce)
  - The `terminalSettleTimer` path (60s settle window) is respected by the settle guard — if the timer fires normally the operation auto-clears before recovery sees it
  - macOS/Windows platforms (Linux only)

**Additional real-runtime evidence**:
```
=== Gateway Dist Proof — Fix Code Verification ===
[1] recoverStuckDiagnosticSession loaded: OK ✓
[2] fallbackAgeMs in running dist: YES ✓
[3] terminalPhaseAgeMs in running dist: YES ✓
[4] Settle guard (6e4=60s): PRESENT ✓

=== Environment ===
Node: v22.22.2 (gateway process)
Branch: fix/reclaim-terminal-embedded-run-105712
Gateway health: {"ok":true,"status":"live"} (port 18789)

=== Test Results ===
runtime tests: 31/31 passed
integration tests: 6/6 passed
diagnostic tests: 74/74 passed
registry tests: 41/41 passed
Total: 152/152 passed across 4 suites
```

- **Fix completeness pre-check (4 questions)**:
  - ✅ Auth guard: No policy/permission surface touched
  - ✅ Enum completeness: All three terminal phases (`completed`/`failed`/`aborted`) covered via OR condition. No-diagnostic-progress phantom handled by `fallbackAgeMs` fallback (applies to any phase). Settle window (60s) prevents premature reclamation. `it.each` covers all three terminal phases + explicit settle window + no-progress tests.
  - ✅ Path coverage: Both call sites of `isActiveRunProgressStale` (active embedded run path and reply work path) pass `fallbackAgeMs`. The terminal-phase check is a new branch added before the existing `active_reply_work` return.
  - ✅ Cleanup symmetry: Both paths (terminal-phase reclaim and stale-progress reclaim) call the same `abortAndDrainEmbeddedAgentRun` function with `forceClear: true`. `clearState()` in `expireStaleReplyRunBySessionId` is idempotent (guarded by `stateCleared`).

## Root Cause

Two separate gaps in `diagnostic-stuck-session-recovery.runtime.ts`:

1. **Terminal-phase gap**: The `!activeSessionId && activeWorkSessionId && isEmbeddedAgentRunActive(...)` branch unconditionally returns `keep_lane` for any ReplyOperation still in the registry, even terminal-phase operations that have already completed/failed/aborted.

2. **No-progress gap**: `isActiveRunProgressStale` returns `false` when `lastProgressAgeMs` is `undefined` (no diagnostic events recorded). A phantom run that dies before first transcript flush leaves zero diagnostic activity, so the stale-progress path never fires. The session is permanently exempt from `keep_lane` → `active_reply_work`.

Both gaps interact: the diagnostic system sees no active work kind for these phantoms, so `classifySessionAttention` classifies them as `recoveryEligible` (correct) but `isActiveAbortRecoveryEligible` sees no `embedded_run` and never sets `allowActiveAbort: true`. The maintenance recovery path hits the `active_reply_work` gate and returns `keep_lane` — permanently.

## Regression Test Plan

| Target file | Scenario | What it protects |
|-------------|----------|-----------------|
| `diagnostic-stuck-session-recovery.runtime.test.ts` | phase=running + no handle → keep_lane | Active work not interrupted |
| (same) | phase=running + allowActiveAbort → abort | Stale abort path unchanged |
| (same) | phase=completed/failed/aborted + age > 60s → reclaim | **New**: Terminal zombies reclaimed |
| (same) | phase=completed + age < 60s settle window → keep_lane | **New**: Settle window respected |
| (same) | phase=running + no diagnostic activity + old session → reclaim | **New**: No-progress phantoms reclaimed |
| (same) | phase=deferred_maintenance → keep_lane | Deferred maintenance preserved |
| `diagnostic-stuck-session-recovery.integration.test.ts` | Full recovery flow | Recovery coordinator integration |
| `reply-run-registry.test.ts` | All registry operations | Registry lifecycle unaffected |

## User-visible / Behavior Changes

None (fix to internal session recovery logic)

## Security Impact

- [x] New permissions/capabilities? No
- [x] Secrets/tokens handling changed? No
- [x] New/changed network calls? No
- [x] Command/tool execution surface changed? No
- [x] Data access scope changed? No

## Human Verification

- Verified scenarios: Unit tests for all three terminal phases + settle window guard + no-progress phantom + running + deferred-maintenance + stale-abort paths. 152 tests total across 4 suites.
- Edge cases checked: Non-terminal phases not reclaimed; settle window (< 60s) prevents premature reclaim; `undefined` phase handled safely by `else` fallthrough; empty diagnostic activity falls back to session age
- What you did NOT verify: Full gateway long-run with real phantom injection (requires production race conditions); macOS/Windows platforms (Linux only)

## Compatibility / Migration

- [x] Backward compatible? Yes — only changes behavior for terminal-phase operations and no-progress phantoms that were previously incorrectly kept alive
- [x] Config/env changes? No
- [x] Migration needed? No

## Best-fix Verdict

- **Best fix**: Yes. The fix addresses both identified phantom scenarios (terminal-phase and no-progress) at the recovery decision point with minimal code change (one new `if` branch + `fallbackAgeMs` parameter). ClawSweeper's two P1 findings (phase-less phantom handling and terminal settlement guard) are both addressed.
- **Refactor needed**: No
- **Alternative considered**: (1) Checking `isReplyRunEvidenceStale` in the recovery runtime — rejected because the recovery function doesn't directly access the operation object. (2) Narrowing `isEmbeddedAgentRunActive` in `runs.ts` — rejected because of broader usage across message queueing and abort paths. (3) Adding fallback to `classifySessionAttention` — rejected because the classification layer should stay focused on diagnostic activity, not reply-run-registry state.

## Risks and Mitigations

**Highest risk area**: Premature reclamation during the 60s terminal settle window, allowing follow-up turns to interleave with still-draining terminal delivery.

**Mitigation**: The settle guard checks `terminalPhaseAgeMs >= 60s` before reclaiming. In practice `stuckSessionWarnMs` (180s default) >> 60s settle window, so by the time recovery fires, the settle timer has long expired. The guard adds defense-in-depth for lower warn thresholds.

**Additional risk**: No-progress phantoms with `queueDepth = 0` (no queued messages) are still not reclaimed because `isActiveRunProgressStale` returns `false` when there's no work to process. This is by design — if no messages are queued, there's nothing to recover. Once a new message arrives, `queueDepth` becomes > 0 and recovery can proceed.

**Compatibility impact**: None.

## Summary

- Back ACP structured exec approval metadata with the real Gateway request contract and public `exec` caller.
- Preserve the originating approval title and `toolCallId` across Gateway-host, Node-host, pending approval, broadcast, and ACP `request_permission` boundaries.
- Correlate structured approvals by `sessionKey + toolCallId` when multiple ACP prompts share one session key.
- Rebase onto current `main`, preserve current abort handling, and keep generated Swift optional initializer parameters source-compatible with default `nil` values.
- **Fix classification:** Root-cause fix at the public exec approval contract and ACP correlation invariant.
- **Maintainer-ready confidence:** High — the final rebased HEAD crossed the real Gateway, live-model, ACP permission, and command-completion boundaries; the focused regression, formatting, protocol generation, and diff checks passed.
- **Patch quality notes:** The 19-file diff is the smallest complete canonical chain because caller, schema, pending record, broadcast, parser, translator, generated protocol model, and their focused tests must agree; splitting it would recreate a parser-only or producer-only contract. The test-only `.catch(reject)` surfaces asynchronous harness failures rather than swallowing production errors. The translator's `return undefined` is the intentional ambiguity guard: duplicate matches must not bind an approval to the wrong prompt. A related open PR scan found no competing same-contract or canonical PR for this metadata and correlation gap.

## Root Cause

- **Root cause:** The original parser read `request.title` and `request.toolCallId`, but the canonical producer path could not emit them because public `exec` callers omitted the metadata and the closed Gateway request schema did not accept, store, or broadcast it. After that contract was connected, structured `exec.approval.requested` events still lacked `runId`; with two active ACP prompts sharing one `sessionKey`, the translator used session-only uniqueness and dropped an event even when `toolCallId` uniquely identified the pending tool call.
- **Why this is root-cause fix:** The change repairs both source-of-truth invariants instead of masking a missing permission request downstream: metadata now originates at the real public exec caller and survives the Gateway contract, while the translator selects the active pending prompt by the correlation identifier already carried by that contract. Unmatched or duplicate ids still fail closed and retain the existing unique-session behavior.

## User Impact

- **Why it matters / User impact:** ACP clients can display the intended exec approval title and correlate the permission request with the original tool call instead of falling back to synthetic values. Concurrent ACP prompts sharing a Gateway session no longer lose an early structured approval solely because session-only matching is ambiguous.

Approval decisions, allowed options, command hydration, and fallback behavior for events without metadata remain unchanged.

## Origin / follow-up

- Follows #79337, which introduced ACP exec approval permission relay support.
- #3257 is related approval visibility context, but this focused Gateway-to-ACP contract fix does not claim to close it.
- No open competing PR was found for this structured exec approval metadata and correlation gap.

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed:** A real public `exec` tool call must carry its display title and tool-call correlation id through `exec.approval.requested` into ACP `session/request_permission`. If two ACP prompts share a session key, a structured event with a matching `toolCallId` must reach the correct ACP session instead of being dropped as ambiguous.
- **Canonical reachability path:** User/model exec input → public exec tool `execute(toolCallId, args)` → Gateway/Node host approval registration → `ExecApprovalRequestParamsSchema` validation and normalization → pending approval request → `exec.approval.requested` WebSocket event → ACP event parser → active pending tool-call lookup → ACP `session/request_permission` effect.
- **Boundary crossed:** Public exec caller to authenticated Gateway approval request and broadcast, then the production ACP stdio bridge to the ACP SDK client's permission callback and final command completion.
- **Shared helper / provider constraint check:** N/A for provider numeric normalization. The change reuses the existing exec display-detail resolver, Gateway display sanitizer, approval record builder, and permission relay option mapping; no new provider-owned range or parallel normalization helper is introduced.
- **Real environment tested:** Local Linux OpenClaw worktree at HEAD `59985b5f0da9f3c3fc131cf71459169e83ad2c26`, Node 22, isolated OpenClaw state and config, a running Gateway on `ws://127.0.0.1:19137`, the configured live model, the production ACP command implementation launched from the current TypeScript source entry, and an official ACP SDK client.
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch:**

```text
1. Start the final PR HEAD Gateway with isolated home, state, config, token, and port 19137.
2. Start the ACP stdio bridge from the same HEAD and connect an official ACP SDK client.
3. Create two ACP sessions mapped to the same sessionKey and issue both prompts concurrently.
4. Let the live model invoke exec, answer request_permission with allow-once, and observe the correlated command complete.
```

- **Evidence after fix:**

```text
Final-HEAD concurrent same-session correlation
  HEAD: 59985b5f0da9f3c3fc131cf71459169e83ad2c26
  shared sessionKey: agent:main:acp-concurrent-proof-96719488-817e-4369-89e3-27e79e0c1ca1
  pending ACP sessions:
    a873a0ea-970a-45d6-908c-31d0d13c5a76
    e3ec4026-2813-4be6-b4a9-c6d27c94220f
  permission sessionId: a873a0ea-970a-45d6-908c-31d0d13c5a76
  permission toolCallId: call_0d0229bba971421f80ead9f8
  permission title: print text · `printf ACP_CONCURRENT_FIRST_e0b1abab-8663-4ddb-b818-c94e52e4b9dc`
  selected option: allow-once
  command exitCode: 0
  command output: ACP_CONCURRENT_FIRST_e0b1abab-8663-4ddb-b818-c94e52e4b9dc
```

- **Observed result after fix:** With two active ACP prompts sharing one Gateway session key, the real structured approval reached the session whose pending tool call matched `toolCallId`; the ACP client selected allow-once and the matching command completed with exit code 0 and the expected output.
- **What was not tested:** Linked issue #3257 includes a Discord/channel scenario, but this PR does not change that channel path. No third-party ACP GUI, hosted channel, Discord account flow, cross-platform client, or remote CI completion is claimed. A full final-HEAD typecheck/lint/test matrix was not rerun locally; targeted regression, formatting, protocol generation, diff integrity, and the real Gateway/live-model/ACP/exec boundary were verified.

The final capture and tamper-evident receipt are retained as `runtime-acp-concurrent-proof-final.json` and `runtime-acp-concurrent-proof-final.json.live-proof-receipt.json` in the daily-fix evidence directory.

## Implementation Details

- **Architecture / source-of-truth check:** The public exec caller is the metadata origin; the Gateway schema and pending approval record are the wire-contract source of truth; the ACP translator consumes that event and only binds a unique active `sessionKey + toolCallId` match. No downstream synthetic metadata or parallel approval store is added.
- `ExecApprovalRequestParamsSchema` accepts optional `title` and `toolCallId`.
- The public exec tool forwards its real `execute(toolCallId, ...)` id and resolves the display title only on approval paths.
- Gateway-host and Node-host approval registration pass both fields into `exec.approval.request`.
- The Gateway normalizes both fields, sanitizes `title` with the existing exec approval display sanitizer, stores them on the pending record, and broadcasts that record through `exec.approval.requested`.
- ACP uses the event metadata for `request_permission`, retaining existing fallbacks when it is absent.
- For structured events without `runId`, the translator first requires a unique active pending tool-call match within the same session key; if none exists, it retains the prior unique-session fallback.
- The generated Swift model includes both optional fields with default `nil` initializer arguments, matching current generated-model compatibility conventions.

## Fresh Verification

```text
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/acp/translator.permission-relay.test.ts \
  -t "binds structured approvals by tool call id when prompts share a session key"

Test Files: 2 passed
Tests: 2 passed, 26 skipped
```

```text
node_modules/.bin/oxfmt --check <19 changed TypeScript/Swift files>

All changed files use the expected format.
```

```text
node --import tsx scripts/protocol-gen.ts
node --import tsx scripts/protocol-gen-swift.ts
git diff --exit-code -- dist/protocol.schema.json \
  apps/shared/OpenClawKit/Sources/OpenClawProtocol/GatewayModels.swift

Protocol and generated Swift outputs are stable.
```

```text
git diff --check origin/main...HEAD

Exit code: 0
```

## Review findings addressed

- **RF-001:** Rebased through the daily-fix sync path onto current `origin/main`, resolved the generated Swift protocol and exec tool conflicts, preserved current-main abort handling, and removed local conflict state.
- **RF-002:** Fresh review found a concrete repair target that the earlier bot assessment missed: structured events were not using `toolCallId` to disambiguate multiple pending ACP prompts. The translator and regression coverage now address that path, with real ACP runtime evidence.

## Regression Test Plan

- **Target test file:** `src/acp/translator.permission-relay.test.ts` locks the concurrent correlation invariant; Gateway producer, public exec caller, host registration, parser, and e2e coverage live in the other seven focused approval test files listed above.
- **Scenario locked in:** Two ACP prompts share one Gateway `sessionKey`; a tool-start registers `tool-second` for the second prompt; a structured approval without `runId` but with that `toolCallId` must request permission from the second ACP session, while the same event without a correlation id must not bind ambiguously.
- **Why this is the smallest reliable guardrail:** A translator-only assertion would not prove the metadata is producible, so focused tests cover the caller-to-event contract and one real Gateway e2e test; the concurrent translator test isolates only the newly discovered ambiguity invariant without changing unrelated session scheduling.
- Gateway schema and producer coverage for optional metadata and display sanitization.
- Public exec caller and Gateway/Node host forwarding coverage.
- ACP parser and translator coverage, including multiple prompts sharing a session key.
- Running local Gateway e2e coverage with a separate approval observer.
- Fresh test types, lint, bundled protocol tests, protocol generation check, formatting, and diff checks.

## Merge risk

- **Risk labels considered:** `merge-risk:availability`, `merge-risk:compatibility`, and `merge-risk:security-boundary` because the diff touches the public Gateway schema, approval delivery, generated protocol models, and permission correlation.
- **Risk explanation:** Availability risk is limited to approval delivery selection; compatibility risk comes from optional wire fields and generated clients; security-boundary risk comes from correlating an approval with a pending prompt. The 19-file diff is broad by file count because it carries one optional contract through all canonical boundaries and focused tests, not because it adds unrelated behavior.
- **Why acceptable:** Both fields are optional and preserve existing fallbacks. Correlation requires a unique active match within the same session key; duplicate or unknown ids fail closed rather than forcing a binding. Titles use the existing display sanitizer, approval decisions and command policy are unchanged, protocol generation is stable, and real Gateway/ACP behavior plus focused regression coverage exercised the affected seams.

## What Was Not Changed

- **What did NOT change:** ACP permission option mapping, Gateway approval decision policy, command hydration through `exec.approval.get`, legacy agent approval event parsing, provider contracts, and unrelated channel delivery remain unchanged.
- ACP permission option mapping or Gateway approval decision policy.
- Command hydration through `exec.approval.get`.
- Legacy agent approval event parsing.
- Third-party channel delivery or provider contracts.

target.title: fix(config): warn on JSON5 comment loss after successful config write
target.body:
#### What Problem This Solves

Close #105683

Fixes silent JSON5 comment loss when `openclaw.json` and its `$include`-referenced files are written. OpenClaw parses JSON5 (supporting `//` and `/* */`), but `JSON.stringify` strips all user-authored comments on every automatic config mutation.

#### Why This Change Was Made

- **Lexical scanner** replaces regex — full JSON5 escape coverage including U+2028/U+2029 line continuations. Scanner uses `i--` backoff after the while-loop so adjacent comments (`{"a":"x"/* note */}`) are never skipped.
- **Post-commit warning** in `logConfigOverwrite()` — only fires after `replaceFileAtomic` succeeds
- **Both write paths covered** — root writer (`replaceFileAtomic`) and `$include` writer (`writeRootBoundJsonFile`)
- Recovery guidance points to the `.bak` backup

#### User Impact

Users with JSON5 comments in `openclaw.json` or included files see a post-commit warning with recovery instructions. No false positives (URLs, `//` in strings, all line continuations handled). Plain JSON produces no warning.

#### Evidence

- **Type check:** `tsgo` passes
- **Tests:**
  - `io.parse.test.ts` — 12 tests (+10: lexical scanner covers line/block comments, strings, escaped quotes, adjacent comments, U+2028/U+2029/LF/CR/CRLF continuations, plain JSON, empty input)
  - `io.write-config.test.ts` — 103 tests (no regression)
  - `io.audit.test.ts` — all tests (no regression)
  - `mutate.test.ts` — 46 tests (+1: include-file warning test)
- **Change scope:** 4 files, +252 lines
  - `src/config/io.ts` — `hasJSON5Comments()` + warning in `logConfigOverwrite`
  - `src/config/mutate.ts` — `onCommitted` callback in `writeRootBoundJsonFile`
  - `src/config/io.parse.test.ts` — 10 focused tests
  - `src/config/mutate.test.ts` — 1 include-writer test
  - No new dependencies, no config/CLI/SDK/docs surface

- **Real behavior proof — root writer:**

target.title: fix(agents): add size limit to LSP message parser
target.body:
## Summary

**Problem**: The LSP message parser accepted unbounded `Content-Length`
values. A malicious or misbehaving LSP server could declare an arbitrarily
large `Content-Length` header, causing unbounded buffer growth and memory
exhaustion. Additionally, a very long decimal `Content-Length` (e.g., 400+
digits) causes `Number.parseInt` to return `Infinity`, which when used in
drain arithmetic leaves pending requests to time out indefinitely.

**Root cause**: Three gaps in the oversized-frame handling:
1. **Partial oversized frames left the session in drain limbo**: when an
   oversized body arrived across chunks, drain state stayed positive until
   all declared bytes arrived. If the server stopped sending, the session
   silently discarded all future LSP output while pending requests timed out.
2. **Post-violation frames were dispatched**: the parser's `continue` after
   draining an oversized frame parsed subsequent frames in the same buffer,
   dispatching responses that arrived after the violating header.
3. **Non-safe integer Content-Length** (`Infinity` from `parseInt` on very
   long decimals) was routed into the finite-drain branch instead of
   failing immediately, permanently suppressing all future LSP output.

**Solution (fail at header boundary)**: When `parseLspMessages` encounters a
fatal oversized or invalid `Content-Length`, it drains whatever body bytes
are available, returns `oversizeSeen: true`, and stops parsing (break,
not continue). `handleIncomingData` dispatches valid messages parsed before
the violating header, then calls `failLspSession` immediately. No cross-chunk
drain tracking remains on the session.

**What changed**: `src/agents/agent-bundle-lsp-runtime.ts`
- `parseLspMessages` now returns `oversizeSeen: boolean`. On oversized/
  invalid Content-Length, drains the body from the current buffer and
  returns early with `oversizeSeen: true` — no post-violation frames parsed.
- `handleIncomingData` checks `oversizeSeen`: dispatches valid messages
  first, then fails the session immediately. Removed all cross-chunk
  drain state (`oversizeDrainRemaining`, `oversizeDrainSeen`).
- `LspSession` type simplified — no drain tracking fields.

**Source**: +37 / -3 lines (source) +141 test lines.

**What did NOT change**: Valid message parsing, session lifecycle, tool
materialization — all unchanged for frames within the 10 MB limit.

## Real behavior proof

Behavior addressed: Three gaps closed —
1. Partial oversized frames now fail the session immediately instead of
   entering drain limbo (P1 fix).
2. Post-violation frames are never dispatched (P2 fix).
3. Non-safe integer Content-Length now signals a fatal protocol error.

Real environment tested: Linux 4.19.112, Node 22.19.0, pnpm 11.2.2

Exact steps or command run after this patch:
```bash
pnpm test src/agents/agent-bundle-lsp-runtime.test.ts
npx tsx evidence/pr-103046-proof.ts
```

Observed result after the fix: All 19 tests pass. L2 proof confirms all 5
parseLspMessages scenarios behave correctly.

After-fix evidence:

**A) Unit tests — 19/19 passing**
```text
 ✓ bundle LSP runtime (12)
 ✓ bundle LSP runtime > oversized Content-Length handling (7)
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  19 passed (19)
```

**B) L2 direct function proof — parseLspMessages with real data**
```text
✓ Case 1: Two valid frames → both parsed, oversizeSeen=false
✓ Case 2: Valid + oversized → valid returned, oversizeSeen=true, no post-violation
✓ Case 3: Partial oversized header → oversizeSeen=true
✓ Case 4: Non-safe integer CL → oversizeSeen=true
✓ Case 5: Valid + unsafe CL → valid returned, oversizeSeen=true
```

target.title: fix(agents): bound finished bash process session retention
target.body:
Closes #105625

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where long-running Gateways retaining many completed background bash/exec sessions would keep an unbounded finished-session map until TTL expiry, and session reset/delete would leave matching finished process records pollable until that TTL. That multiplies retained aggregate output and can grow gateway heap under bursty shell workloads.

## Why This Change Was Made

Keep completed `process poll` / `process log` aggregates (ClawSweeper rejected tail-only retention), but enforce deterministic finished-session count and total-aggregate-byte caps, and purge finished records whose `scopeKey` matches gateway session lifecycle cleanup keys. Shared scopes (for example chat bash) are not purged when an unrelated agent session resets.

## User Impact

Operators get bounded finished-process memory growth under heavy background exec traffic. Resetting or deleting a gateway session no longer leaves that session’s finished process records pollable until job TTL. Completed process log/poll behavior for still-retained sessions is unchanged.

## Evidence

Verification host: local macOS Darwin arm64 (live runtime harness on PR head + focused unit tests)

Live runtime (agent-solo, not Vitest) — see **Real behavior proof** for full redacted transcript:
- Production count cap 50: 51 completed background sessions → 50 retained; oldest unpollable; newest pollable with aggregate
- Production aggregate cap 2,000,000: two 1.2M sessions → only newest retained (1.2M total)
- Scoped reset: `clearSessionResetRuntimeState(["agent:main:main"])` → `finishedProcessSessionsCleared=1`; `chat:bash` retained

Focused tests (pass, supplemental):
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/bash-process-registry.test.ts` — 18 passed
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/auto-reply/reply/session-reset-cleanup.test.ts` — 7 passed
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/bash-tools.process.poll-timeout.test.ts` — 8 passed

Static:
- `pnpm exec oxfmt --check` on touched files — pass
- `git diff --check` — pass

Compatibility note for maintainers: this PR **accepts bounded early eviction** (CS recommended option). Completed process poll/log may disappear before TTL when budgets are exceeded; refine thresholds only if a longer delayed-poll contract is required.

## Real behavior proof

- Behavior addressed: Finished bash process sessions are hard-capped (50 sessions / 2,000,000 aggregate characters) so completed `process poll`/`process log` retention cannot grow unbounded until TTL; session reset/delete purges finished records only for matching lifecycle `scopeKey` values (shared scopes such as `chat:bash` stay).
- Compatibility stance (CS recommended option: **Prove and accept bounded eviction**): Contributor accepts the proposed internal limits. Under burst load, completed process poll/log records may become unavailable **before** the existing job TTL once the 50-session or 2,000,000-character budget is exceeded. Thresholds are intentionally product-owned if maintainers later want a longer delayed-poll window.
- Environment: local macOS Darwin arm64, Node v24.17.0, PR head `683f3c8a0b52964c0b532f57b33bd8aa34c82256` on branch `fix/105625-bash-finished-session-bounds`.
- Current-main contrast: On main, `pruneFinishedSessions` only deletes by TTL; `finishedSessions` has no count/byte cap; `clearSessionResetRuntimeState` does not touch finished process records, so scoped finished sessions remain pollable until TTL.
- Exact steps or command run after this patch (live runtime harness, **not** Vitest):
  1. Load production owner modules from this checkout: `src/agents/bash-process-registry.ts` and `src/auto-reply/reply/session-reset-cleanup.ts` via `tsx`.
  2. Complete 51 real short-lived `child_process` background sessions at production defaults → observe count cap.
  3. Complete 2 sessions with 1,200,000-char aggregates each at production 2,000,000 total cap → observe oldest eviction; newest remains pollable.
  4. Complete three scoped finished sessions (`agent:main:main`, `chat:bash`, `agent:other:main`) and call `clearSessionResetRuntimeState(["agent:main:main"])` (same helper gateway session reset/delete uses).
- Evidence after fix (redacted live transcript, 2026-07-13T05:21:16Z UTC):

```text
=== Live runtime proof: finished bash session retention bounds ===
host: darwin arm64
node: v24.17.0
branch_head: 683f3c8a0b52964c0b532f57b33bd8aa34c82256
method: real child_process echo sessions; production finished caps 50 / 2_000_000; not Vitest
redaction: no tokens/paths/IPs; synthetic ids only

--- A) count cap at production default (50 sessions) ---
completed_background_execs: 51
finished_retained_count: 50
count-00_pollable: false
count-50_pollable: true
count-50_aggregate: "out-50\n"
count_cap_ok: true

--- B) aggregate-char cap at production default (2_000_000) ---
sessions_completed: 2 x 1200000 chars
finished_retained_count: 1
retained_ids: bytes-new
total_aggregated_chars: 1200000
bytes-old_pollable: false
bytes-new_pollable: true
aggregate_cap_ok: true

--- C) clearSessionResetRuntimeState scoped finished-process purge ---
before_reset finished_count=3
before match=true shared=true other=true
reset_keys: ["agent:main:main"]
finishedProcessSessionsCleared: 1
after_reset finished_count=2
after match=false shared=true other=true
scoped_reset_ok: true

=== summary ===
count_cap_ok=true
aggregate_cap_ok=true
scoped_reset_ok=true
overall_ok=true
```

- Control check: Scope purge only matches exact `scopeKey` values; `chat:bash` and `agent:other:main` remain after resetting `agent:main:main`. Retained finished sessions keep full `aggregated` (not tail-only) for poll/log.
- Observed result after fix: Oldest finished sessions are evicted under production count and total-aggregate caps while retained entries stay pollable; session-reset runtime cleanup removes only matching-scope finished process records and reports `finishedProcessSessionsCleared`.
- Supplemental focused unit tests (still pass; not a substitute for the live harness above):
  - `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/bash-process-registry.test.ts` — 18 passed
  - `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/auto-reply/reply/session-reset-cleanup.test.ts` — 7 passed
- What was not tested: Full multi-tenant Control UI reset UX; sustained multi-hour production heap profile under mixed channel traffic (live harness exercises the same in-process registry and reset cleanup path the Gateway process uses).

## AI disclosure

This fix was authored with AI assistance (Grok). Implementation and proof follow ClawSweeper guidance on #105625 (count-plus-byte retention + scope-keyed cleanup; keep completed aggregates).

target.title: fix(slack): mark connected status degraded without bot identity
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When Slack auth.test fails at boot, or channels.slack.botToken is actually a user token (xoxp without bot_id), Socket Mode can still connect and previously published healthState: "healthy". Operators see a connected channel while mention detection is disabled and required-mention rooms fail closed — silent inbound loss.

## Why This Change Was Made

Transport liveness (connected: true) is still useful, but advertising healthy is wrong when bot identity is missing. The fix adds a degraded option to publishSlackConnectedStatus that sets healthState: degraded with the identity error.

## User Impact

- Channels with missing bot identity show "degraded" instead of "healthy"
- Operators can distinguish transport-up from fully operational
- App Home and resolution formatting are unchanged (regressions from earlier branch removed)

target.title: feat(control-ui): one-row automations toolbar, failing drill-down, visible row actions
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes #106043. The Automations page had five usability problems: the search box's focus ring rendered as an offset red rectangle (reads as a validation error), the `Automations | Run history` tabs occupied their own row above the toolbar, the Failing stat card was inert, a permanent "Scheduler: Enabled" chip card conveyed nothing actionable, and the most common per-job actions (Run now, Pause/Resume) were hidden behind the row's ⋯ menu.

## Why This Change Was Made

Daily-use feedback (maintainer): controls should be one row, the failing count should be a drill-down, scheduler state only matters when it is off, and pause/run-now belong on the row, not in a menu.

## User Impact

- **One toolbar row** for both list tabs: view pills + All/Active/Paused + search + filter popover, with refresh and New automation pinned right (`ui/src/pages/cron/view.ts`).
- **Quiet search focus**: cron search inputs replace the global offset outline with a subtle accent border tint (`ui/src/styles/cron.css`).
- **Failing card is a button**: clicking it opens Run history pre-filtered to `status=error` (`onShowFailingRuns` in `ui/src/pages/cron/cron-page.ts`).
- **Scheduler card removed**: a danger banner ("Scheduler disabled — The scheduler is stopped.") appears above the toolbar only while `cron.status.enabled` is false; stats grid is now 3 cards.
- **Visible row actions**: every row gets a Run now (▶) button and an enabled switch; the ⋯ menu keeps Run if due / Clone / Remove. The detail-header switch behavior is unchanged.
- **Run history filters** compacted into a single unlabeled row (search box, status/delivery dropdowns, sort select) used by both the Run history tab and the job detail history tab.
- i18n: removed the now-unused `cron.stats.scheduler` key; generated bundles pruned via `sync --write` (fallbacks=0, removal only — no new keys).

### Screenshots

| List (one-row toolbar, 3 stat cards, row actions) | Search focus | Failing → Run history |
| --- | --- | --- |
| ![list](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/steipete/openclaw-pr-assets/main/automations-redesign-2026-07/cron-list.png) | ![focus](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/steipete/openclaw-pr-assets/main/automations-redesign-2026-07/cron-search-focus.png) | ![failing](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/steipete/openclaw-pr-assets/main/automations-redesign-2026-07/cron-failing-history.png) |

## Evidence

- Mock-gateway Playwright screenshots above (dark, 1440×860) show the merged toolbar, the quiet focus ring, per-row ▶ + switch + ⋯, and the failing-card drill-down landing on Run history with the Error status filter applied.
- `pnpm test ui/src/pages/cron` (view + page tests) green on Blacksmith Testbox, including new coverage: failing-card click → activity tab + `cron.runs` called with `statuses: ["error"]`; inline row Run now / toggle wiring; scheduler banner only when `enabled: false`.
- `pnpm check:changed` green on Testbox.
- i18n: `sync --write` output `fallbacks=0` for all 20 locales; diff is exactly one deleted key per bundle.

### Follow-up in this PR

- Run-history rendering extracted to `ui/src/pages/cron/view-runs.ts` with a local leaf props contract (no module cycle; `view.ts` 2069 → 1803 lines).
- Autoreview (Codex, branch vs origin/main): clean, no actionable findings.

target.title: improve(ui): move Devices into Settings and redesign the device inventory
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The Devices page lived as a top-level workspace destination even though it is fleet/system configuration, and its layout had accumulated visual debt: three header buttons at three different heights, a redundant card title repeating the page title, a manual Refresh button on a page that already receives live presence events, plain-text rows with no visual anchor, and low-contrast "muted div" section separators that made pending approvals easy to miss.

## Why This Change Was Made

Devices is now a Settings page (System group, `/settings/devices`, with `/nodes` kept as a route alias so old links and the e2e path keep working). The inventory card was redesigned around a per-device identity tile: a form-factor icon (phone / browser / terminal / machine, gateway gets a server glyph) derived from the shared gateway client id/mode contract, with the connectivity dot anchored to the tile. Sections (Pending approval, Paired, Connected without pairing) use proper labels, header actions are two equal-height buttons (stale cleanup + pair), and the static card subtitle became a live "N of M connected · K awaiting approval" summary. The manual Refresh button is gone: the page already refreshes via presence/pairing gateway events plus a 30s poll, so the button was redundant surface.

## User Impact

Devices now lives where users expect fleet management (Settings → Devices, searchable from settings search), pending pairing requests stand out, every device row is scannable at a glance by device type and status, and there is no confusing manual Refresh button — the list stays current on its own. Old `/nodes` URLs continue to work.

target.title: fix(agents): reject with AbortError when tool execution is cancelled
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When a tool execution is cancelled via the agent's AbortSignal, onAbortSignal calls run.kill() to terminate the child process — but the outer Promise resolved normally with the process exit code. The agent manager was misled into believing the tool finished normally, causing it to keep executing steps with dead process output.

## Why This Change Was Made

The process exit handler always called resolve(buildExecForegroundResult(...)) regardless of whether the exit was caused by an abort signal. Additionally, the yield timer remained armed after abort, creating a race where it could resolve the promise with a "running" result before the killed-process exit handler could reject it.

## User Impact

- Cancel/stop during bash tool execution now correctly aborts the agent run
- Yield timer race is eliminated: abort atomically clears the timer + kills the process
- Backgrounded and yielded sessions remain unaffected

## Evidence

### Real Exec Tool Transcript (3/3 scenarios)

```
$ npx tsx proof/abort-exec-proof.ts

================================================================
 ABORT BEHAVIOR PROOF — REAL EXEC TOOL
 PID: 151586  Time: 2026-07-13 06:46:38
================================================================

--- 1. Normal execution completes normally ---
  Output: hello world

--- 2. Abort during execution -> rejects with AbortError ---
  ✅ REJECTED: DOMException - Tool execution was aborted

--- 3. Yield timer + abort -> rejects (timer cleared) ---
  ✅ REJECTED: DOMException - Tool execution was aborted

================================================================
 ABORT BEHAVIOR CONFIRMED — 3/3 scenarios
================================================================
```

### Unit Tests (35/35 passed)

```
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/bash-tools.test.ts --reporter=verbose
 ✓ suppresses onUpdate after abort signal fires
 ✓ rejects with AbortError when abort fires before yield window expires
 ✓ ... (33 other tests)

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  35 passed (35)
```

### Lint + Format
```
$ npx oxlint -c .oxlintrc.json src/agents/bash-tools.exec.ts
  No errors
$ npx oxfmt --check src/agents/bash-tools.exec.ts
  All matched files use the correct format
```

## What Changed

- src/agents/bash-tools.exec.ts: +13 lines (toolAborted flag + clear yieldTimer + AbortError rejection)
- src/agents/bash-tools.test.ts: +23 lines (regression test for yield timer race)

Fixes #105681

target.title: fix(cron): batch pending-media snapshot in session reaper to avoid O(SxT) loop
target.body:
#### What Problem This Solves

Close #105694

Fixes an O(S × T) CPU bottleneck in the cron session reaper that blocks the Node.js event loop on each timer tick. For every cron continuation row, `sweepCronRunSessions` called `hasPendingGeneratedMediaTaskForSessionKey`, which internally performs `listTaskRecords` — a full cloned-and-sorted snapshot of all task records plus in-process generated-media activity. With thousands of sessions, this synchronous work saturates the main thread and causes gateway timeout / WebSocket disconnection.

#### Why This Change Was Made

Instead of changing the per-row `hasPendingGeneratedMediaTaskForSessionKey` helper (still used by the single-invocation `cron-run-continuation-cleanup` path), this adds `buildPendingGeneratedMediaSessionKeySet` — a one-shot snapshot that collects all session keys with pending generated-media work by iterating the in-process activity map once and the full task registry once. The reaper then does O(1) `Set.has()` lookups inside the loop.

Key design decisions:
- Preserves the exact `requesterSessionKey` / `ownerKey` matching contract — no semantic change, only a scan-lifting optimization
- The snapshot is deliberately conservative: session keys that the reaper never visits may still be included, which is harmless
- ClawSweeper confirmed the shape: "one canonical bulk pending-generated-media session-key snapshot that combines active in-process work with nonterminal persisted requester and owner keys"

#### User Impact

No visible impact. The cron reaper produces identical pruning decisions with strictly less CPU time per sweep.

#### Evidence

- **Type check:** `tsgo` passes with no errors
- **Unit tests:**
  - `task-status-access.test.ts` — 10 tests pass (+6: `buildPendingGeneratedMediaSessionKeySet`)
  - `session-reaper.test.ts` — 20 tests pass (mock updated to use `buildPendingSet`)
  - `cron-run-continuation-cleanup.test.ts` — 5 tests pass (no regression)
- **Change scope:** 5 files, +131 −7 lines
  - `src/tasks/generated-media-task-activity.ts` — new `getAllActiveGeneratedMediaSessionKeys` export
  - `src/tasks/task-status-access.ts` — new `buildPendingGeneratedMediaSessionKeySet` helper
  - `src/cron/session-reaper.ts` — one snapshot call before the loop, `Set.has()` per row
  - `src/tasks/task-status-access.test.ts` — 6 new tests
  - `src/cron/session-reaper.test.ts` — mock updated for new function
  - No config, CLI, SDK, docs, or changelog surface affected
- **No new dependencies** — reuses existing `listTaskRecords`, `getActiveGeneratedMediaTasks`, `isTerminalTaskStatus`
- **Timing proof:** the `listTaskRecords` mock performs real clone+sort work on every call (matching production). Old and new paths are compared side-by-side at realistic scale with wall-clock measurement. The reaper was seeded with 500 cron continuation sessions and real `sweepCronRunSessions` verified the production code path.

```
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/cron/_proof-reaper-timing.test.ts --reporter verbose

 ✓ new path calls listTaskRecords exactly once at S=500 (old would call ~250x)

  [S=500, T=200]
  new path: buildPending + 500x Set.has → 0.76ms
  old path: 50x hasPending (sampled)   → 4.58ms
  old path projected (500x):           → 45.81ms
  speedup: 60.4x
  pending set: 83, new hits: 43, old hits (sampled): 30
  sweep result: swept=true, pruned=457

 ✓ new and old produce identical decisions on sampled rows

  correctness: 100/100 match, 0 mismatch
  pending set size: 165

 ✓ requesterSessionKey + ownerKey both captured, terminal excluded
   (video_generation processing → both keys in set; succeeded task excluded; chat excluded)

 ✓ scale: at S=1000, new path still sub-millisecond

  [S=1000, T=500] pending set: 105, loop hits: 210
  total (buildPending + 1000x Set.has): 0.77ms
  old path projected: ~192.7ms (500 continuation rows × clone+sort)

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  4 passed (4)
```

- **S=500, T=200:** 60.4x speedup (0.76ms new vs 45.81ms old projected)
- **S=1000, T=500:** ~250x speedup (0.77ms new vs ~192.7ms old projected)
- **Correctness:** 100/100 sampled rows produce identical old-vs-new decisions

target.title: fix(ui): catalog sessions select in place and continue from desktop-app sources
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

External Codex/Claude Code sessions surfaced in the Control UI sidebar ("session catalog") were effectively unusable:

1. **Wrongly view-only.** Almost every real Claude Code session on the gateway host showed "This external session source is view-only." Two causes:
   - Sessions driven through the Claude Code **desktop app** are recorded with `source: "claude-desktop"` during catalog discovery, and the anthropic plugin hard-required `source === "claude-cli"` for `canContinue`/continue — even though desktop sessions live in the same `~/.claude/projects` JSONL store (discovery drops desktop records without one) and `claude --resume --fork-session` continues them identically.
   - The chat pane showed the view-only banner whenever catalog metadata wasn't loaded yet, so even continuable sessions flashed "view-only" while loading.
2. **Selection lifted the session into the chats block.** Clicking a catalog row synthesized a phantom row in the regular sessions list labeled with the raw `catalog:claude:gateway%3Alocal:…` key (deep-link fallback in `resolveSessionNavigation`), and previously adopted sessions rendered twice — once in the catalog group and once in the regular list, jumping to the top on activity. Catalog rows also never showed a selected state.
3. **"Local Codex" / "Local Claude" noise.** Rows carried the gateway-host label as subtitle whenever a catalog had more than one host, adding no signal (the group header already names the source).

## Why This Change Was Made

Catalog sessions should feel like regular sessions that happen to run through Codex/Claude Code: click → selected in place, transcript shown, type → continue with streaming. All gating keys off the provider-reported per-session `canContinue`, so paired-node continuation (PR #105833) lights up in this UI automatically once it lands.

## User Impact

- Local Claude Code sessions (CLI **and** desktop app) are continuable from the web UI: type into the transcript view, the session is adopted, and the reply streams in as a normal session run.
- The view-only banner never flashes during load; after metadata loads, any non-continuable state (including a failed lookup) shows the explanatory banner instead of a silently disabled composer.
- Clicking a catalog session selects it in place. No phantom `catalog:…` row, no duplicate entry jumping to the top of the chats list. Adopted sessions render as full live session rows (run spinner, unread dot, pin/menu actions) inside their catalog group, bound immediately on adoption via a document-level `openclaw-session-catalog-continued` event instead of waiting for the next 30s catalog poll.
- Host subtitles only show a paired node's machine name; "Local Codex"/"Local Claude" subtitles are gone.
- Structure: sidebar catalog rendering moved to `app-sidebar-session-catalogs.ts`, the catalog metadata lookup to `catalog-key.ts`, and the Claude node-host commands to `session-catalog-node-commands.ts` (mirrors the codex plugin layout).

## Evidence

- Live verification against a scratch gateway built from this branch on a Mac with 40 real Claude Code sessions (mixed CLI/desktop):
  - Before: every session showed the view-only banner, and clicking created the phantom raw-key row.
  - After: `sessions.catalog.list` reports `canContinue: true` for desktop-source sessions, rows select in place with the active highlight, the composer is enabled, and sending ran the full flow — `sessions.catalog.continue` succeeded (adoption + history import), `chat.send` started a run through the claude-cli backend with `useResume=true` (gateway log), and the adopted row stayed inside the catalog group with the live run spinner and no duplicate in the chats block. (The CLI turn itself returned empty on that box because ~20 concurrent agent sessions were contending the local `claude` OAuth — standalone `claude -p` reproduced "Not logged in" in isolation; the resume path is the same shipped one used for `claude-cli`-source adoption.)
- Tests (all passing locally via `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs`):
  - `extensions/anthropic/session-catalog.test.ts` (8) — incl. new: desktop-source rows list as continuable and adopt with the same one-shot fork binding.
  - `ui/src/lib/sessions/navigation.test.ts` (12) — incl. new: no synthesized row for catalog session keys.
  - `ui/src/components/app-sidebar.test.ts` (54 with navigation shard) — incl. new: node-only host subtitles; in-place active highlight without a phantom chat row; adopted rows render once (as live rows) inside the catalog group; catalog-continued event binds the adopted key immediately.
  - `ui/src/e2e/codex-sessions.e2e.test.ts` + `ui/src/e2e/claude-sessions.e2e.test.ts` (3) — existing catalog flows still pass.
- `pnpm tsgo:ui` and `pnpm tsgo:extensions` pass locally.
- Autoreview (Codex `gpt-5.6-sol`, thinking xhigh, branch vs origin/main): one P2 finding (silent disabled composer after failed lookup) — fixed in 47591dfeaf9; rerun clean: "patch is correct", no actionable findings.

target.title: fix(telegram): catch unhandled rejections in webhook and ingress worker shutdown
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes two channel reliability bugs in the Telegram plugin where shutdown paths can produce unhandled promise rejections, which Node.js terminates the process for by default:

1. **Webhook shutdown**: if `bot.stop()` rejected during abort-triggered shutdown, the rejection was unhandled (`void shutdown()`), crashing the process.
2. **Ingress worker stop**: `stop()` was not idempotent, so calling it twice could post a second `stop` message and leak a second 15s terminate timer. If `worker.terminate()` rejected, the rejection was unhandled.

## Why This Change Was Made

- **Webhook**: catch shutdown errors in both the pre-aborted path and the abort listener, route them to `runtime.error`, and continue owned cleanup (transport close, status, diagnostics) in a `finally` block even if `bot.stop()` rejects.
- **Ingress worker**: guard `stop()` with a `stopped` flag for idempotency, catch `postMessage` errors for already-terminated workers, and catch `worker.terminate()` rejections.

## User Impact

No more unhandled rejection crashes during Telegram channel restart or shutdown.

## Evidence

### Tests

```bash
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/telegram/src/webhook.test.ts extensions/telegram/src/telegram-ingress-worker.test.ts -- --run
```

```
 Test Files  2 passed (2)
      Tests  38 passed (38)
```

### Negative Control Proof

**Webhook shutdown rejection handling**:

```bash
# Step 1: Revert to origin/main version
git checkout origin/main -- extensions/telegram/src/webhook.ts

# Step 2: Run test - Expected: FAIL with Unhandled Rejection
pnpm test extensions/telegram/src/webhook.test.ts -- --run -t "does not leak unhandled rejections when shutdown throws"
```

Result: ❌ **FAILED** - Unhandled Rejection: Error: bot stop failed

```bash
# Step 3: Restore fix
git checkout HEAD -- extensions/telegram/src/webhook.ts

# Step 4: Run test - Expected: PASS
pnpm test extensions/telegram/src/webhook.test.ts -- --run -t "does not leak unhandled rejections when shutdown throws"
```

Result: ✅ **PASSED** - 1 passed

**Ingress worker stop idempotency**:

```bash
# Step 1: Revert to origin/main version
git checkout origin/main -- extensions/telegram/src/telegram-ingress-worker.ts

# Step 2: Run test - Expected: FAIL
pnpm test extensions/telegram/src/telegram-ingress-worker.test.ts -- --run
```

Result: ❌ **FAILED** - AssertionError: expected Promise{…} to be Promise{…} (stop() not idempotent)

```bash

git checkout HEAD -- extensions/telegram/src/telegram-ingress-worker.ts

# Step 4: Run test - Expected: ALL PASS
pnpm test extensions/telegram/src/telegram-ingress-worker.test.ts -- --run
```

Result: ✅ **PASSED** - 2 passed

### Changes

- `extensions/telegram/src/webhook.ts`: catch shutdown errors in abort paths, log via `runtime.error`, continue cleanup in `finally`
- `extensions/telegram/src/webhook.test.ts`: new test for shutdown rejection handling
- `extensions/telegram/src/telegram-ingress-worker.ts`: idempotent `stop()` with shared stop promise, catch `postMessage` and `terminate` errors
- `extensions/telegram/src/telegram-ingress-worker.test.ts`: new tests for stop idempotency and terminate rejection handling

target.title: fix(agents): tighten grepSchema context/limit from Type.Number to Type.Integer
target.body:
## Summary

Fixes #105822

**Problem**: `grepSchema.context` and `grepSchema.limit` use `Type.Number`, accepting fractional values like `1.5` or `10.5` that are semantically invalid for context lines and match counts.

**Solution**: Change both fields to `Type.Integer` so schema validation rejects floats before reaching tool logic, and export `grepSchema` so the unit test validates against the production schema rather than a reconstructed copy. Importing `grepSchema` from the grep module is safe for a unit test because the schema is a plain TypeBox object with no runtime side effects. This follows the same pattern applied to the `ls` tool schema in PR #105827.

**What changed**: In `src/agents/sessions/tools/grep.ts` — `Type.Number` → `Type.Integer` for `context` and `limit`, `const grepSchema` → `export const grepSchema`. Rewrote `grep.limit-schema.test.ts` to import and validate against the production schema (4 scenarios). Removed standalone `_validate_grep.mjs` (redundant).

target.title: fix(nostr): keep profile imports as cancellable drafts
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Nostr profile imports could mutate config before the user reviewed relay data. While an import was pending, a same-field edit could be overwritten by the response. Cancel could close the form while a server-side merge still persisted.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Control UI now requests `autoMerge: false`, treats relay data as a draft, locks profile controls while importing, and aborts/invalidate imports on Cancel, disconnect, or form replacement. Late responses cannot update a hidden or newer form. Explicit **Save & Publish** remains the write path.

The existing HTTP contract is preserved: callers that explicitly send `autoMerge: true` retain server-side merge and persistence. Only the Control UI opts into draft mode.

## User Impact

Imported values fill the open form for review. Users can edit and explicitly publish them; Cancel cannot hide a persisted mutation, and stale responses cannot replace a newer form.

## Evidence

### Real Control UI + relay/browser proof

A standalone Chromium run drove the actual Control UI. Its import request was forwarded to the actual `createNostrProfileHttpHandler`, which queried the public relay `wss://nos.lol`. The server held the response until after the browser clicked Cancel; completion then produced no config write. The browser reopened the form and verified the local value remained, then exercised **Save & Publish** and observed the expected PUT and success UI.

Redacted output:

```json
{
  "browser": "Chromium",
  "relay": "wss://nos.lol",
  "pubkeyPrefix": "c938f0bd…",
  "relayPublish": "accepted",
  "pendingImport": { "browserRequest": { "autoMerge": false }, "fieldsDisabled": true },
  "cancel": {
    "clientAction": "Cancel",
    "serverCompletedAfterCancel": true,
    "serverPersistenceCalls": 0,
    "persistedProfile": { "name": "local" },
    "formValueAfterReopen": "local",
    "requestWasDelayedUntilCancel": true
  },

    "requestMethod": "PUT",
    "requestBody": { "name": "saved-draft" },

}
```

The run generated pending-import, after-Cancel/reopen, and after-Save screenshots plus a Chromium WebM recording under `.artifacts/control-ui-e2e/nostr-live-proof/`. target.title: fix(agents): strip runtime stream-boundary markers from user-visible text
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes #105113: runtime stream-boundary markers `[e~[` / `[e[` / `[1]` leak into user-visible channel deliveries.

When a tool-using assistant reply passes through the final channel delivery boundary, some streaming transports inject internal delimiters that the existing sanitizer pipeline does not strip — the markers reach the user as visible noise appended to the end of each message.

## Root Cause

The `sanitizeUserFacingText` pipeline strips `<tool_call>`, `<function_calls>`, `<system-reminder>`, MiniMax tool XML, legacy bracket blocks, and several other internal scaffolding patterns. However, it does **not** cover runtime stream-boundary markers (`[e~[`, `[e[`, `[1]`), which are functionally analogous to SSE `[DONE]`. These markers are injected at the transport layer and survive all existing strip stages.

## Fix

Add `stripRuntimeStreamMarkers` to the `sanitizeUserFacingText` pipeline. The function strips:

- `[e~[` / `[e[` — stream boundary marker (SSE `[DONE]` analog)
- Trailing `[1]` — compact marker after the boundary (only at end of text)
- Trailing lone `[` after whitespace — truncated marker fragment

Inline `[1]` references ("See [1] for details") are **preserved** — only a trailing `[1]` at the very end of the text is stripped.

## Files Changed

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `src/agents/embedded-agent-helpers/sanitize-user-facing-text.ts` | New `stripRuntimeStreamMarkers` function + call in pipeline |
| `src/agents/embedded-agent-helpers.sanitizeuserfacingtext.test.ts` | 3 new regression tests |

## Evidence

### Real behavior proof — OpenClaw main + PR patch, live Node.js import

```
$ node --import tsx/esm -e "import { sanitizeUserFacingText } from '...'; ..."

PASS: Stream boundary suffix  "Hello, how can I help?[e~[" → "Hello, how can I help?"
PASS: Variant without tilde   "Done.[e["                  → "Done."
PASS: Only marker             "[e~["                      → ""
PASS: Trailing compact marker "Done.[1]"                  → "Done."
PASS: Trailing lone bracket   "Partial reply ["           → "Partial reply"
PASS: Double-space bracket    "Done.  ["                  → "Done."
PASS: Inline reference preserved  "See [1] and [2]..."    → unchanged
PASS: Multi-line preserved    "Item [1]\nItem [2]"       → unchanged
PASS: Normal text unchanged   "Hello world"              → unchanged

✅ ALL 9 TESTS PASS
```

### Vitest

```
✓ strips runtime stream-boundary markers from user-visible text (#105113)
✓ strips compact runtime stream markers trailing the boundary (#105113)
✓ preserves inline [1] references that are not trailing stream markers
✓ removes trailing lone bracket fragments from truncated stream markers
```

target.title: fix(macos): prevent launch stalls with many Node versions
target.body:
Closes #106082

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where macOS app users with many Node versions could see the entire app stall for minutes immediately after launch while CLI PATH discovery scanned version-manager directories on the main thread.

## Why This Change Was Made

CLI status checks now cross an explicit Swift 6.2 `@concurrent` boundary before filesystem discovery and reuse one discovered PATH snapshot for every executable probe in that status pass. This keeps the launch-time main actor free without introducing a stale process-wide cache or changing CLI resolution behavior.

Release note: Fixed macOS app launch stalls when large Node version-manager directories make CLI discovery slow.

## User Impact

The macOS app remains responsive while it discovers CLI and Node version-manager paths during startup. Existing `nvm`, `fnm`, `asdf`, and Volta discovery continues to feed the same CLI status checks.

## Evidence

- Before: an observed process sample repeatedly held the main thread in `MacNodeModeCoordinator` -> `CLIInstaller.status()` -> `CommandResolver.versionedNodeBinPaths()` -> filesystem metadata syscalls; main-queue timers did not fire.
