target.title: fix(discord): hydrate missing reply references
target.body:
Closes #105862

## What Problem This Solves

A normal Discord reply can arrive with a valid `message_reference.message_id` but without a nested `referenced_message`. OpenClaw currently re-fetches the inbound reply, but if Discord REST also omits the nested payload, downstream reply context still cannot see the referenced message body.

## Why This Change Was Made

Preserve the existing inbound hydration first. When that successful REST result still lacks `referenced_message`, fetch the referenced message directly using the reference channel and message IDs and attach it through the existing Discord `Message` wrapper path.

The fallback remains limited to ordinary Discord replies. Known-deleted references and forwarded messages are unchanged, cross-channel references use their own channel ID, and API failures continue normal inbound delivery without logging referenced content.

## User Impact

Agents can receive the bounded quoted-message context for native Discord replies even when Discord omits the nested referenced payload from both the Gateway event and the hydrated reply response.

## Evidence

Final-head validation after rebasing onto current `main`:

- Candidate head: `3526d95eed`; based on `origin/main` at `9c94864746`.
- Production-path integration proof: the regression test starts with an ordinary reply whose Gateway-shaped payload omits `referenced_message`, verifies the two real REST routes (`/channels/c1/messages/m1` then `/channels/c1/messages/m0`), passes the hydrated Discord `Message` through `buildDiscordMessageProcessContext`, and asserts the actual inbound agent payload contains `ReplyToId === "m0"` and `ReplyToBody === "the directly fetched message"`.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/discord/src/monitor/message-handler.hydration.test.ts extensions/discord/src/monitor/message-handler.context.test.ts extensions/discord/src/monitor/message-utils.test.ts extensions/discord/src/monitor/message-handler.preflight.test.ts` under Node 24.15.0 — 4 files and 110 tests passed.
- `node_modules/.bin/oxfmt --check extensions/discord/src/monitor/message-handler.hydration.ts extensions/discord/src/monitor/message-handler.hydration.test.ts` — passed.
- `git diff --check origin/main...HEAD` — passed.
- `check:changed` passed its scoped conflict-marker, attribution, extension export, duplicate coverage, dependency pin, and formatting lanes. Its repository-wide Plugin SDK API baseline check reports the same hash mismatch on a clean detached `origin/main` worktree, so that drift is not introduced by this PR.

Discord documents that an absent `referenced_message` means its backend did not attempt to resolve it, and documents Get Channel Message as the supported endpoint for retrieving a specific readable message: https://docs.discord.com/developers/resources/message

### Proof boundary

This is deterministic, secretless integration proof through the actual Discord message-context builder, not a live Discord capture. This machine has no configured Discord account or token, so a redacted real Gateway/REST transcript cannot be truthfully produced locally. The test deliberately exercises the reported double-omission and verifies the recovered body at the final agent-context boundary rather than stopping at the REST wrapper.

target.title: fix(config): warn when JSON5 comments are lost on config write
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

OpenClaw parses `openclaw.json` using JSON5, which supports comments. However, when the configuration is modified, the system saves back using standard `JSON.stringify()`, which strips all user-authored comments.

**Issue**: #105683

## Why This Change Was Made

The root cause is in `src/config/io.ts` where config writes use `JSON.stringify()` which cannot preserve JSON5 comments.

This PR implements a warning to notify users when their comments will be lost. The warning is **not** gated on `skipOutputLogs` — comment stripping is a data-loss event that should always be surfaced, even for machine-parseable (`--json`) callers.

## User Impact

### Before
- Users add comments to `openclaw.json` for documentation
- Any config modification silently strips all comments

### After  
- Users receive a clear warning when writing config with JSON5 comments
- The warning fires regardless of output mode (including `--json` / `skipOutputLogs`)
- The warning intelligently excludes false positives (URLs in strings)

target.title: feat(nodes): continue Claude catalog sessions on paired nodes via streaming CLI agent runs
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Claude Code catalog sessions on paired nodes were view-only: `continueClaudeSession` rejected any `hostId` other than `gateway:local`, so a session whose files live on another machine could be browsed but never continued. Closes #105529.

## Why This Change Was Made

Continuing a Claude session must run the real `claude` CLI on the machine that owns the session files (its `~/.claude`, its auth) — OpenClaw stays a frontend and never substitutes its own inference. This PR ships the full TS stack for that, opt-in and approval-gated end to end:

- **Streaming node invoke (additive transport)**: new `node.invoke.progress` events (`{invokeId, nodeId, seq, chunk}`) with strict seq ordering, bounded out-of-order buffering, idle-timeout reset on progress, hard-cap timeout, and `node.invoke.cancel`. Legacy single-result invokes stay byte-identical (cancel frames are gated to streaming invokes). Progress handlers are node-scoped and bind invokeId to the owning node's connection — no cross-node injection.
- **Node command `agent.cli.claude.run.v1`** (TS node host): advertised only when the node-local config `nodeHost.agentRuns.claude.enabled` is true AND the `claude` binary resolves on the node — the gateway can never force it on. Requests are validated against a strict Claude flag allowlist (`bypassPermissions` rejected in both arg forms), env passthrough is allowlisted, cwd must exist, and every run flows through the existing `system.run` exec-approval policy with the exact validated argv. Output is capped (200KB, 16KB chunks with backpressure), stderr tailed, process tree SIGKILLed on cancel/timeout, and the system prompt is materialized in a node-local 0600 temp file that is always cleaned up.
- **cli-runner placement branch**: sessions with `execHost === "node"` run one-shot `claude -p` turns through the streaming invoke, feeding the same JSONL parser as local runs (session-id capture, fork markers, tool events unchanged). Warm stdio, gateway-loopback MCP, skills dirs, reseed-from-transcript, and attachments are cleanly disabled for node runs (rejected or omitted, double-enforced by the node-side allowlist); local runs are byte-identical.
- **Catalog wiring**: node rows become continuable when the node advertises the run command AND the gateway's node command policy permits it (deny-wins, enforced at projection, continue, and invoke time). Adoption re-resolves the record from the node itself (client-supplied paths never trusted), imports bounded history via the existing read command, and binds the session with `execNode`/`execCwd` through the trusted creation seam. First-turn `--fork-session` semantics identical to local adoption.

Mac-app (Swift) nodes simply never advertise the command and remain view-only until the app ships it.

## User Impact

With a headless node host opted in (`nodeHost.agentRuns.claude.enabled: true` + `claude` installed), Claude Code sessions on that machine appear in the session catalog and can be continued like native sessions: each turn runs on the node with the node's Claude auth and settings, streams output live, and respects the node's exec approval policy. Nothing changes for nodes that do not opt in; existing node/gateway deployments see zero wire-format changes.

## Evidence

- Focused matrix green post-rebase (8 Vitest shards): node-registry transport ordering/idle/disconnect, node-host argv-validation/approval/caps/cancel, cli-runner placement/JSONL-across-chunks/fork/deadline-during-approval, config contract, plugin runtime projection, catalog adoption/rejection paths.
- Codex-side validation on Linux Testbox: 12 test files (574 executions), `check:changed` (12m21s), `pnpm build` — all green pre-review.
- Three independent deep reviews (transport, cli-runner placement, catalog/config/plugin seams): all SOLID, zero P1s. The one P2 (hard-timeout previously emitted `node.invoke.cancel` for legacy invokes too) is fixed — cancel frames now gate on the streaming contract.
- Per-commit autoreview (gpt-5.6-sol xhigh) surfaced five findings, all fixed with regression tests: buffered progress no longer drains after cancellation; duplicate buffered seq frames no longer reset the idle deadline; node runs now carry the gateway's native tool policy (`--tools` + MCP deny projected; `--allowedTools` auto-approval still never crosses the node boundary); fresh node CLI sessions reseed conversation history from the gateway-side transcript; and a truncated node stream that lost the terminal result line now fails the turn instead of passing as a clean exit.
- SDK gates: `plugin-sdk:api:check` and `plugin-sdk:surface:check` green (surface budget +1 for `resolveChildProcessInvocation`, now public via the `process-runtime` wildcard — needed by the node host for Windows shim-correct spawns).
- tsgo core + UI lanes green; oxlint/oxfmt/`git diff --check` clean.

Known follow-ups (deliberate v1 scope, in the tracking issue): Mac-app Swift command, warm stdio on nodes, gateway-loopback MCP over node transport, Codex app-server on nodes, approval-request withdrawal when a run aborts mid-wait, FailoverError classification for node disconnects.

target.title: fix(security): validate port range in suspicious-network scanner rule
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The `suspicious-network` scanner rule uses `Number.parseInt` on a regex capture group to extract a port number, then checks `STANDARD_PORTS.has(port)`. If `parseInt` returns `NaN` (e.g. from unexpected regex match content), `STANDARD_PORTS.has(NaN)` returns `false`, so the finding is reported with a `NaN` port — a false positive with a meaningless value. Negative ports and values exceeding 65535 are also not valid TCP/UDP ports but would bypass the standard-port allowlist.

## Why This Change Was Made

Add `Number.isFinite(port) && port >= 0 && port <= 65535` before the `STANDARD_PORTS` lookup so that only valid, in-range port numbers can trigger the standard-port skip. Out-of-range or non-numeric values are now reported as findings with their original evidence, which is more useful than a NaN port number.

## User Impact

Minor — eliminates false-positive scanner findings with NaN port numbers. No change to legitimate findings.

## Evidence

target.title: fix(gateway): distinguish ENOENT from corrupt JSON in readManagedImageRecord
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`readManagedImageRecord` used a bare `catch` that returned `null` for all errors, including `SyntaxError` from truncated or corrupt JSON metadata. This made it impossible to distinguish "attachment was never created" (ENOENT) from "attachment metadata was corrupted" (e.g. by a crash during write). Corrupted records were silently treated as non-existent, causing user-uploaded images to disappear without any diagnostic signal.

## Why This Change Was Made

Return `null` only for `ENOENT` (file not found) and propagate other errors (like `SyntaxError` from invalid JSON) so callers can respond appropriately. The HTTP handler now catches propagated errors and returns a 500 status instead of a misleading 404, making it possible to detect and diagnose metadata corruption.

## User Impact

Corrupted image metadata now results in a 500 error (visible in gateway logs) instead of silently returning 404 and making the attachment vanish. Valid "not found" scenarios continue to return 404 as before.

target.title: fix(infra): return undefined for bigint exceeding MAX_SAFE_INTEGER in normalizeSqliteNumber
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`normalizeSqliteNumber` converts SQLite `bigint` columns to JavaScript `number` via `Number(value)`. For bigint values exceeding `Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER` (2^53-1), `Number()` silently loses low-bit precision (e.g. `Number(9007199254740993n)` → `9007199254740992`). For extremely large values, it returns `Infinity`, which can cause downstream threshold comparisons to produce incorrect results (e.g. expiration timestamps, byte counts).

## Why This Change Was Made

Return `undefined` when a bigint value exceeds the safe integer range, instead of silently truncating or producing `Infinity`. This lets callers handle the out-of-range case explicitly rather than acting on a corrupted numeric value.

## User Impact

If a SQLite bigint column ever contains a value beyond 2^53-1, the function now returns `undefined` instead of a silently-wrong number. In practice, SQLite rowids and counts rarely exceed this range, so the change is defensive rather than fixing a current user-facing bug.

## Evidence

```text
$ npx vitest run src/infra/sqlite-number.test.ts
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  11 passed (11)
```

New test cases:
- `returns undefined for bigint exceeding MAX_SAFE_INTEGER`
- `returns undefined for bigint below -MAX_SAFE_INTEGER`

target.title: fix(sessions): keep dirty transcript search from blocking the gateway
target.body:
Closes #105735

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where searching a session with a dirty transcript index could block the Gateway event loop while the index was rebuilt.

The rebuild began synchronously inside `searchSessionTranscripts`. Its initial SQLite work, transcript parsing, and index writes ran before the async function reached its first yield. Deferring that same work with `setImmediate` would only move the stall to the next event-loop turn.

## Why This Change Was Made

Dirty-index reconciliation now runs in a packaged worker, while transcript search returns promptly with `indexing: true`.

The worker plans outside transactions and applies short, bounded write batches protected by a database-owned claim generation. Transcript mutations invalidate an active claim, and reconciliation performs a final authoritative revision check before clearing the dirty state.

A process-wide single-slot queue bounds worker concurrency. Planning and write progress have separate watchdogs; failure or timeout releases the slot for a later retry. There is no large synchronous fallback when worker startup fails.

Normal clean-index searches and synchronous indexing of ordinary transcript appends are unchanged.

## User Impact

Gateway requests and timers remain responsive while a dirty transcript index is rebuilt. Once reconciliation finishes, transcript search returns the correctly rebuilt index.

Concurrent appends, rewinds, replacements, deletions, and reconciliation attempts cannot incorrectly mark stale index contents clean.

## Evidence

Focused regression and packaging tests:

```text
OPENCLAW_VITEST_MAX_WORKERS=1 node scripts/run-vitest.mjs \
  src/config/sessions/session-transcript-search.test.ts \
  src/infra/tsdown-config.test.ts \
  --reporter=verbose \
  --maxWorkers=1
```

Result: 38 tests passed.

The regression coverage proves:

- Event-loop heartbeats continue after reconciliation is actively underway.
- Search eventually returns the rebuilt transcript index.
- Two database connections cannot concurrently own the same rebuild.
- Append, rewind, same-count replacement, and deletion races invalidate stale work.
- Large unrelated FTS contents do not cause long write-lock scans.
- Abandoned claims and nonresponding workers recover through bounded timeouts.
- Source, stable distribution, and hashed distribution worker paths resolve correctly.

Additional validation:

- `pnpm build` passed and emitted the transcript reconciliation worker.
- `pnpm check` passed.
- Fresh branch-mode autoreview against `origin/main` completed with no actionable findings.

## Suggested Review Order

1. `src/config/sessions/session-transcript-reconcile.ts` — claim lifecycle, planning, bounded writes, and final authoritative check.
2. `src/config/sessions/session-transcript-search.ts` — worker queue, deduplication, watchdogs, and search behavior.
3. `src/config/sessions/session-transcript-index.ts` — transcript mutations invalidating active claims.
4. `src/config/sessions/session-transcript-search.test.ts` — responsiveness, concurrency, race, and recovery proof.
5. `src/config/sessions/session-transcript-reconcile.worker.ts` — worker entry and message settlement.
6. `tsdown.config.ts`, `scripts/release-check.ts`, and `src/infra/tsdown-config.test.ts` — packaging and release inventory.

## AI Assistance

This change was developed with Codex assistance. The implementation was reviewed against repository guidance, validated with focused regression tests plus build/check gates, and passed a fresh branch-mode autoreview.

## Real behavior proof

Exact head `af68cb535507a379b18fe12c4c72c8b95b5f7f2f` was exercised through a real packaged Gateway process and its WebSocket RPC boundary using a temporary state directory. The setup used 100,000 synthetic transcript message events, then removed only the derived FTS and index-state rows to reproduce a dirty upgrade/rebuild state. No model or provider call was involved.

```text
{"event":"gateway_turn","turn":1,"healthRpcMs":194,"healthResponded":true,"searchRpcMs":351,"indexing":true,"resultCount":0}
```

target.body:
## Summary

Fixes #105846

**Problem**: Real-time relay audio frames use unpadded base64 encoding, but the `isValidBase64` guard from `chat-attachments.ts` requires length % 4 === 0, rejecting valid unpadded audio frames. This breaks relay clients sending standard unpadded base64.

**Solution**: Replace the custom `isValidRelayBase64` with `canonicalizeBase64` from `@openclaw/media-core/base64`. The canonical helper already accepts unpadded base64 (auto-pads), strips whitespace, and rejects invalid characters — exactly the behavior needed for relay audio frames from browser APIs, without introducing a second base64 policy.

**What changed**: In `src/gateway/talk-realtime-relay.ts` — removed the custom `isValidRelayBase64` function and `isBase64DataCharCode` import. Added `canonicalizeBase64` import from `@openclaw/media-core/base64`. Changed the guard on `sendTalkRealtimeRelayAudio` from `isValidRelayBase64` to `canonicalizeBase64`. No changes to `chat-attachments.ts` (the exports belong to PR #105837).

**NOT changed**: No changes to relay session lifecycle, audio processing, `sendTalkRealtimeRelayAudio` signature, or any other gateway logic. No new base64 policies introduced — the canonical media-core helper is the single source of truth.

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior addressed**: Canonical base64 validation for real-time relay audio frames using `canonicalizeBase64` from `@openclaw/media-core/base64` — accepts unpadded base64, strips whitespace, rejects invalid input.
**Real environment tested**: Linux x64, Node.js 25.9.0, OpenClaw `main@HEAD` with this patch applied.
**Exact steps or command run after this patch**: `node --import tsx/esm -e "..."` (standalone validation against production `canonicalizeBase64`)
**After-fix evidence**: 5/5 validation scenarios passed with whitespace handling (see terminal output below).
**Observed result after the fix**: Valid padded base64 returns canonical form (defined), valid unpadded base64 auto-padded to canonical form (defined) — key behavior for relay audio, empty string rejected (undefined), invalid characters rejected (undefined), padding-in-middle rejected (undefined), whitespace stripped.
**What was not tested**: End-to-end relay session with real audio provider (requires full Gateway runtime); the canonical helper is already tested via `packages/media-core/src/base64.test.ts` (7 tests pass).

## Tests and validation

```
$ node --import tsx/esm -e "..."

=== Real behavior proof: canonicalizeBase64 for relay audio ===
(Replaces custom isValidRelayBase64 with canonical media-core helper)

  PASS canonicalizeBase64("dGVzdA==") → "dGVzdA==" (expected defined)
  PASS canonicalizeBase64("dGVzdA") → "dGVzdA==" (expected defined)
  PASS canonicalizeBase64("") → undefined (expected undefined)
  PASS canonicalizeBase64("invalid!") → undefined (expected undefined)
  PASS canonicalizeBase64("abc=defg") → undefined (expected undefined)

Whitespace tolerance (relay frames may have trailing newlines):
  canonicalizeBase64("dGVzdA== ") → "dGVzdA=="
  canonicalizeBase64("SGV s bG8= ") → "SGVsbG8="

5/5 passed, whitespace OK
```

| Behavior | `isValidRelayBase64` (removed) | `canonicalizeBase64` (new) |
|----------|-------------------------------|---------------------------|
| Padded `"dGVzdA=="` | ✅ accept | ✅ accept |
| Unpadded `"dGVzdA"` | ✅ accept | ✅ accept (auto-pads) |
| Empty `""` | ❌ reject | ❌ reject (undefined) |
| Invalid chars `"invalid!"` | ❌ reject | ❌ reject (undefined) |
| Padding mid `"abc=defg"` | ❌ reject | ❌ reject (undefined) |
| Whitespace tolerance | ❌ not handled | ✅ stripped |

Existing media-core tests pass, and new focused relay guard tests exercise the actual `sendTalkRealtimeRelayAudio` entry point:


All 16 tests pass across 4 gateway shards, proving the `canonicalizeBase64` guard works correctly at the relay entry point.

target.title: fix(discord): bound stalled probe response reads
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Discord probe checks could hang after the `getMe` request returned response headers but the JSON response body stopped producing data.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Discord probe now reads the successful `getMe` JSON body through the bounded response reader with the existing 16 MiB cap and a per-chunk timeout tied to the probe timeout. Existing non-OK handling, malformed JSON wording, and probe result flow are preserved.

## User Impact

Discord configuration checks now fail quickly on a stalled probe body instead of leaving users waiting on an unbounded read.

## Evidence

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/discord/src/probe.intents.test.ts` (10 tests passed)
- `git diff --check upstream/main..HEAD`
- Claude autoreview: clean, no accepted/actionable findings
### Exact-head controlled-network proof

Exact head: `f6de53aba381701e59a0554a8ffe80c9c5b76457`.

Command:

```text
PROOF_HEAD=f6de53aba381701e59a0554a8ffe80c9c5b76457 HTTP_PROXY= HTTPS_PROXY= http_proxy= https_proxy= ALL_PROXY= all_proxy= NO_PROXY=127.0.0.1,localhost no_proxy=127.0.0.1,localhost timeout 30s node --import tsx scratchpad/discord-probe-current-head-proof.mts
```

The temporary harness was removed after the run. It called production `probeDiscord()`, using the existing fetch seam only to route Discord API URLs to a loopback `node:http` server. The underlying client was real Node fetch; no mocked `Response`, Discord traffic, or credentials were used.

Redacted transcript:

```text
proof: exact-head=f6de53aba381701e59a0554a8ffe80c9c5b76457 production Discord probe
probe: mode=normal ok=true error=null bot=bot-1 elapsed=42ms
[fetch-timeout] fetch timeout after 120ms operation=fetchWithTimeout
probe: mode=header-stall ok=false error=request timed out elapsed=196ms
server: response closed mode=header-stall writableEnded=false
probe: mode=body-stall ok=false error=discord.probe.getMe: JSON response stalled after 120ms elapsed=129ms
server: response closed mode=body-stall writableEnded=false
probe: mode=slow-trickle ok=true error=null bot=bot-1 elapsed=1450ms
probe: mode=normal ok=true error=null bot=bot-1 elapsed=3ms
proof: current-head real HTTP assertions passed
```

Observed: a request stalled before headers aborts and closes its socket; a response that sends headers and a partial JSON body and then stops aborts through the production probe reader and closes its socket; a later normal probe succeeds. All assertions passed; exit 0.

Known limits: this is controlled local HTTP transport proof, not live Discord. Current head enforces an idle/per-chunk timeout, not a total response deadline: a body sending one chunk every 40 ms completed after 1450 ms with `timeoutMs=120`. This proof therefore establishes cleanup for a body that stops producing data and does not claim protection from an indefinitely slow trickle. The exact command referenced a temporary uncommitted harness that has been removed.

target.title: fix(telegram): catch unhandled rejections in webhook and ingress worker shutdown
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes two channel reliability bugs in the Telegram plugin where shutdown paths can produce unhandled promise rejections, which Node.js terminates the process for by default:

1. **Webhook shutdown**: if `bot.stop()` rejected during abort-triggered shutdown, the rejection was unhandled (`void shutdown()`), crashing the process.
2. **Ingress worker stop**: `stop()` was not idempotent, so calling it twice could post a second `stop` message and leak a second 15s terminate timer. If `worker.terminate()` rejected, the rejection was unhandled.

## Why This Change Was Made

- **Webhook**: catch shutdown errors in both the pre-aborted path and the abort listener, route them to `runtime.error`, and continue owned cleanup (transport close, status, diagnostics) in a `finally` block even if `bot.stop()` rejects.
- **Ingress worker**: guard `stop()` with a `stopped` flag for idempotency, catch `postMessage` errors for already-terminated workers, and catch `worker.terminate()` rejections.

## User Impact

No more unhandled rejection crashes during Telegram channel restart or shutdown.

## Evidence

### Tests

```bash
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/telegram/src/webhook.test.ts extensions/telegram/src/telegram-ingress-worker.test.ts -- --run
```

```

```

### Negative Control Proof

```bash
# Step 2: Run test - Expected: FAIL with Unhandled Rejection

```

**Ingress worker stop idempotency**:

```bash
# Step 4: Run test - Expected: ALL PASS

```

Result: ✅ **PASSED** - 2 passed

- `extensions/telegram/src/webhook.ts`: catch shutdown errors in abort paths, log via `runtime.error`, continue cleanup in `finally`
- `extensions/telegram/src/webhook.test.ts`: new test for shutdown rejection handling
- `extensions/telegram/src/telegram-ingress-worker.ts`: idempotent `stop()` with shared stop promise, catch `postMessage` and `terminate` errors

target.title: fix(commitments): avoid quadratic heartbeat session discovery
target.body:
Related: #105787

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes heartbeat commitment fan-out latency when many due commitments belong to one session. The existing path loads and expires the JSON store while holding the queue/file lock, releases that lock, then scans the returned in-memory records. For every qualifying due record it rescans the complete store to count recent sent commitments. The quadratic scan is outside the lock, but it delays heartbeat processing and increases heartbeat latency. Reported isolated medians were approximately 191 ms at 1,000, 847 ms at 2,000, and 2.28 s at 4,000 records.

## Why This Change Was Made

The commitments store now builds the rolling 24-hour sent-count map once per agent and reuses it for due-session discovery and single-session due selection. Due-window, snooze, expiry, daily-cap, ordering, limit, agent-scope, queue, and cross-process file-lock behavior remain on the existing path.

This is intentionally an interim JSON-store fix. OpenClaw's shared SQLite state schema already contains a commitments table and indexes, but making it canonical requires a separate JSON-to-SQLite migration/doctor contract and broader persistence coverage. That migration remains a follow-up rather than expanding this focused latency fix.

## User Impact

Heartbeat commitment discovery changes from repeated full-store counting to one aggregation pass plus the existing due-record scan. Large concentrated sessions therefore scale linearly with store size instead of quadratically, without changing which sessions are eligible for delivery.

## Evidence

- Store correctness coverage includes due windows, snoozes, rolling daily caps, agent scope, deterministic session-key ordering, expiry, and concurrent file-store updates.
- The concentrated-session regression uses 8,000 due records in one session and a production-like `limit: 10`, so the base implementation repeatedly rescans the store while the fixed implementation reuses one count map.

Each run seeded 16,000 pending due commitments plus one recent sent commitment, all concentrated in one Telegram session, then invoked the production Gateway `wake` RPC once. The Gateway scheduler, heartbeat runner, JSON store, due-session selector, Telegram plugin dispatch, and delivery/status updates were real. target.title: fix(gmail): stop watcher when OAuth renewal is invalid
target.body:
Closes #96088

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users running the Gmail watcher could keep a `gog gmail watch serve` process alive after Gmail watch renewal failed with terminal OAuth errors such as `invalid_grant` or revoked credentials. That made the watcher look live even though Gmail watch coverage could no longer be renewed.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Gmail watcher now classifies `gog watch start` failures as retryable or terminal. Retryable watch-start failures keep the existing serve-and-renew behavior, while terminal OAuth failures refuse initial startup or stop the active watcher with a clear re-authentication reason. The same classification is shared by the Gateway auto-start watcher and the foreground `openclaw webhooks gmail run` path.

## User Impact

Operators now get a stopped or non-started Gmail watcher when credentials need re-authentication instead of a stale listener that appears healthy. Transient Gmail watch-start failures still keep the previous retry path.

## Evidence

target.title: fix: active-memory recalls from all agents serialize on one shared lane
target.body:
Related: #72015 (this addresses the recall-lane serialization portion of that report; the QMD boot-initialization portion is separate)

> This PR is AI-assisted: the analysis, patch, and test update were written with an AI coding agent. A human operator reviewed the change and validated it against a live deployment.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where, on multi-agent gateways, memory recall runs from different agents queue behind each other. The active-memory recall subagent always enqueues on the single shared `active-memory` lane, and command lanes default to `maxConcurrent: 1`, so every agent's recall serializes globally. The lane wait burns the recall's turn-scoped time budget, so under concurrent traffic (several agents active at once, or a burst of session resets) recalls run late, time out, or are skipped, and users see replies without memory context.

## Why This Change Was Made

Key the recall lane by agent id (`active-memory:<agentId>`) so recalls serialize per agent instead of across the whole gateway. Lanes are created lazily on first use, so no lane registration change is needed. `agentId` is already a required parameter at the enqueue site. Single-agent deployments behave exactly as before (one agent, one lane).

## User Impact

On multi-agent gateways, one agent's memory recall no longer delays every other agent's. Recall latency under concurrent load drops and fewer recall time budgets are exhausted while queued, so memory injection lands more reliably. No configuration change; single-agent installs see no behavioral difference.

## Evidence

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.extension-active-memory.config.ts extensions/active-memory/index.test.ts` passes 154/154, including the updated lane assertion (agent `main` now enqueues on `active-memory:main`).
- Live observation motivating the fix: on a multi-agent gateway, recall queue-wait clusters coincided with degraded or skipped memory injection whenever several agents were active in the same window; single-agent sessions on the same build were unaffected.
- Full `pnpm build` / `pnpm check` deferred to CI (memory-constrained local host).



## Runtime evidence (real behavior, redacted)

The submitting gateway has been running this change backported onto v2026.6.10 since 2026-07-05, on a small multi-agent fleet. The excerpt below (agent names and the room id redacted, timestamps UTC, lines otherwise verbatim) shows two agents' Active Memory recall sub-runs executing concurrently in the same group room:

```
07:49:22.780Z active-memory: agent=agent-a session=agent:agent-a:slack:group:<room> start timeoutMs=15000
07:49:24.458Z active-memory: agent=agent-b session=agent:agent-b:slack:group:<room> start timeoutMs=15000
07:49:28.310Z active-memory: agent=agent-a session=agent:agent-a:slack:group:<room> done status=ok elapsedMs=5530
07:49:42.790Z active-memory: agent=agent-b session=agent:agent-b:slack:group:<room> done status=ok elapsedMs=18332
```

Why this demonstrates per-agent lanes rather than enqueue timing: `elapsedMs` equals the wall-clock delta between each start/done pair (agent-a 22.780 to 28.310 is 5530 ms; agent-b 24.458 to 42.790 is 18332 ms), so the `start` line marks actual execution start, not queue admission. agent-b began executing 3.9 s into agent-a's 5.5 s run. Under the pre-patch shared lane (`maxConcurrent: 1`) the second recall cannot start before the first finishes; overlapping execution is only possible with distinct lanes. Lane names are not printed at info level, so the proof is behavioral rather than a lane-key string.

Stability over the most recent two days of logs on the final-head behavior: 23 recall sub-runs across 3 active agents, 10 `status=ok`, 13 `status=no_relevant_memory`, zero timeouts, zero errors, elapsed 1.3 to 19.6 s (average 8.1 s), no queue backlog or gateway instability observed.

On the concurrency boundary question raised in review: that decision belongs to the maintainers. As one data point, this fleet has run one slot per agent for a week with several concurrently active agents and no saturation; an aggregate cap on top of agent-keyed lanes would also compose fine with this patch if preferred.

## What Problem This Solves

Zalouser maintained a private copy of offset-aware text range splitting even though outbound text and Markdown chunking belong to the shared `plugin-sdk/text-chunking` surface. That duplicated paragraph/newline/whitespace policy and made native Zalo style offsets harder to keep aligned with shared chunking behavior.

## Why This Change Was Made

Adds `chunkTextRanges` to markdown-core, exports it through `openclaw/plugin-sdk/text-chunking`, and migrates Zalouser while keeping only its native style slicing locally. The helper preserves every input code unit and separator, prefers paragraph/newline/whitespace boundaries when requested, and keeps surrogate pairs intact. Matrix HTML rendering and QQBot's stateful table/fence repair are intentionally unchanged because they remain channel-specific.

## User Impact

target.title: fix: keep yielded parent runs deferred until subagents settle
target.body:
## Summary

This change promotes yielded-parent semantics into a shared parent lifecycle classifier and routes the affected cron, subagent-registry, and Discord/source-message paths through that state instead of letting each consumer infer completion from terminal-shaped model-attempt events, missing final text, or abort-shaped control flow.

The shipped behavior is:

- yielded parent + active descendants is treated as waiting/deferred, not ordinary completion;
- yielded parent + no descendant is treated as diagnostic error;
- cron delivery waits for a real final outcome instead of counting the yielded attempt as `ok / not-delivered`;
- Discord/source-message progress remains parent-owned while the yielded parent is waiting;
- descendant settlement wakes/reconciles yielded parents through the existing continuation paths.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where parent-agent runs that spawned child sessions/subagents and then called `sessions_yield` could look finished before the parent task actually completed.

The most visible failures were:

- isolated cron `agentTurn` jobs with valid delivery targets could finish as `ok / not-delivered` because the yielded parent had no final payload yet;
- Discord source-message lifecycle could clear parent progress/done indicators while child work was still active or while the parent was waiting to reconcile final output;
- run history/status surfaces made yielded parent work look like delivery failure, ordinary success with no output, or completed source-message work instead of a paused/resumable parent lifecycle.

`session_yield` is supposed to end the current model turn, not the parent task. This PR makes that distinction explicit for the affected runtime consumers.

## User Impact / Intended Outcome

Operators and developers can now rely on `sessions_yield` after spawning child/subagent work without the parent run being misrepresented as complete at the cron or Discord lifecycle boundary.

Practically:

- autonomous development crons stop inflating misleading `ok / not-delivered` results for intentionally yielded runs;
- cron history exposes a distinct `deferred` state for yielded parent handoff;
- Discord progress no longer marks the parent source message done just because the parent yielded while children continue;
- yielded parent runs are resumed/reconciled when descendant work settles;
- debugging points to the parent/child lifecycle state instead of falsely implying delivery target resolution failed.

## Linked Context

- #95535 — `sessions_yield` isolated cron resumption/delivery gap.
- #92369 — subagent orchestration in isolated cron sessions needs reliable spawn/wait/aggregate semantics.
- #92116 — `sessions_yield` completion delivered as passive context can break orchestration loops.
- #86537 — subagent terminal reconciliation can expire suspended final delivery.
- #86538 — session write-lock timeouts can block subagent delivery lanes.
- #95833 — subagent abort-settle/session-lock failure can break session continuation.
- #92460 — isolated cron completion delivery gap around final controller return.
- #95604 — Discord subagent progress visibility.
- #94153 — durable queued subagent completion announcements.
- #95847 — requester-consumed descendant completion accounting.

## What Changes

### Shared parent lifecycle state

- Adds `src/agents/agent-lifecycle-parent-state.ts`.
- Classifies lifecycle events with explicit yielded/waiting vs terminal semantics.
- Exports the classifier through `openclaw/plugin-sdk/reply-runtime`.
- Routes subagent registry and Discord source-message handling through the classifier instead of local `yielded && paused` inference.

### Cron lifecycle and delivery

- Adds first-class cron run status `deferred`.
- Classifies yielded descendant handoff before delivery-mode branching, so text, structured payloads, `delivery.mode: none`, source-satisfied delivery, and normal direct delivery all share the same semantics.
- Prevents duplicate/interim parent announcements while descendants are active.
- Records yielded-without-descendant as explicit error diagnostic.
- Keeps deferred manual task runs active rather than failing them.
- Disables one-shot deferred cron jobs after handoff to avoid retry loops.

### Persistence, protocol, CLI, and UI

- Extends run-log JSON/SQLite encoding and status filtering for `deferred`.
- Extends Gateway protocol schemas and cron server filters.
- Extends CLI status/wait typing and docs.
- Extends hook-visible status typing.
- Adds Control UI status/filter labels and generated locale fallbacks.

### Parent/subagent reconciliation

- Tracks yielded/paused parents that still have pending descendants.
- Marks yielded parents with `wakeOnDescendantSettle` so they are resumed/reconciled when descendant work settles.
- Handles child success/failure settlement through existing subagent lifecycle recovery paths.
- Adds regression coverage for yielded parents being reconciled after child failure so diagnostics can wake the parent.

### Discord/source-message lifecycle

- Projects lifecycle events from agent execution into reply/channel handling.
- Uses the shared classifier to identify yielded/waiting parent state.
- Preserves in-progress/progress representation for yielded parents with active children.
- Avoids prematurely marking Discord status reactions done or clearing draft/progress state when the parent yielded and remains waiting.

### Concurrent user-message semantics

`docs/tools/subagents.md` documents the selected policy: if a human sends another message while a requester is yielded, the new message starts a normal turn for the same requester session. OpenClaw keeps the yielded run visible as waiting on descendant completion rather than converting it into a stale final reply; when descendant completion arrives, the completion event is handed back to the requester for synthesis.

## Implementation Notes

Implementation details are included in the What Changes section above; focused evidence and live behavior proof are preserved below.

## Tests / Verification

Focused test coverage plus type, docs, and formatting gates are preserved under Evidence below.

## Evidence

### Rebase/Squash/Proof

- Common upstream base: `13ecca5408cbc94e66105608bfe770d0fc660d76` (`origin/main`, `fix(telegram): back off session init spool retries`)
- Previous PR head: `c163d18fa610687e7dfb8585f1fe8f30b0c4185d`
- Current PR head: `73cff6aa1b0a3ab5786fdfc3a96c98f575e7fcc8`

### ClawSweeper Requested Real Behavior Proof Coverage

ClawSweeper requested redacted live behavior proof for the yielded-parent/deferred lifecycle across the surfaces touched by this PR. This body currently includes the live cron/subagent deferred handoff proof below: a real Dev-01 cron run where the yielded parent remained `deferred` while a descendant was active, with redacted run output, child completion marker, and run/shared-state checks.

Remaining ClawSweeper-requested proof not present in this body yet:

- Redacted Discord visual status/progress/status-reaction proof showing a yielded parent with active descendants remains visibly in progress until descendant settlement.
- Best-effort cron yielded handoff proof/regression after the `deliveryBestEffort` bypass fix, showing best-effort delivery does not incorrectly bypass the yielded-parent deferred lifecycle.
- Migration/upgrade compatibility proof for the detected persistent data-model/status-contract changes.

Maintainer acceptance is still needed for the public `deferred` cron/status/SDK contract; that is a review decision, not something runtime proof alone can certify.

### Real / Live Behavior Proof

Redacted observed output from the live run:


The non-zero wait exit is expected for this proof: `openclaw cron run --wait` exits non-zero for persisted `deferred` status, while still returning the run record. Follow-up inspection showed the spawned child completed with marker `CHILD_MARKER pr95996-95847-live-20260623T222458Z` and the shared state row recorded `ended_reason = subagent-complete`. Coverage includes:

target.title: fix(slack): bound userCache growth with pruneMapToMaxSize
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`userCache` in Slack monitor context stores resolved user names from `users.info` API calls but has no pruning — every unique user ID accumulates forever. On a busy Slack workspace with thousands of users, this Map grows without bound.

## Why This Change Was Made

`channelCache` already uses `pruneMapToMaxSize(channelCache, 1024)` but `userCache` was missed. The fix adds the same pattern at 2048 entries.

## User Impact

- Prevents unbounded memory growth in long-running Slack monitor sessions
- Oldest entries are evicted when the cap is reached
- No behavioral change for typical usage (2048 entries covers most workspaces)

## Evidence

### Real Slack API — Token + users.info

```
$ curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer \$SLACK_TOKEN" https://slack.com/api/auth.test
{
    "ok": true,
    "bot_id": "B0BGACNKEGJ",
    "team_id": "T0BG72E2G2Z",
    "user_id": "U0BFV1X131V"
}

$ curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer \$SLACK_TOKEN" https://slack.com/api/users.info?user=U0BFV1X131V
{
    "ok": false,
    "error": "missing_scope",
    "needed": "users:read",
    "provided": "channels:history,channels:read,chat:write,..."
}
```

The token is valid but lacks `users:read` scope, matching the `missing_scope` error path already handled by the catch block in `resolveUserName`. Real Slack workspaces with `users:read` scope would resolve successfully and fill the cache.

### Unit Test — Proves actual eviction

```
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/slack/src/monitor/context.test.ts
 ✓ evicts the oldest user name when the bounded user cache fills
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  10 passed (10)
```

Test flow:
1. resolveUserName("U0OLDEST") → 1 API call, cached
2. Fill 2048 more users → 2048 API calls, U0OLDEST evicted
3. Re-request resolveUserName("U0OLDEST") → fresh API call (cache miss)
4. expect(usersInfo).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(2050) → PASS

Without eviction, step 3 would return the stale cached entry and total would stay at 2049.

### Lint + Format
```
$ npx oxlint -c .oxlintrc.json extensions/slack/src/monitor/context.ts  # No errors
$ npx oxfmt --check extensions/slack/src/monitor/context.ts              # Correct format
```

## What Changed

- extensions/slack/src/monitor/context.ts: +2 lines (SLACK_USER_CACHE_MAX_ENTRIES + pruneMapToMaxSize)
- extensions/slack/src/monitor/context.test.ts: +19 lines (eviction test with re-request assertion)

## AI Assistance 🤖
- **AI-assisted**: Yes
- **Co-Authored-By**: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>
- **Human confirmed understanding**: Yes

target.title: fix(cli): use startsWith for loopback IPv4 check in container proxy
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`isLoopbackProxyHostname` used `split(".", 1)[0] === "127"` to detect 127.0.0.0/8 loopback addresses. While `isIP()` already rejects invalid octets (leading zeros, out-of-range) before this branch, `split(".", 1)[0]` is unnecessarily indirect and obscures the intent of matching the full 127.0.0.0/8 range.

## Why This Change Was Made

`startsWith("127.")` directly expresses the intent of matching any valid IPv4 address in the 127.0.0.0/8 loopback block. It is equivalent in behavior (since `isIP() === 4` already validated the format) but clearer and less fragile.

## User Impact

No behavior change — same loopback detection logic, just more readable and maintainable.

## Evidence

```text
$ npx vitest run src/cli/container-target.test.ts
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  32 passed (32)
```

All existing test cases including `127.0.0.01` (rejected by `isIP()`) and `127.0.0.1` (detected as loopback) continue to pass.

target.title: feat(skills): capture reusable techniques from successful work
target.body:
Closes #105672

## What Problem This Solves

Opt-in Skill Workshop autonomy can capture explicit corrections, but reusable procedures discovered during long successful work are otherwise lost when the user did not phrase the result as a correction.

## Why This Change Was Made

When autonomous capture is enabled, successful foreground turns with at least ten model iterations may schedule a separate learning review after the run has finished and the whole agent system has remained idle for 30 seconds. The delayed review rechecks live autonomy, sandbox, agent, provider, sender, and conversation tool policy before it starts.

The reviewer is isolated to the exact resolved provider and model, reuses the auth profile when available, and disables model fallback. It runs on a dedicated background lane and receives a bounded rendering of only the current turn. Its Skill Workshop surface permits list/inspect plus at most one create or revise mutation; live-skill updates and proposal lifecycle actions are unavailable. Every generated result remains a pending proposal for human review.

The evidence bar is intentionally narrow: concrete struggle, correction, repeated failure, or a stable procedure expected to save at least two future model/tool round trips. Routine success, one-off facts, preferences, transient failures, secrets, generic advice, and uncertain cases must abstain.

## User Impact

Users who explicitly enable autonomous Skill Workshop capture can receive reviewable learning proposals after meaningful work without delaying foreground requests. The feature remains off by default, waits for idle state across embedded and reply-backed runs, bounds retained work, serializes learning reviews, and never applies a proposal automatically.

The new Self-learning guide documents enablement, eligibility, transcript and provider behavior, cost and privacy implications, proposal-only permissions, review commands, and troubleshooting. Skill Workshop, skills configuration, navigation, and the generated docs map link to that guide.

## Evidence

- Blacksmith Testbox [run 29221332451](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/29221332451): 32 focused scheduler, Workshop, and lane tests passed; Oxlint reported zero findings; `tsgo:core` and `tsgo:core:test` passed.
- Blacksmith Testbox [run 29222289445](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/29222289445): final scheduler suite passed after exact-model fail-closed pinning; Oxlint and both TypeScript lanes passed.
- Public-network AWS Crabbox run `run_07545709b518`: live OpenAI evaluation created exactly one pending proposal for a recovered deployment preflight and created no additional proposal for a routine one-off audit.
- Docs validation: `docs:check-mdx`, `docs:check-links`, `docs:check-i18n-glossary`, `docs:map:check`, `format:docs:check`, and `git diff --check` passed.
- Fresh autoreview: clean, no accepted/actionable findings.

target.title: perf(subagent-registry): replace full-table scans with scoped indexed queries
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The `listSubagentRunsForController` hot path loads the **entire persisted subagent registry** (all rows from SQLite via `getSubagentRunsSnapshotForRead`) and performs synchronous `Array.filter()` scanning, blocking the event loop linearly with registry size. The SQLite schema already has `idx_subagent_runs_controller_session_key` but the store layer never uses it.

## What This PR Does

1. **Store layer** — Added `loadSubagentRunsForControllerFromSqlite`: a scoped Kysely query that uses the existing `idx_subagent_runs_controller_session_key` index with a compound predicate preserving the `controllerSessionKey || requesterSessionKey` fallback semantics. Also added `loadSubagentRunsForRequesterFromSqlite` for test/standby use.
2. **State layer** — Added `getSubagentRunsSnapshotForController`: a scoped snapshot function that overlays in-memory runs on scoped SQL results. **Now includes a per-controller-key cache** with the same 500ms TTL used by the full-snapshot path, so repeated status/control calls and recursive multi-controller traversals reuse indexed reads instead of issuing synchronous SQLite queries on every lookup. Cache entries are invalidated on `persistSubagentRunsToDisk`.
3. **Caller** — Updated `listSubagentRunsForController` in `subagent-registry.ts` and `subagent-registry-read.ts` to use the scoped snapshot. The `listSubagentRunsForRequester` path is **unchanged**.
4. **Tests** — 8 new store tests, 5 state-layer tests (equivalence + cache behavior), and 5 end-to-end correctness+benchmark tests (cold, warm, recursive).

No schema migration required — all needed indexes already exist.

## Evidence

### Benchmark results (10K records, ext4 SSD, Windows x64)

```
=== Controller query cold-cache benchmark (10000 records) ===
Full-scan (load all + filter): avg=290.75ms
Scoped   (indexed query):      avg=2.14ms
Cold-cache speedup: 136.1x

=== Warm repeated-call benchmark (20 calls, same key) ===
Full-scan (global cache): total=350.50ms avg=17.52ms
Scoped   (per-key cache): total=11.18ms avg=0.56ms
Warm speedup: 31.3x

=== Recursive multi-controller benchmark (10 keys, 10000 records) ===
Full-scan (1 hydrate + N filters): total=364.54ms avg=36.45ms
Scoped   (N indexed + cache):      total=99.03ms avg=9.90ms
Recursive speedup: 3.7x
```

The scoped path with per-key caching **strictly dominates** the full-scan approach across all workloads: cold (136x), warm repeated (31x), and recursive multi-controller (3.7x).

### Benchmark reproducer

```bash
pnpm vitest run src/agents/subagent-registry-scoped.bench.test.ts
```

### Correctness

- Scoped controller snapshot produces **identical results** to filtering the full snapshot
- In-memory record overlay preserves the same `controllerSessionKey || requesterSessionKey` precedence
- Scoped cache is invalidated on persist, ensuring consumers see fresh data after writes

### Tests

```bash
pnpm test src/agents/subagent-registry-state.test.ts
pnpm test src/agents/subagent-registry.store.sqlite.test.ts
pnpm test src/agents/subagent-registry.test.ts
pnpm test src/agents/subagent-registry-scoped.bench.test.ts
pnpm test src/agents/subagent-registry-read-context.test.ts
pnpm test src/auto-reply/reply/commands-subagents-status.test.ts
```

**268/268 passing, 0 failures, 0 regressions.**

### Files changed (8 files, +806/-5)

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `src/agents/subagent-registry.store.sqlite.ts` | +71: 2 scoped query functions |
| `src/agents/subagent-registry-state.ts` | +133: 2 scoped snapshot functions + per-key cache |
| `src/agents/subagent-registry.ts` | +10/-4: DI surface + controller caller |
| `src/agents/subagent-registry-read.ts` | +7/-1: controller caller |
| `src/agents/subagent-registry.store.sqlite.test.ts` | +131: 8 store test cases |
| `src/agents/subagent-registry-state.test.ts` | +144: 5 equivalence + cache tests |
| `src/agents/subagent-registry.test.ts` | +12/-19: mock surface update |
| `src/agents/subagent-registry-scoped.bench.test.ts` | +305: 5 e2e benchmarks (new file) |

Fixes #105423.

target.title: fix: deliver completed replies when post-turn compaction fails
target.body:
Closes #94688

Related: #94928

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users could lose a completed channel reply when post-turn transcript compaction failed or the gateway restarted during compaction. The reply could already be present in the local transcript and Control UI while never reaching the originating channel.

## Why This Change Was Made

The turn owner now records the canonical, user-visible pending final before optional post-turn compaction. An ordinary compaction failure remains visible in logs but no longer blocks delivery when a genuinely sendable final exists; restart and stale-lifecycle aborts still fail closed so the old run cannot double-send.

The pending marker follows provider and successful-compaction session successors, and cleanup uses exact session ownership checks so an unrelated later rotation cannot clear another run's state. Silent, reasoning-only, heartbeat-only, and outbound-suppressed relay payloads do not manufacture pending-delivery state.

This is intentionally implemented on current `main` rather than by updating #94928: the older branch is conflicting and only catches the compaction exception. It does not make the completed final durable before compaction, so it leaves the restart window and successor-session cleanup unresolved.

## User Impact

Users can expect a completed reply to be delivered even if optional post-turn compaction times out or otherwise fails. If the process restarts in that window, restart recovery has a durable text marker instead of relying only on the local transcript.

No configuration surface or timeout default changes. Empty or intentionally suppressed replies still treat compaction failure as fatal, and successful compaction behavior is unchanged.

## Evidence

- Validation environment: local macOS using the repository's narrow Codex-worktree fallback; hosted CI is pending on this draft.

- No live configuration was changed and no private transcript or deployment log is included in this PR.

target.title: fix(cron): batch pending-media snapshot in session reaper to avoid O(SxT) loop
target.body:
#### What Problem This Solves

Close #105694

Fixes an O(S × T) CPU bottleneck in the cron session reaper that blocks the Node.js event loop on each timer tick. For every cron continuation row, `sweepCronRunSessions` called `hasPendingGeneratedMediaTaskForSessionKey`, which internally performs `listTaskRecords` — a full cloned-and-sorted snapshot of all task records plus in-process generated-media activity. With thousands of sessions, this synchronous work saturates the main thread and causes gateway timeout / WebSocket disconnection.

#### Why This Change Was Made

Instead of changing the per-row `hasPendingGeneratedMediaTaskForSessionKey` helper (still used by the single-invocation `cron-run-continuation-cleanup` path), this adds `buildPendingGeneratedMediaSessionKeySet` — a one-shot snapshot that collects all session keys with pending generated-media work by iterating the in-process activity map once and the full task registry once. The reaper then does O(1) `Set.has()` lookups inside the loop.

Key design decisions:
- Preserves the exact `requesterSessionKey` / `ownerKey` matching contract — no semantic change, only a scan-lifting optimization
- The snapshot is deliberately conservative: session keys that the reaper never visits may still be included, which is harmless
- ClawSweeper confirmed the shape: "one canonical bulk pending-generated-media session-key snapshot that combines active in-process work with nonterminal persisted requester and owner keys"

#### User Impact

No visible impact. The cron reaper produces identical pruning decisions with strictly less CPU time per sweep.

#### Evidence

- **Type check:** `tsgo` passes with no errors
- **Unit tests:**
  - `task-status-access.test.ts` — 10 tests pass (+6: `buildPendingGeneratedMediaSessionKeySet`)
  - `session-reaper.test.ts` — 20 tests pass (mock updated to use `buildPendingSet`)
  - `cron-run-continuation-cleanup.test.ts` — 5 tests pass (no regression)
- **Change scope:** 5 files, +131 −7 lines
  - `src/tasks/generated-media-task-activity.ts` — new `getAllActiveGeneratedMediaSessionKeys` export
  - `src/tasks/task-status-access.ts` — new `buildPendingGeneratedMediaSessionKeySet` helper
  - `src/cron/session-reaper.ts` — one snapshot call before the loop, `Set.has()` per row
  - `src/tasks/task-status-access.test.ts` — 6 new tests
  - `src/cron/session-reaper.test.ts` — mock updated for new function
  - No config, CLI, SDK, docs, or changelog surface affected
- **No new dependencies** — reuses existing `listTaskRecords`, `getActiveGeneratedMediaTasks`, `isTerminalTaskStatus`
- **Timing proof:** the `listTaskRecords` mock performs real clone+sort work on every call (matching production). Old and new paths are compared side-by-side at realistic scale with wall-clock measurement. The reaper was seeded with 500 cron continuation sessions and real `sweepCronRunSessions` verified the production code path.

```
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/cron/_proof-reaper-timing.test.ts --reporter verbose

 ✓ new path calls listTaskRecords exactly once at S=500 (old would call ~250x)

  [S=500, T=200]
  new path: buildPending + 500x Set.has → 0.76ms
  old path: 50x hasPending (sampled)   → 4.58ms
  old path projected (500x):           → 45.81ms
  speedup: 60.4x
  pending set: 83, new hits: 43, old hits (sampled): 30
  sweep result: swept=true, pruned=457

 ✓ new and old produce identical decisions on sampled rows

  correctness: 100/100 match, 0 mismatch
  pending set size: 165

 ✓ requesterSessionKey + ownerKey both captured, terminal excluded
   (video_generation processing → both keys in set; succeeded task excluded; chat excluded)

 ✓ scale: at S=1000, new path still sub-millisecond

  [S=1000, T=500] pending set: 105, loop hits: 210
  total (buildPending + 1000x Set.has): 0.77ms
  old path projected: ~192.7ms (500 continuation rows × clone+sort)

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  4 passed (4)
```

- **S=500, T=200:** 60.4x speedup (0.76ms new vs 45.81ms old projected)
- **S=1000, T=500:** ~250x speedup (0.77ms new vs ~192.7ms old projected)
- **Correctness:** 100/100 sampled rows produce identical old-vs-new decisions
- **Contract:** `requesterSessionKey` + `ownerKey` both captured; terminal tasks excluded; non-generated-media ignored

target.title: fix(cli): stop rewriteUpdateFlagArgv from corrupting positional --update values
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`rewriteUpdateFlagArgv` rewrites any occurrence of `--update` to `update`, even when `--update` appears:
- After the `--` end-of-options marker (where it's a positional value)
- After a subcommand like `config set` (where it's a value, not a root flag)

This corrupts user input and can silently change values passed to commands like `openclaw config set`. Fixes #105923.

## Why This Change Was Made

The function is meant to support the old root-level `--update` spelling (equivalent to the `update` subcommand). The fix constrains rewriting to only when `--update` is used as a root-level command — before any subcommand and before `--`.

The fix:
1. Finds the `--` end-of-options marker and only searches for `--update` before it
2. Checks for a subcommand (first non-flag, non-flag-value word) before `--update`; if one exists, `--update` is a positional argument, not a root command
3. Skips long-flag value pairs (`--flag value`) when scanning for subcommands

## Evidence

```
$ npx vitest run src/cli/run-main.test.ts --no-coverage -t "rewriteUpdateFlagArgv"

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  7 passed | 36 skipped (43)
```

All 7 tests pass (4 existing + 3 new regression tests):
- `--update` after `--` is not rewritten
- `--update` as a positional value for a subcommand is not rewritten
- `--update` after a subcommand is not rewritten

## Merge Risk

Low. The change only affects the `rewriteUpdateFlagArgv` function used during CLI startup. Existing behavior for root-level `--update` is preserved. The only behavioral change is that `--update` used as a positional value (after `--` or after a subcommand) is no longer incorrectly rewritten.

target.title: fix(agents): bound compaction planning worker payloads
target.body:
Addresses #100635

## What Problem This Solves

Compaction planning sanitizes private fields before worker handoff, but previously still sent full model-visible tool-result text and base64 image data through `workerData`. Large browser/command results or multimodal transcripts could therefore force multi-megabyte structured-clone work before summary-prompt truncation had a chance to help.

## Why This Change Was Made

This adds a planning-only projection before worker handoff:

- oversized tool-result text/content keeps a bounded UTF-16-safe sample plus omitted-character accounting;
- image blocks in user, custom, and tool-result content keep their type/MIME metadata but omit base64 bytes;
- token-pressure accounting remains conservative, so chunking and pruning decisions still reflect the original payload;
- local fallback behavior and private-field sanitization remain unchanged.

Image bytes are not used by compaction's text serializer, while image token pressure is a fixed per-block estimate. Omitting only `data` therefore reduces worker cloning without changing summary text or planning pressure. The pure projection helper is split from worker orchestration so both implementation files remain below the repository's 500-line guard (476 and 109 lines).

## User Impact

Long or multimodal sessions should spend less time and memory cloning redundant payloads into the compaction planning worker, reducing event-loop stall and OOM risk without changing compaction decisions or generated summary text.

## Evidence

- Final `upstream/main` rebase: `26210c16003f16768b02e989af773e536b15d6f2`; branch HEAD: `0899710631f6350c8fe34e238a9d12049415b0b9`.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/agents/compaction.token-sanitize.test.ts packages/agent-core/src/harness/compaction/compaction.test.ts packages/agent-core/src/harness/compaction/compaction-image-tokens.test.ts`: 13 tests passed across 3 files on the final rebased HEAD.
- `pnpm check:loc --base-ref upstream/main`: passed; implementation files are 476 and 109 lines.
- Changed-file `oxlint` and `git diff --check upstream/main...HEAD`: passed.
- Core production typecheck passed locally. The same code also passed the repository build and CI `build-artifacts` lane before the final baseline-only rebase.
- Independent `codex review --uncommitted`: no correctness findings after fixing the user-image coverage gap it identified.
- Text projection microbenchmark:
  - 1 x 120k-char tool result: `120,134` -> `8,436` bytes (`92.98%` reduction), token estimate `30,000` -> `30,001`.
  - 65 x 40k-char tool results: `2,608,758` -> `548,258` bytes (`78.98%` reduction), token estimate `650,000` -> `650,065`.
- Packaged-worker image smoke using `dist/agents/compaction-planning.worker.js` with one 1 MB user image and one 1 MB tool-result image in a 64-message request:

  - serialized summary input: identical;

target.title: fix(ios): block omitted share attachments
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes #103363.

The iOS Share Extension accepted at most three image attachments and ignored videos, files, PDFs, and unknown attachment providers while still moving toward the normal send flow. That let a user share partial content without any visible explanation.

## Why This Change Was Made

This keeps the current gateway media contract unchanged: the share route still sends image attachments only, and it does not attempt to add video/PDF/file transport in this PR.

Instead, extraction now records selected image count, accepted image count, and unsupported attachment classes. If the extension would omit selected content, the compose card enters the existing blocked state with a concrete recovery message, so send stays disabled until the user removes omitted items and shares again.

## User Impact

- Sharing 6 images now shows: `Only 3 of 6 images can be sent. Remove omitted items and share again.`
- Sharing a video, PDF/file, or unknown attachment now shows an unsupported-item message instead of silently sending only text or the first accepted images.
- Normal shares with up to 3 images are unchanged.

## Evidence

Focused local proof:

```text
SHARE_ATTACHMENT_SUMMARY_PROOF=PASS
Only 3 of 6 images can be sent. Remove omitted items and share again.
OpenClaw Share cannot send 1 video(s), 2 file(s), 1 unsupported item(s) yet. Remove omitted items and share again.
```

Validation run:

```text
swiftc /tmp/.../ShareAttachmentSummary.swift /tmp/.../main.swift -o /tmp/.../share-proof && /tmp/.../share-proof
git diff HEAD^ HEAD --check
```

### Real proof

Exact-head native simulator proof for `5dda9040ac66350805428609bca660dd5373e6f6`.

Environment: iPhone 17 Pro simulator, iOS 26.2 (`23C54`), Xcode 27.0. The installed app's `OpenClawGitCommit` is the exact PR head above. Both scenarios used the real Photos → Share Sheet → OpenClaw Share Extension path.

#### Six-image omission path

- Selected 6 photos in Photos.
- The extension rendered: `Only 3 of 6 images can be sent. Remove omitted items and share again.`
- Send was disabled.
- After entering `Compare all six images`, Send remained disabled.
- XCTest result: **Passed** (`39.91s`).

![Six selected images show the omission warning with Send disabled](https://files.catbox.moe/91crio.png)

#### Normal one-image control

- Selected 1 photo in Photos.
- After entering `Describe this image`, Send enabled normally.
- XCTest result: **Passed** (`27.65s`).

![A normal one-image share enables Send after draft text is entered](https://files.catbox.moe/1vcxn8.png)

```text

xcodebuild ... -only-testing:OpenClawUITests/ShareExtensionUITests/testOneSelectedImageStillEnablesSendAfterDraftText test
```

target.title: feat(ui): render streaming chat markdown live instead of plain text
target.body:
Closes #106053

## What Problem This Solves

Resolves a problem where assistant replies streaming into the Control UI chat (web UI) showed the in-flight portion as raw plain text — `**bold**` markers, bare `| table |` rows, and unstyled code — until the whole message finished, then the message snapped into formatted markdown. The streaming renderer only formatted text up to the last blank line outside a code fence, so single paragraphs, lists, tables, and open fenced code blocks stayed unformatted for their entire streaming lifetime.

## Why This Change Was Made

Streamed replies are the primary reading surface in web chat; raw markdown markers plus the end-of-run reflow made them noticeably harder to read than the final render. The stable-prefix pipeline (markdown-it + DOMPurify with repo-specific rules for file links, sanitize hooks, copy buttons, and task lists) is kept as-is; only the tail handling changes:

- The streaming tail is repaired with `remend` (Vercel's zero-dependency `string -> string` incomplete-markdown fixer extracted from Streamdown, Apache-2.0) and then rendered through the same sanitized markdown-it pipeline. Unclosed `**` / `*` / `` ` `` / `~~` close instead of flashing literal markers, half-written links render as text-only, and math completion is disabled since this pipeline does not render KaTeX.
- Inside an open code fence, repair is skipped and markdown-it auto-closes the fence at end of input (CommonMark), so code streams as a live-highlighted code block instead of escaped text.
- Refactor while in the area: the uncached render core is extracted (`renderSanitizedMarkdown`) so per-delta tail renders stop churning the LRU markdown cache, and the now-unused `toStreamingPlainTextHtml` path plus its tests/mocks are deleted. Net −7 non-test LOC.

Alternatives (Streamdown itself is React-only; smd/Incremark/stream-markdown-parser replace the whole pipeline) are covered in #106053.

## User Impact

Everyone using the Control UI / web chat sees streamed replies render as formatted markdown while they arrive: headings, bold/italic, lists, tables, links, and code blocks with live syntax highlighting. No more raw markers or full-message reflow when a reply completes. Completed-message rendering is unchanged.

## Evidence

- `pnpm test ui/src/components/markdown.test.ts` — 104 passed, including new coverage: tail bold closes while streaming, half-written links render text-only, tables render before the closing row, `$$50` prose is left alone, open fences (top-level, in lists, in blockquotes) stream as highlighted code blocks, and the stable prefix still renders exactly once across deltas (cache reuse asserted via `md.render` spy).
- `pnpm test ui/src/pages/chat/components/chat-message.test.ts` — 91 passed (streaming rows keep routing through `toStreamingMarkdownHtml`).

target.title: gateway: fs.listDir node pairing can be approved without operator.admin
target.body:
## Summary
A caller with `operator.pairing` and `operator.write`, but without `operator.admin`, can approve a node surface that declares `fs.listDir`. The same command is explicitly admin-gated when it is invoked, so the pairing trust decision is weaker than the command's execution boundary.

## Environment
- Commit: a674ce5e0d1ab0774546086fa7b2730516eca176 (origin/main at time of filing)
- Surface: Gateway node pairing authorization and node-host filesystem directory browsing

## Steps to reproduce
1. Register a pending node pairing request whose declared commands are `["fs.listDir"]`.
2. Call `node.pair.approve` with an operator session containing `operator.pairing` and `operator.write`, but not `operator.admin`.
3. Observe that the pairing is accepted and persists `fs.listDir` on the node surface.

## Expected
Approving a node surface that declares `fs.listDir` should require `operator.admin`, matching the existing invoke-time authorization for that command.

## Actual
The approval-scope resolver classifies `fs.listDir` as a generic non-exec command and requires only `operator.pairing` plus `operator.write`. The accepted surface is then persisted by the real pairing approval path.

## Root cause
`src/infra/node-pairing-authz.ts:11` defines the commands that need admin approval:

```ts
const ADMIN_APPROVAL_COMMANDS = [...NODE_SYSTEM_RUN_COMMANDS, NODE_BROWSER_PROXY_COMMAND];
```

`fs.listDir` was added in #105114 and is included in `ADMIN_ONLY_NODE_INVOKE_COMMANDS` in `src/gateway/server-methods/nodes.ts:115`, but it was never added to `ADMIN_APPROVAL_COMMANDS`. `approveNodePairing` calls `resolveNodePairApprovalScopes` before it persists the node surface, so every `node.pair.approve` path uses the weaker mapping.

## Sibling surfaces
#104491 fixed the same approval-versus-invocation scope mismatch for `browser.proxy` by adding that command to `ADMIN_APPROVAL_COMMANDS`. This report concerns the separate `fs.listDir` command introduced later in #105114. The command is live: it is advertised by the node command policy, accepted by the node host runtime, and dispatched by the `fs.listDir` gateway handler. This is not an unreachable or dead declaration.

target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Telegram diagnostics and membership audits could keep waiting after the Bot API returned response headers but then stalled or only trickled the response body.

## Why This Change Was Made

Telegram Bot API diagnostic body reads now use a Telegram-local bounded reader with the existing byte cap, a per-chunk idle timeout, and an overall body deadline. The change covers `getMe`, best-effort `getWebhookInfo`, and membership-audit `getChatMember` reads without changing fetch/header timeout or webhook best-effort semantics.

## User Impact

Telegram setup checks and membership audits now fail or degrade on a bounded deadline instead of appearing to spin forever on a stuck response body.

## Evidence

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/telegram/src/response-body-timeout.test.ts extensions/telegram/src/probe.response-body-timeout.test.ts extensions/telegram/src/probe.test.ts extensions/telegram/src/audit.test.ts` (22 tests passed)

```text
HTTP_PROXY= HTTPS_PROXY= http_proxy= https_proxy= ALL_PROXY= all_proxy= NO_PROXY=127.0.0.1,localhost no_proxy=127.0.0.1,localhost node_modules/.bin/tsx scratchpad/telegram-diagnostic-exact-head-proof.mts
```

The temporary harness was removed after the run. It called production `probeTelegram()` and `auditTelegramGroupMembership()` through the production Telegram undici transport, routing only the Bot API root to a loopback `node:http` server. It used a redacted fake token, no mocked adapter, no real Telegram traffic, and no credentials.

Redacted transcript:

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where a sender allowed to use one channel could be treated as a global command owner. With config commands enabled, that incorrectly allowed owner-gated mutations such as `/allowlist` and `/config`.

## Why This Change Was Made

The shared command authorization resolver now keeps transport-level command access separate from global owner authority. Only an explicit `commands.ownerAllowFrom` identity or an internal `operator.admin` session grants owner status; channel/context allowlists continue to authorize ordinary commands. This central fix applies to every privileged command using the existing owner gate instead of adding command- or channel-specific authorization branches.

## User Impact

Channel allowlists still let approved senders talk to the bot and use ordinary commands. Owner-only commands now require an explicit command owner, preventing a channel-scoped identity from changing authorization or configuration globally.

Existing one-owner setups remain straightforward: the first approved DM pairing bootstraps `commands.ownerAllowFrom`, and doctor explains how to configure an owner when none exists.

target.title: fix(cli): rewriteUpdateFlagArgv corrupts positional values containing --update
target.body:
Fixes #105923

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where `openclaw --update` was rewritten to `openclaw update` even when `--update` appeared after the `--` terminator or as a positional value for another command (for example, `openclaw config set some.key --update`). This silently corrupted user input.

## Why This Change Was Made

`rewriteUpdateFlagArgv` used `argv.indexOf("--update")`, which matches `--update` anywhere in the argument list. The intended behavior is to preserve the legacy root-level `--update` spelling only when `--update` is the first non-root-option token and appears before `--`. The fix scans past root options (`--profile`, `--log-level`, `--container`, `--dev`, `--no-color`), stops at `--`, and only rewrites the first matching `--update`.

## User Impact

Users can now safely pass `--update` as a literal value to CLI commands or after `--` without it being rewritten to the `update` subcommand. Root-level `openclaw --update` and `openclaw --profile p --update` continue to work as before.

## Evidence

### Real CLI behavior (after fix)

Using an isolated state dir on the PR branch (`08abe64`):

```text
$ OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR=/tmp/openclaw-proof pnpm openclaw --update --help
OpenClaw 2026.7.2 (08abe64) — All your chats, one OpenClaw.

Usage: openclaw update [options] [command]

Update OpenClaw and inspect update channel status
```

Root-level `--update` is still routed to the `update` subcommand.

```text
$ OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR=/tmp/openclaw-proof pnpm openclaw config set env.vars.TEST -- --update
Updated env.vars.TEST. Restart the gateway to apply.

$ OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR=/tmp/openclaw-proof pnpm openclaw config get env.vars.TEST
--update

$ OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR=/tmp/openclaw-proof cat /tmp/openclaw-proof/openclaw.json
{
  "env": {
    "vars": {
      "TEST": "--update"
    }
  },
  "meta": {
    "lastTouchedVersion": "2026.7.2",
    "lastTouchedAt": "2026-07-13T05:44:33.088Z"
  }
}
```

`--update` passed after `--` is preserved as the literal string value instead of being rewritten to `update`.

### Automated tests

Focused tests added to `src/cli/run-main.test.ts`:

- `does not rewrite --update after the -- terminator`
- `does not rewrite --update when it is a positional value for another command`

Before the fix:

```ts
rewriteUpdateFlagArgv(["node", "entry.js", "config", "set", "foo", "--", "--update"]);
// => ["node", "entry.js", "config", "set", "foo", "--", "update"]

rewriteUpdateFlagArgv(["node", "entry.js", "config", "set", "update.channel", "--update"]);
// => ["node", "entry.js", "config", "set", "update.channel", "update"]
```

After the fix:

```ts
// both leave --update unchanged
```

### Validation run

- `pnpm test src/cli/run-main.test.ts --run` → 38/38 passed
- `pnpm test src/cli --run` → 157 files, 2924 tests passed
- `pnpm format:check src/cli/run-main-policy.ts src/cli/run-main.test.ts` → clean
- `node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs src/cli/run-main-policy.ts src/cli/run-main.test.ts` → 0 warnings, 0 errors
