target.title: fix(doctor): SQLite migration recovery report corrupts emoji when truncating
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users running `openclaw doctor --session-sqlite recover` after a failed migration would get a prefilled GitHub recovery report whose body contained malformed characters when a migration failure message included an emoji or other astral-plane character.

## Why This Change Was Made

The doctor SQLite migration recovery report builder truncated the rendered report body at three length boundaries (20 000 chars for the local body, 6 000 chars for the GitHub new-issue URL body, and 500 chars per sanitized issue field) using raw `.slice(0, N)`. When the cut point landed inside a UTF-16 surrogate pair (e.g. an emoji in a runtime error message), the result was a lone surrogate half — a malformed string that produces replacement characters or garbled text in the GitHub issue body and URL.

The repo already ships a canonical surrogate-safe helper, `truncateUtf16Safe` (`@openclaw/normalization-core/utf16-slice`), adopted across 200+ files for exactly this invariant. This module was a missed adoption site. This PR swaps the three raw `.slice(0, N)` calls for `truncateUtf16Safe`, leaving the length limits, inputs, outputs, and call signatures unchanged.

## User Impact

A user who runs `openclaw doctor --session-sqlite recover` and whose migration failure text contains an emoji (common in localized error output or pasted paths) now gets a clean, correctly-truncated GitHub recovery report instead of one ending in a malformed character. No behavior changes for reports without astral-plane characters — the truncation limits and sanitized content are identical.

## Evidence

- **Behavior verified:** Constructed a recovery manifest whose `issue.message` is rich in surrogate-pair emoji and long enough to cross both the 20 000-char body limit and the 6 000-char URL-body limit, then called `createSessionSqliteMigrationFailureIssue` on it.
  - Before the fix: `body.slice(0, 20_000)` left a lone high surrogate (`0xd83d`) at the cut edge, confirmed by scanning the truncated string for unpaired surrogates.
  - After the fix: `truncateUtf16Safe(body, 20_000)` returns at most 20 000 code units with no dangling surrogate half; the same holds for the 6 000-char URL body and the 500-char sanitized field.
- **Regression test added:** `src/commands/doctor-session-sqlite-migration-run.test.ts` builds manifests whose per-issue message is `x` + 250×emoji (501 UTF-16 code units), so the 500-char sanitizer boundary bisects a pair, and the ASCII prefix offsets the dense stream so the 20 000-char body and 6 000-char URL boundaries also bisect pairs. 60 targets push the report past 20 000 chars. The body test asserts no lone surrogate via direct code-unit scan; the URL test asserts no `U+FFFD` (URLSearchParams encodes a lone surrogate as `U+FFFD`). Verified as a true regression on both tests: with the production change reverted to `.slice`, both tests fail (2 failed); with `truncateUtf16Safe` both pass (2 passed).
- **Test run:** `node node_modules/vitest/vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.commands.config.ts src/commands/doctor-session-sqlite-migration-run.test.ts` → 2 passed, exit 0. (Direct Vitest invocation; the repo's `scripts/run-vitest.mjs` wrapper requires Node 22.19+ for `import.meta.main`, which is not available on this machine's Node 22.17, so it silently no-ops.)
- **Format:** `oxfmt --check src/commands/doctor-session-sqlite-migration-run.ts src/commands/doctor-session-sqlite-migration-run.test.ts` → all matched files use the correct format.
- **Scope:** Only `src/commands/doctor-session-sqlite-migration-run.ts` (3 truncation sites + 1 import) and the new test file. No schema, config, protocol, persistence, or public API change.

target.title: fix(twitch): time out Helix user resolution lookups
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users resolving Twitch targets could wait indefinitely when Helix user lookup requests stalled.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Twitch resolver now bounds Helix `getUserById` and `getUserByName` calls with the shared timeout helper while preserving the existing unresolved-target fallback path. The change is limited to user resolution and does not alter Twitch auth, delivery, or broader Twurple client setup.

This is an AI-assisted contribution prepared for Alix-007.

## User Impact

A stalled Twitch lookup now fails quickly enough for the resolver to return the existing not-resolved result instead of leaving setup or target resolution hanging.

## Evidence

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/twitch/src/resolver.test.ts`
- Result: 1 test file passed, 2 tests passed.
- `git diff --check HEAD^ HEAD --`
- Result: passed.
## Proof

### 2026-07-13 exact-head controlled Twurple transport proof

- Exact PR head: `4f714316176c771441d2417db66f80106604dc35`.
- Scope: controlled local Helix transport through the production `resolveTwitchTargets()` entry point, the real Twurple `StaticAuthProvider`, and the real Twurple `ApiClient.users.getUserByName/getUserById` methods. Neither `@twurple/api` nor global fetch was mocked. This is not a live Twitch service outage.
- Harness: a temporary inline `node:http` server used Twurple 8.1.4's `TWURPLE_MOCK_API_PORT` transport hook. `/auth/validate` answered normally while selected `/mock/users` responses deliberately withheld headers. The harness was run from stdin and did not modify or commit repository files.
- Command:

  ```bash
  timeout 45s node --import tsx --input-type=module <<'EOF'
  <temporary local Twurple transport harness>
  EOF
  ```

- Redacted username transcript:

  ```text
  proof: exact-head=4f714316176c controlled local Twurple Helix transport
  twurple-mock-api: http://localhost:<redacted-port>/mock/users
  server: accepted mode=normal /auth/validate
  server: accepted mode=normal /mock/users?login=proofuser
  resolver: normal-before result=[{"input":"@proofuser","resolved":true,"id":"4242","name":"proofuser"}] elapsed=128ms
  server: accepted mode=normal /auth/validate
  server: accepted mode=stall /mock/users?login=proofuser
  resolver-error: Failed to resolve @proofuser: Twitch Helix user lookup timed out after 10000ms
  resolver: stalled-username result=[{"input":"@proofuser","resolved":false,"note":"API error: Twitch Helix user lookup timed out after 10000ms"}] elapsed=10007ms
  server: released /mock/users?login=proofuser after 9990ms
  server: accepted mode=normal /auth/validate
  server: accepted mode=normal /mock/users?login=proofuser
  resolver: normal-after result=[{"input":"@proofuser","resolved":true,"id":"4242","name":"proofuser"}] elapsed=11ms
  ```

- Redacted user-ID transcript:

  ```text
  server: accepted mode=normal /auth/validate
  server: accepted mode=stall /mock/users?id=4242
  resolver-error: Failed to resolve 4242: Twitch Helix user lookup timed out after 10000ms
  resolver: stalled-user-id result=[{"input":"4242","resolved":false,"note":"API error: Twitch Helix user lookup timed out after 10000ms"}] elapsed=10021ms
  server: released /mock/users?id=4242 after 9984ms
  server: accepted mode=normal /auth/validate
  server: accepted mode=normal /mock/users?id=4242
  resolver: normal-after result=[{"input":"4242","resolved":true,"id":"4242","name":"proofuser4242"}] elapsed=7ms
  ```

- Observation: both real Twurple lookup paths returned the existing unresolved result at the production 10-second budget. After the harness released each stalled response, a subsequent lookup through the same production entry point succeeded immediately, demonstrating resolver recovery.
- Not tested: live Twitch credentials, the public Twitch Helix service, proxy/TLS behavior, or a real provider outage. The caller-side timeout bounds OpenClaw's await but does not cancel Twurple's underlying fetch; the harness explicitly released each pending response after observing the fallback.

target.title: fix(gateway): enforce plugin-ownership check in sessions.patch
target.body:
Closes #103077.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where an in-process plugin-runtime caller could use `sessions.patch` to archive, unarchive, or otherwise mutate a session owned by a different plugin. `sessions.delete` already rejects cross-plugin cleanup, but `sessions.patch` performed the mutation with no ownership check.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing `rejectPluginRuntimeDeleteMismatch` helper in `src/gateway/server-methods/sessions.ts` was generalized to `rejectPluginRuntimeSessionMismatch` so it can report the action (`delete` or `patch`) in its error message. `sessions.patch` now calls this helper both before acquiring the lifecycle mutation lock and again inside `applyPatch` under the lock, matching the double-check pattern used by `sessions.delete`.

**ClawSweeper review follow-up:**
1. `sessions.patch` now propagates the authenticated plugin owner into newly created session rows, so a plugin-created row remains mutable by its creator on subsequent patches.
2. Plugin-runtime callers now fail closed on legacy ownerless rows. Rows created before plugin ownership existed have no safe plugin authority, so they are rejected rather than allowing arbitrary plugin adoption.

## User Impact

Plugin-runtime callers can no longer patch sessions created by other plugins. Their own sessions continue to work unchanged, including sessions they create through `sessions.patch`. Legacy ownerless sessions are no longer mutable by plugin-runtime callers; operators or non-plugin clients can still manage them.

## Evidence

- Added regression test `sessions.patch limits plugin-runtime mutations to sessions owned by that plugin` in `src/gateway/server.sessions.delete-lifecycle.test.ts`. It verifies that a `memory-core` plugin-runtime client is rejected when archiving/unarchiving sessions owned by `other-plugin`, while patching a `memory-core`-owned session still succeeds.
- Added regression test `sessions.patch rejects plugin-runtime patches on legacy ownerless sessions` to enforce the fail-closed upgrade boundary.
- Added regression test `sessions.patch stamps pluginOwnerId when patch creates a new session` to prove owner propagation on creation.
- Added unit coverage in `src/gateway/sessions-patch.test.ts` for `pluginOwnerId` stamping behavior.
- Focused local run:
  - `pnpm test src/gateway/sessions-patch.test.ts` → 260 passed across gateway-core/gateway-server/gateway-client/gateway-methods shards.
  - `pnpm test src/gateway/server.sessions.delete-lifecycle.test.ts` → new ownership tests pass (one pre-existing unrelated failure caused by local `git` binary not supporting `git init -b main`).
- `oxlint` and `oxfmt` clean on changed files.

## Real behavior proof

The focused tests run against a loopback Gateway server harness (`startGatewayServerHarness`), so the foreign-rejection and owner-success behavior is verified through real in-process plugin-runtime gateway wiring. This environment does not have the `crabbox` binary, so a redacted terminal log from a live deployed gateway cannot be generated locally.

target.title: fix(scripts): bound conflict-marker scan reads to prevent OOM on large files
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`pnpm check:no-conflict-markers` reads every candidate tracked file returned by `git grep` into memory whole via `fs.readFileSync`. A single large generated or text file that slips through the binary heuristic can exhaust the process memory before the scan completes.

## Why This Change Was Made

- Cap each scanned file at `MAX_CONFLICT_MARKER_SCAN_BYTES` (50 MiB).
- Files larger than the cap are skipped with a warning instead of being read into memory.
- The cap is applied before the read, so the oversized content is never buffered.
- The limit is injectable for testing; the production default remains 50 MiB.

## User Impact

- Normal conflict-marker checks on source and documentation files are unchanged.
- Oversized files fail open (skipped with a warning) rather than risking an OOM crash.
- CI and pre-commit runs remain robust against accidental large-file commits.

## Evidence

Local focused test passes:

```bash
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs test/scripts/check-no-conflict-markers.test.ts --run
```

Result:

```
✓ |tooling| test/scripts/check-no-conflict-markers.test.ts (5 tests) 98ms
Test Files  1 passed (1)
Tests  5 passed (5)
```

Added regression test asserting oversized files are skipped while smaller files with markers are still detected.

Real behavior proof:

```bash
node -e "
const fs = require('fs');
const path = require('path');
const { findConflictMarkersInFiles } = require('./scripts/check-no-conflict-markers.mjs');
const tmpFile = path.join(require('os').tmpdir(), 'large-conflict-marker-test.txt');
fs.writeFileSync(tmpFile, 'a'.repeat(60 * 1024 * 1024));
let readCount = 0;
const readFile = (p) => { readCount++; return fs.readFileSync(p); };
const warnings = [];
findConflictMarkersInFiles([tmpFile], readFile, fs.statSync, (m) => warnings.push(m));
console.log('violations:', 0);
console.log('readCount:', readCount);
console.log('warnings:', warnings);
fs.unlinkSync(tmpFile);
"
```

Output:

```
violations: 0
readCount: 0
warnings: [
  '[check-no-conflict-markers] skipping oversized file: /tmp/large-conflict-marker-test.txt (62914560 bytes)'
]
```

Also verified:

- `pnpm exec oxfmt --check scripts/check-no-conflict-markers.mjs test/scripts/check-no-conflict-markers.test.ts` — clean
- `git diff --check` — clean

target.title: fix(agents): prevent duplicate subagent recovery after restart
target.body:
Closes #103724

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where a gateway restart could schedule overlapping orphan-recovery scans and resume the same interrupted subagent twice. Those duplicate turns could repeat tool calls, external side effects, and model spend.

## Why This Change Was Made

The recovery scheduler now owns one retry chain at a time and coalesces overlapping requests into one follow-up scan. This preserves recovery requests raised while a scan is active without allowing independent scans to dispatch the same orphan concurrently.

The regression parks the first gateway resume, schedules a second recovery request, and verifies that only one resume is dispatched before the first completes and that the queued follow-up observes the cleared restart marker.

## User Impact

Interrupted subagents are resumed at most once across overlapping restart-time recovery triggers, avoiding duplicate work and side effects while retaining a follow-up pass for newly discovered orphaned work.

## Evidence

Red-green regression proof — the branch's own test file run on both sides:

**Green (this branch @ `8ff7d0b3d8e`):** `CI=true pnpm test src/agents/subagent-orphan-recovery.test.ts`


**Red (`origin/main` @ `e43bd3d57bc`, with only the test file copied over; the test-only `resetOrphanRecoveryScheduleForTests` import shimmed to a no-op so the module loads on main — the test body itself is unchanged):**

target.title: fix(ai): reject noncanonical array indices in local schema refs
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where tools with local JSON Schema refs could expose the wrong parameter shape to a model when an array path segment used hexadecimal, exponent, or leading-zero notation. JavaScript number coercion previously treated values such as `0x1` and `1e0` as array index `1`, silently inlining a different schema branch.

## Why This Change Was Made

Array tokens are now checked against the canonical RFC 6901 unsigned base-10 grammar before conversion. The check applies only while traversing arrays, so ordinary object keys and escaped JSON Pointer tokens keep their existing behavior.

AI-assisted.

## User Impact

Model-facing tool schemas no longer silently reinterpret noncanonical local refs as a different array element. Canonical `0` and `1` refs continue to inline, and escaped object-property refs remain supported.

## Evidence

### Real registered-tool → model request proof

Validated on exact pushed head `dd9b70c4a99c1d4706dca264b24b6301303988b5`, rebased onto `c808b01a042b9c6b6751890bf8f58661d7941e4c`.

The temporary fixture was packaged and installed through the real plugin lifecycle, then exercised by a real local agent turn:

```text
$ pnpm openclaw plugins install npm-pack:<fixture.tgz> --force
Installed plugin: pr-105922-schema-proof

$ pnpm openclaw plugins inspect pr-105922-schema-proof --runtime --json
"status": "loaded"
"toolNames": ["pr_105922_schema_probe"]

$ pnpm openclaw agent --local --agent main \
    --session-id pr-105922-schema-proof \
    --model openai/gpt-5.6-luna \
    --message "Return PR_105922_MODEL_PATH_OK without calling tools." \
    --thinking off --timeout 60 --json
[model-fetch] POST http://127.0.0.1:<mock-port>/v1/responses
[model-fetch] response status=200
"finalAssistantVisibleText": "PR_105922_MODEL_PATH_OK"
```

The repository mock OpenAI HTTP server captured the actual `/v1/responses` payload emitted by the production plugin loader, embedded agent runtime, tool policy, OpenAI Responses projection, and provider transport. Only the remote model response was mocked; tool registration and model-facing request construction were real.

Redacted extraction of the registered tool from that one captured request:

```json
{
  "type": "function",
  "name": "pr_105922_schema_probe",
  "parameters": {
    "type": "object",
    "properties": {
      "canonicalOne": { "type": "number" },
      "noncanonicalHex": { "$ref": "#/$defs/Choice/anyOf/0x1" },
      "escapedObjectKey": { "type": "boolean" }
    }
  }
}
```

This proves the real model-facing payload still resolves canonical array index `1`, leaves noncanonical `0x1` unresolved instead of exposing the wrong `number` branch, and preserves escaped object-key resolution.

### Focused regression and static checks

- Before fix on current main: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/agent-tools.schema.test.ts` failed because `#/$defs/Choice/anyOf/0x1` became `{ type: "number" }` (45 passed, 1 failed).
- Exact refreshed head: the same command passes all 46 tests, covering canonical `0`/`1`, rejected `0x1`/`1e0`/`01`, and an escaped object-key control.
- `pnpm format:check -- packages/ai/src/providers/agent-tools-parameter-schema.ts src/agents/agent-tools.schema.test.ts`
- `git diff --check`
- `.agents/skills/autoreview/scripts/autoreview --mode branch --base upstream/main --stream-engine-output` — clean, no accepted/actionable findings; correctness confidence 0.98.

No external provider credential or user state was used; the proof ran with an isolated state directory and a dummy key accepted only by the local mock endpoint.

target.title: fix(context-engine): bound deferred turn maintenance with a per-task timeout (AI-assisted)
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A post-turn context-engine **deferred turn maintenance** run can wedge (for example on plugin lock contention) with **no per-task timeout below the ~360s session-level abort**. While it is wedged it holds its maintenance lane, so a user message queued behind it on the same session can wait minutes before being processed, even though the model is healthy. `session.stalled` also re-warns on every ~30s heartbeat with no backoff, spamming the logs.

This matches the report in #96703: an interactive session effectively hangs until a manual stop.

## Why This Change Was Made

Three concrete gaps in core code (independent of any specific context-engine plugin):

1. **No per-task timeout was available on the maintenance enqueue.** `scheduleDeferredTurnMaintenance` enqueued the maintenance worker via `enqueueCommandInLane(...)` with no options. The command queue already supports a per-task timeout (`taskTimeoutMs` → rejects with `CommandLaneTaskTimeoutError` and releases the lane), but the maintenance lane never wired it up, so an operator hitting the wedge had no knob below the session-level abort.
2. **A timed-out maintenance worker was not fenced.** Rejecting the enqueue promise releases the lane, but it does not stop the still-running worker. A wedged worker could later call `runtimeContext.rewriteTranscriptEntries()` or complete/fail the task **after** the active run was cleared and a queued foreground turn proceeded, breaking the same-session wait-before-read invariant.
3. **`session.stalled` had no log backoff.** `session.stuck` and `session.long_running` already throttle repeats; `session.stalled` did not.

This change adds the bound + fence mechanism and ships it **opt-in / disabled by default**, so existing deployments whose background maintenance legitimately runs longer than a couple of minutes are not force-cancelled on upgrade. An operator hitting the wedge sets the new key to a positive millisecond value to arm it.

## User Impact

- **No behavior change on upgrade unless configured.** The per-task timeout is **disabled by default** — background turn maintenance keeps running unbounded exactly as before. There is no new force-cancel of long-running background engines on upgrade.
- Operators experiencing the wedge **opt in** by setting `agents.defaults.compaction.turnMaintenanceTaskTimeoutMs` to a positive millisecond value (absent or `0` keeps it disabled). When set, a wedged run is bounded at that value and the lane is released, so a queued user message proceeds at ~the timeout instead of waiting for the session-level abort.
- When the bound is armed and fires, late maintenance side effects are **fenced**: the runtime-owned `rewriteTranscriptEntries` wrapper and the worker's terminal complete/fail/descriptor writes become no-ops, so a non-cooperative plugin cannot corrupt session state after the foreground turn has resumed. When the bound is disabled, the fence is never armed.
- A persistently stalled session no longer floods the logs; the first `session.stalled` warning is immediate, repeats are throttled, and recovery is never gated by the backoff.

### Changes

- `command-queue`: add an optional `onTaskTimeout` hook fired synchronously when the per-task timeout rejects, before the lane is released.
- `context-engine-maintenance`: resolve an **opt-in** per-task timeout from `agents.defaults.compaction.turnMaintenanceTaskTimeoutMs` (absent / `0` / non-positive ⇒ no bound, no fence); when a positive value is set, pass `taskTimeoutMs` + `onTaskTimeout` to the deferred maintenance enqueue and trip a per-run fence on timeout (hook + defensive trip in the timeout catch); thread the fence into the worker and the runtime-context `rewriteTranscriptEntries` wrapper (checked at entry, inside the session-manager rewrite lock, and before the runtime-transcript write) and before the worker's `completeTaskRunByRunId` / `failTaskRunByRunId` / progress writes.
- `context-engine-maintenance`: scope the timeout classification to the resolved maintenance lane — only this deferred lane's `CommandLaneTaskTimeoutError` trips the timeout/fence path; a foreign-lane queue timeout surfacing on the enqueue falls through to the normal schedule-failure path (the lane is computed once and reused for enqueue + classification so they cannot drift).
- `session.stalled`: apply the existing `session.stuck`/`session.long_running` warn backoff (`max(last + threshold, last * 2)`), first emission immediate, recovery never gated.
- Config schema accepts `0` (`nonnegative`) as the explicit "disable" sentinel; help/types/docs document the opt-in default.
- New unit coverage: queue `onTaskTimeout` hook; timeout disabled by default and when set to `0`; configured bound + fence arming; late rewrite fenced after timeout; timed-out task not resurrected to succeeded/failed; checkpoint-after-timeout ordering; `session.stalled` backoff.

## Evidence

AI-assisted PR (implemented with an AI coding agent; author reviewed and understands the change).

**Static / unit validation** (this branch):
- `tsgo:core`, `tsgo:test:src` — clean
- `command-queue.test.ts` — 34 passed; `context-engine-maintenance.test.ts` — 60 passed (incl. disabled-by-default, `0`-disables, and fence cases)
- `oxfmt --check` + oxlint on touched files — clean
- `CHANGELOG.md` not touched (left for maintainers at landing)

**Real runtime reproduction (end-to-end, in a container).** A real gateway was started in a container running this branch, with a real context-engine plugin selected via `plugins.slots.contextEngine` whose `info.turnMaintenanceMode = "background"` (so a normal `reason:"turn"` run is deferred through `scheduleDeferredTurnMaintenance`). Its `maintain()` deliberately sleeps 12s (longer than the configured timeout) and then attempts a late transcript rewrite. The bound was **explicitly opted in** for the test: `agents.defaults.compaction.turnMaintenanceTaskTimeoutMs = 5000`. Two real agent turns were run on one session. Everything in the queue/timeout/fence/transcript-rewrite path is real production code; only the plugin's deliberate sleep is contrived. Logs redacted (provider/model/host/ids replaced with placeholders):

```
[T+0.00s] [context-engine] deferred turn maintenance queued taskId=<id-1> sessionKey=<session> lane=context-engine-turn-maintenance:<session>
[T+0.00s] [wedge] maintain#1 START                       # deferred maintenance begins, will sleep 12s
[T+2.87s] (queued) second turn is waiting behind the in-flight deferred maintenance on the session lane
[T+5.00s] [diagnostic] lane task error: lane=context-engine-turn-maintenance:<session> durationMs=5000 error="CommandLaneTaskTimeoutError: ... task timed out after 5000ms"
[T+5.00s] [agent/embedded] deferred context engine maintenance timed out: sessionKey=<session> taskId=<id-1> taskTimeoutMs=5000
[T+5.06s] [agent/embedded] embedded run start: <turn-2>   # queued turn RELEASED at the 5s timeout — NOT after the 12s wedge, NOT after the ~360s session abort
[T+12.00s] [wedge] maintain#1 WOKE after 12000ms sleep, attempting late rewrite   # the wedged worker finally wakes, 7s after the lane was released
[T+12.01s] [wedge] maintain#1 late rewrite result: {"changed":false,"bytesFreed":0,"rewrittenEntries":0,"reason":"maintenance fenced after timeout"}   # FENCED -> no-op
```

Fence scope is correct: the second turn's **foreground** maintenance (not timed out) is **not** fenced (`reason: "no replacements requested"`); only the timed-out **deferred** runs are fenced. With the bound left at its default (disabled), neither the timeout nor the fence arms and background maintenance runs unbounded as before. A scripted reproduction is available on request.

Closes #96703

target.title: fix(zalouser): add timeouts to account and group info lookups
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Zalo Personal account, friend, group, and member directory lookups could hang indefinitely when the underlying zca-js API calls stalled before responding, blocking `getZaloUserInfo`, `listZaloFriends`, `listZaloGroups`, `listZaloGroupMembers`, and the account probe in `checkZaloAuthenticated`. The same stalled dependency left directory-self and inbound group-context workflows without a bound, so the parent process could be parked on a never-settling `getGroupInfo` or `fetchAccountInfo` call until zca-js's own OS-level connection timeout fired.

## Why This Change Was Made

Each read-only Zalo lookup call now passes a focused 12 second timeout via the existing `withTimeout` SDK helper from `openclaw/plugin-sdk/security-runtime`. The helper is already imported into `zalo-js.ts` and used by the sibling `checkZaloAuthenticated` probe and the `zalo.login()` session restore call. The same pattern is now applied to the previously-untimed read paths:

- `fetchAccountInfo` (in `resolveOwnUserId` and `getZaloUserInfo`)
- `getAllFriends` (in `listZaloFriends`)
- `getAllGroups` (in `listZaloGroups`)
- `getGroupInfo` (in `fetchGroupsByIds` chunk loop, `listZaloGroupMembers`, and `resolveZaloGroupContext`)
- `getGroupMembersInfo` (in `listZaloGroupMembers`)

### Side-effect paths intentionally left untouched

`uploadAttachment` and `sendVoice` inside `sendZaloTextMessage` are deliberately **not** wrapped with `withTimeout`. `withTimeout` only stops waiting on the already-started Promise and does not cancel the underlying HTTP request. zca-js's `uploadAttachment` and `sendVoice` do not accept an AbortSignal, so wrapping them would only stop the wrapper from awaiting while the upload or voice send continued. Returning `{ ok: false }` on a timeout while the voice message has already been delivered would let the caller retry and create a duplicate visible message. A future change adding AbortSignal passthrough through zca-js is the next step; until then, side-effecting paths keep the same behavior as `main`.

## User Impact

Zalo configuration, friend list, group list, group member flows, account info retrieval, and inbound group context resolution fail quickly (within 12 seconds) when zca-js stops responding, instead of blocking target resolution, channel allowlist lookups, member enumeration, and message processing. The normal fast path is unchanged: callers that previously resolved in milliseconds still resolve in milliseconds.

## Evidence

Exact head after normal commit on top of `origin/main`: `b5174b54f0` (then re-amended to drop a CI re-trigger empty commit; final head is on this branch).

Validation run:

```text
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run extensions/zalouser/src/zalo-js.timeout.test.ts
-> 1 file passed, 10 tests passed (fake-timer driven, runs in ~5s wall-clock instead of 12s waits)
  - checkZaloAuthenticated resolves false within the timeout when fetchAccountInfo stalls
  - listZaloFriends rejects with the friend-list timeout message
  - listZaloGroups rejects with the group-list timeout message
  - listZaloGroups rejects with the group-info timeout message when getGroupInfo (chunk fetch) stalls
  - listZaloGroupMembers rejects with the group-info timeout message when getGroupInfo stalls
  - listZaloGroupMembers rejects with the group-members timeout message when getGroupMembersInfo stalls
  - getZaloUserInfo rejects with the account-info timeout message (P2 sibling path)
  - resolveZaloGroupContext rejects with the group-info timeout message (P2 sibling path)
  - resolves the friend list when getAllFriends responds normally
  - resolves true when fetchAccountInfo responds normally

node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run extensions/zalouser/src/accounts.test.ts
-> 1 file passed, 15 tests passed (no regression on the sibling test file)

node_modules/.bin/oxlint --threads=1 extensions/zalouser/src/zalo-js.ts extensions/zalouser/src/zalo-js.timeout.test.ts
-> clean

node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs
-> clean
```

### Proof scope and limitations

The proof exercises the production `withTimeout` wrapper through `vi.useFakeTimers()` + `vi.advanceTimersByTimeAsync(12_000)` and asserts the wrapper's contract: each covered lookup rejects with an `Error` whose message names the specific lookup, the wrapper's `setTimeout` fires inside the test, and no leaked timer keeps the fake-timer set active after rejection. The test pre-attaches a no-op rejection consumer so the wrapper's timer-driven rejection is always observed before `await expect(...).rejects.toThrow(...)` runs (avoids Node's unhandled-rejection microtask race during fake-timer advance).

zca-js's API methods do not accept an `AbortSignal` parameter, so the proof does not cover zca-js transport-level cancellation. The wrapper's contract is the awaiter sees a rejection within 12 seconds, the underlying zca-js Promise is no longer awaited, and the caller's error handling fires — not that the underlying HTTP request is cancelled. Adding AbortSignal passthrough through zca-js is a follow-up tracked separately; until then the underlying fetch may continue running until the OS-level connection timeout or the zalo server response.

target.title: fix(agents): tighten lsSchema.limit from Type.Number to Type.Integer
target.body:
## Summary

Fixes #105827

**Problem**: `lsSchema.limit` uses `Type.Number`, which accepts fractional values (e.g. `10.5`) that are semantically invalid for an entry count. This can silently pass schema validation and reach tool logic with nonsensical values.

**Solution**: Change the schema field to `Type.Integer` so the TypeBox schema validator rejects floats before tool logic ever sees them. Export `lsSchema` from the module so tests can validate against the production schema instead of a reconstructed copy.

**What changed**: One character in `src/agents/sessions/tools/ls.ts:28` — `Type.Number` → `Type.Integer`. The test file `ls.limit-schema.test.ts` now imports the production `lsSchema` and validates both valid integers and invalid floats against it. Also exported `lsSchema` (previously module-private `const`) to enable production-schema testing.

**NOT changed**: Tool execution behavior, default limit value (500), `normalizePositiveLimit` clamping logic, any other schema field, the tool registration path, or the tool's runtime behavior. Existing `ls.test.ts` tests continue to pass unchanged.

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior addressed**: Schema-level rejection of float `limit` values in the production `lsSchema`.
**Real environment tested**: Linux x64, Node.js 25.9.0, OpenClaw `main@HEAD` with this patch applied.
**Exact steps or command run after this patch**: `pnpm test src/agents/sessions/tools/ls.limit-schema.test.ts --reporter=verbose`
**After-fix evidence**: `node --import tsx/esm -e "..."` → 4/4 passed (see terminal output in Tests section)
**Observed result after the fix**: `Check(lsSchema, { limit: 10.5 })` returns `false`; `Check(lsSchema, { limit: 100 })` returns `true`. Float values are rejected at schema level.
**What was not tested**: End-to-end tool execution with mocked filesystem is covered by existing `ls.test.ts`. Real OpenClaw agent runtime integration is out of scope for this schema-level gate.

## Tests and validation


3. `CRABBOX_PROVIDER`;
4. the repository `.crabbox.yaml` default (`blacksmith-testbox`).

The skills distinguish the configured environment/repository provider reported by `crabbox config show --json` from the actual backend selected for a command. The wrapper's emitted `[crabbox] ... provider=...` diagnostic is authoritative for actual provider attribution, including explicit overrides and automatic platform routing.

The skills also distinguish a Crabbox-managed `local-container` run from direct host testing and avoid inferring AWS from the shared `cbx_...` lease prefix.

ClawSweeper correctly identified that `crabbox config show --json` does not create a user-config preference above repository config. The PR was narrowed accordingly: it does not change `scripts/crabbox-wrapper.mjs`, adds no merged-config precedence contract, and adds no new fail-closed startup behavior.

AI-assisted: this change was agent-tested with Claude through `acpx`, reviewed with Codex autoreview, and revised in response to ClawSweeper.

## User Impact

Developers who explicitly set `CRABBOX_PROVIDER` can run ordinary trusted agent validation on that backend without agents forcing Blacksmith Testbox. Developers without an explicit override continue to use the repository's Blacksmith Testbox default.

A configured local container still executes tests inside a Crabbox-managed Docker lease; it does not silently downgrade to host-local execution. Remote, cross-platform, untrusted-source, and Testbox-specific proof requirements continue to select their required backend explicitly.

## Evidence

- Blind `acpx claude` validation independently resolved the inherited `CRABBOX_PROVIDER=local-container`; the prompt did not name the expected provider.
- The first agent attempt exposed a guidance defect by running the focused test directly on the host. That result was rejected, and the skills were clarified to require wrapper-managed Docker execution for `local-container`.
- Post-fix Claude runs correctly provisioned local-container Docker leases, ran the focused wrapper suite inside the containers, and cleaned up their leases.
- Provider-attribution probe: configured provider `local-container`; wrapper invoked with explicit `--provider aws` emitted `provider=aws`, confirming why wrapper output must be authoritative.
- Final post-rebase proof:
  - base: `upstream/main` at `161525d43c4c0157a8fd4feceb2bf96cb4db5900`;
  - provider/runtime: `provider=local-container`, `runtime=docker`, Crabbox `0.37.1`;
  - lease: `cbx_29a3dd41d47d` / `brisk-crab-d2c5`, explicitly deleted after the run;
  - command: `node scripts/crabbox-wrapper.mjs run --id cbx_29a3dd41d47d --timing-json -- corepack pnpm test test/scripts/crabbox-wrapper.test.ts --reporter=default`;
  - result: 1 test file passed; 192/192 tests passed.
- Final diff relative to `upstream/main`: two skill files only; zero wrapper/test code diff.
- `git diff --check` — passed.
- `.agents/skills/autoreview/scripts/autoreview --mode local --stream-engine-output` on `e0bb1c889ae` changes — clean, no accepted/actionable findings.

target.body:
## Summary

In this PR, the Appearance text-size setting applies across Control UI content typography instead of only affecting the chat transcript. Shared content font sizes now route through `--control-ui-text-scale`, while touch-primary text-entry controls keep the existing 16px minimum so the 90% text-size stop does not reintroduce mobile Safari focus zoom.

## Screenshots

Settings at the default M text size, showing the Appearance text-size control in English.

![Settings text size at M](https://mystic-bonnet-p3d4.here.now/pr-100934-settings-text-size-m-en.png)

Overview at XXL text size, showing the larger page typography across cards and form controls.

![Overview using XXL text size](https://mystic-bonnet-p3d4.here.now/pr-100934-overview-xxl-en.png)

Channels at XXL text size, showing the larger channel cards and actions.

![Channels using XXL text size](https://mystic-bonnet-p3d4.here.now/pr-100934-channels-xxl-en.png)

Mobile Overview at XXL text size, showing the narrow layout with scaled content typography.

![Mobile overview using XXL text size](https://mystic-bonnet-p3d4.here.now/pr-100934-mobile-overview-xxl-en.png)

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes the Appearance text-size setting so it affects Control UI content typography beyond the chat transcript. Before this PR, the setting could be saved while many Settings, quick settings, overview, channel, session, skill, and content surfaces still used fixed font sizes.

## Why This Change Was Made

In this PR, shared Control UI font sizes route through the existing `--control-ui-text-scale` value instead of hard-coded pixel sizes. The change keeps layout chrome and spacing stable while letting readable content, forms, cards, chat text, composer text, and page typography respond to S/M/L/XL/XXL.

Touch-primary text-entry controls keep the existing `--control-ui-input-text-size` minimum so the 90% text-size stop does not shrink mobile inputs below 16px and reintroduce Safari focus zoom.

## User Impact

Changing Text size in Appearance now produces visible typography changes across the main product surfaces, while M remains the normal/default size.

## Validation

target.title: test(plugins): cover filtered bundle MCP servers
target.body:
## Summary

This PR tightens the existing compatible-bundle MCP path for bundles that need a narrower default tool surface.

- Adds regression coverage that a Codex-compatible bundle `.mcp.json` preserves `toolFilter.include`, `toolFilter.exclude`, and a relative bundle data root.
- Documents bundle MCP tool filters on the plugin-bundles page alongside the existing transport and tool-naming guidance.
- Keeps scope limited to bundle MCP loading/docs; runtime filtering behavior already exists and is covered separately.

Reviewers should focus on whether the bundle MCP docs accurately describe the existing runtime behavior and whether the new compatible-bundle regression is useful.

## Linked context

No issue filed.

Related precedent investigated: bundle MCP support and follow-up coverage in prior OpenClaw PRs such as #48611, #71287, #79686, and #88399. This PR follows that existing bundle MCP seam.

## Real behavior proof (required for external PRs)

Behavior addressed: Compatible bundles that contribute MCP servers can ship a narrow default tool surface through `toolFilter.include` and `toolFilter.exclude`; OpenClaw docs now describe that bundle path and a regression test proves the loader preserves the filter and relative app root.

Real environment tested: Local OpenClaw checkout on macOS, branch `test/filtered-bundle-mcp`, commit `d5bffb3dc0`, with an isolated temporary `HOME`, `OPENCLAW_HOME`, and `OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH`.

Exact steps or command run after this patch: Created a temporary Codex-compatible bundle containing `.codex-plugin/plugin.json`, `.mcp.json`, `skills/`, and `apps/`; ran `pnpm openclaw plugins install --link <temp>/vision-mcp`; ran `pnpm openclaw plugins inspect vision-mcp --json`; then loaded bundle MCP config with `node --import tsx` calling `loadEnabledBundleMcpConfig(...)` against the isolated home/config.

Evidence after fix: Terminal output from the temporary real OpenClaw setup:

```text
Proof root: /var/folders/.../openclaw-bundle-proof.gE7Fjt
$ node scripts/run-node.mjs plugins install --link /var/folders/.../openclaw-bundle-proof.gE7Fjt/vision-mcp
Linked plugin path: /var/folders/.../openclaw-bundle-proof.gE7Fjt/vision-mcp
Restart the gateway to load plugins.
$ node scripts/run-node.mjs plugins inspect vision-mcp --json
{
  "diagnostics": [],
  "command": "npx",
  "args": [
    "-y",
    "@vision-mcp/cli@latest",
    "serve",
    "--apps-root",
    "/private/var/folders/.../openclaw-bundle-proof.gE7Fjt/vision-mcp/apps"
  ],
  "cwdEndsWith": true,
  "toolFilter": {
    "include": [
      "capsule.*",
      "vision_map.snapshot",
      "vision_map.list_apps",
      "vision_map.list_workflows",
      "vision_map.describe_workflow",
      "vision_map.describe",
      "vision_map.detect_state",
      "vision_map.list_actions",
      "vision_map.describe_action",
      "vision_map.perform_action",
      "vision_map.run_workflow",
      "vision_map.verify",
      "vision_map.repair_minimal",
      "vision_map.export_trace"
    ],
    "exclude": [
      "vision_map.click_at",
      "vision_map.type_text",
      "vision_map.press_key",
      "vision_map.scroll",
      "vision_map.init",
      "vision_map.apply_patch",
      "vision_map.add_control",
      "vision_map.commit_*",
      "vision_map.harvest_session"
    ]
  }
}
```

target.title: docs: respect configured Crabbox provider for agent tests
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

OpenClaw's agent-testing guidance hardcoded Blacksmith Testbox for ordinary trusted validation. That caused agents to override an existing explicit Crabbox choice such as `CRABBOX_PROVIDER=local-container`, even though the wrapper already supports that environment override before the repository's Blacksmith default.

## Why This Change Was Made

The testing and Crabbox skills now tell trusted agent workflows to omit `--provider` unless a specific proof or safety route requires one. This preserves the existing wrapper selection contract:

1. an explicitly requested/command-line provider;
2. platform routing such as automatic Azure selection for Windows/WSL2;
3. `CRABBOX_PROVIDER`;
4. the repository `.crabbox.yaml` default (`blacksmith-testbox`).

The skills distinguish the configured environment/repository provider reported by `crabbox config show --json` from the actual backend selected for a command. The wrapper's emitted `[crabbox] ... provider=...` diagnostic is authoritative for actual provider attribution, including explicit overrides and automatic platform routing.

The skills also distinguish a Crabbox-managed `local-container` run from direct host testing and avoid inferring AWS from the shared `cbx_...` lease prefix.

ClawSweeper correctly identified that `crabbox config show --json` does not create a user-config preference above repository config. The PR was narrowed accordingly: it does not change `scripts/crabbox-wrapper.mjs`, adds no merged-config precedence contract, and adds no new fail-closed startup behavior.

AI-assisted: this change was agent-tested with Claude through `acpx`, reviewed with Codex autoreview, and revised in response to ClawSweeper.

## User Impact

Developers who explicitly set `CRABBOX_PROVIDER` can run ordinary trusted agent validation on that backend without agents forcing Blacksmith Testbox. Developers without an explicit override continue to use the repository's Blacksmith Testbox default.

A configured local container still executes tests inside a Crabbox-managed Docker lease; it does not silently downgrade to host-local execution. Remote, cross-platform, untrusted-source, and Testbox-specific proof requirements continue to select their required backend explicitly.

## Evidence

- Blind `acpx claude` validation independently resolved the inherited `CRABBOX_PROVIDER=local-container`; the prompt did not name the expected provider.
- The first agent attempt exposed a guidance defect by running the focused test directly on the host. That result was rejected, and the skills were clarified to require wrapper-managed Docker execution for `local-container`.
- Post-fix Claude runs correctly provisioned local-container Docker leases, ran the focused wrapper suite inside the containers, and cleaned up their leases.
- Provider-attribution probe: configured provider `local-container`; wrapper invoked with explicit `--provider aws` emitted `provider=aws`, confirming why wrapper output must be authoritative.
- Final post-rebase proof:
  - base: `upstream/main` at `161525d43c4c0157a8fd4feceb2bf96cb4db5900`;
  - provider/runtime: `provider=local-container`, `runtime=docker`, Crabbox `0.37.1`;
  - lease: `cbx_29a3dd41d47d` / `brisk-crab-d2c5`, explicitly deleted after the run;
  - command: `node scripts/crabbox-wrapper.mjs run --id cbx_29a3dd41d47d --timing-json -- corepack pnpm test test/scripts/crabbox-wrapper.test.ts --reporter=default`;
  - result: 1 test file passed; 192/192 tests passed.
- Final diff relative to `upstream/main`: two skill files only; zero wrapper/test code diff.
- `git diff --check` — passed.
- `.agents/skills/autoreview/scripts/autoreview --mode local --stream-engine-output` on `e0bb1c889ae` changes — clean, no accepted/actionable findings.

target.title: fix(cli): one-shot agent --local runs never export OTel diagnostics
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where one-shot `openclaw agent --local` runs would export no OTel telemetry at all when `diagnostics.otel.enabled: true` and the `diagnostics-otel` plugin are configured: zero spans, metrics, or logs reached the OTLP collector, while the same turns dispatched through the Gateway exported fine. Gateway-to-embedded fallback runs (gateway timeout or transport failure) silently dropped telemetry the same way, so exactly the runs that bypass the Gateway were invisible in tracing backends.

## Why This Change Was Made

Diagnostics exporters are plugin services and were only ever started inside the Gateway process (`startPluginServices` at gateway startup/reload); embedded CLI runs emit diagnostic events in the CLI process where nothing subscribes. The CLI now starts the `diagnostics-otel` service around embedded agent runs via a scoped, non-activating plugin load that honors the same plugin-enablement config as the Gateway, and flushes on exit: drain the async diagnostic-event queue, then shut the SDK down (force flush), bounded by a 10s timeout so an unreachable collector cannot hang the CLI. `diagnostics-prometheus` intentionally stays Gateway-only — it is a pull-based scrape server that is useless in a short-lived process and would race the Gateway for its port. No new config surface; configs without OTel enabled short-circuit before any plugin load.

## User Impact

Operators running one-shot `openclaw agent --local` turns (and runs that fall back from the Gateway to the embedded agent) now get the same OTel traces, metrics, and logs as Gateway-executed turns, flushed before the process exits. Setups without OTel export enabled are unaffected.

## Evidence

## Summary

- remove the `@anthropic-ai/vertex-sdk` runtime dependency from the shipped OpenClaw package

target.body:
## Problem

Fixes #40768

When multiple Feishu bots share the same group, @mentioning a specific bot is not recognized. The bot logs `message in group ... did not mention bot` even though it's correctly mentioned.

## Root Cause

Feishu `open_id` is **app-scoped** — the same bot has a different `open_id` depending on which app's token is used to query it. Confirmed by querying the same message with two different bot tokens:

```
# Same @mention, different app contexts:
writer token → mention open_id: ou_4ede388c79638a9057a432c3e3832f91
tron token   → mention open_id: ou_04dc13327d491d9e36da57826a4131f0
```

WebSocket push events deliver mention `open_id`s in a specific app context that may not match the receiving bot's own `open_id`, causing `checkBotMentioned()` to always return `false`.

## Fix

`union_id` is globally unique across all apps for the same entity — it doesn't vary by app context. This PR:

1. Fetches `union_id` alongside `open_id` from `bot/v3/info` at startup
2. Stores it in a new `botUnionIds` map in monitor state
3. Passes it through to `checkBotMentioned()` as a fallback
4. Matches mentions by `union_id` when `open_id` doesn't match

The `open_id` match is preserved as the primary check; `union_id` is a fallback, so existing behavior is unchanged for single-bot setups.

## Files Changed

- `types.ts`: add `botUnionId` to `FeishuProbeResult`
- `probe.ts`: extract `union_id` from `bot/v3/info` response
- `monitor.startup.ts`: propagate `botUnionId` through `FeishuMonitorBotIdentity`
- `monitor.state.ts`: add `botUnionIds` map with proper clear/delete
- `monitor.account.ts`: store/clear `botUnionId`, pass to `handleFeishuMessage`
- `bot.ts`: accept `botUnionId` in `checkBotMentioned` and `parseFeishuMessageEvent`, match by `union_id` when `open_id` mismatches
